scope: 22 in-scope WCAG SCs (categories.json); 174 unique techniques / 210 SC-technique pairs from w3c/wcag@7bc46c7
method: per-SC analyze + adversarial verify (39 overclaims corrected) + synthesis; see report

verdict_legend.CAPTURED: a lane genuinely assesses the technique condition
verdict_legend.PARTIAL: touched but not fully assessed / capable-but-not-surfaced / inert-only
verdict_legend.OUT_OF_DOMAIN: medium the harness does not assess (PDF etc.)

scs.title: Non-text Content
scs.summary: SC 1.1.1 has NO authoritative lane in v3 (axe image-alt family RUNS but 1.1.1 is not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS so all findings are dropped; the alt-text-adequacy rubric is shadow+inert; ax-state-diff/field-label-probe are bound to 4.1.2/3.3.2, not 1.1.1): presence/null/missing-alt failures (F65/F38/F39/H37/H67/H2/H24/H36 + the H44 label-association mechanism) are mechanically/authoritatively assessable only at the label-association level, short-alt equivalence/placeholder/functional-name adequacy (G94/G95/G100/G196/G82/F30/H30/H65/ARIA6/ARIA9/ARIA10) sits only in the inert rubric, and all long-description, CSS-background, color-semantic, temporal, homoglyph/ASCII/emoji, CAPTCHA, live-media, object-fallback, and PDF techniques (ARIA15/F3/F13/F20/F67/F71/F72/G68/G73/G74/G92/G143/G144/C9/C18/H53/H86/PDF1/PDF4) are NOT_CAPTURED or OUT_OF_DOMAIN.

techniques.rationale: ARIA6 verifies that an aria-label accurately labels an object / describes its purpose. The alt-text-adequacy rubric explicitly judges svg/canvas/role=img accessible-name adequacy and so conceptually covers aria-label adequacy, but it is shadow + inert. There is NO authoritative 1.1.1 lane: the ax-state-diff catalog runner reads accessible names but it disposes ONLY 4.1.2 (catalog.js: sc:'4.1.2') and is never wired to 1.1.1, so it provides zero authoritative 1.1.1 coverage and is not a 1.1.1 lane.
techniques.gap: No authoritative check of aria-label adequacy for 1.1.1; the adequacy rubric is inert/shadow and axe name rules are not surfaced for 1.1.1.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric for accessible-name objects and surface axe name rules for 1.1.1; extend the rubric prompt to cover aria-label on non-image objects (landmarks, role=math, buttons).

techniques.rationale: ARIA9 concatenates an input name from several text nodes via aria-labelledby; test #1 (ids resolve/unique) is deterministically checkable from DOM but no current lane runs that idref-resolution check, and test #2 (concatenated name is descriptive of purpose) is an adequacy judgment only the inert rubrics touch. The field-label-probe runner is bound to 3.3.2 (catalog.js: sc:'3.3.2') label presence, not 1.1.1 concatenation adequacy, so it is not a 1.1.1 lane here.
techniques.gap: No deterministic aria-labelledby idref-resolution check wired to 1.1.1, and no authoritative descriptiveness check; the rubrics are inert.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic idref-resolution detector (aria-labelledby ids exist+unique) and route descriptiveness to the (activated) alt-text-adequacy / field-label rubric.

techniques.rationale: ARIA10 uses aria-labelledby to supply a text alternative for non-text content (e.g. role=img composed of images). Test #2 (the labelledby value is a valid id on the page) is mechanically determinable and axe runs related aria-* checks at collection, but 1.1.1 is not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS so they are discarded; test #3 (the referenced text accurately labels the content) is an adequacy judgment only the inert rubric attempts. No authoritative 1.1.1 lane.
techniques.gap: Idref validity not surfaced/wired to 1.1.1; adequacy judgment only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe aria/name findings into v3 (add 1.1.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS) and activate the adequacy rubric for role=img + aria-labelledby.

techniques.rationale: ARIA15 uses aria-describedby to attach a LONG DESCRIPTION to an image when the short alt is insufficient — its actual test is whether the long DESCRIPTION adequately conveys the function/information of the image. The alt-text-adequacy rubric is scoped to SHORT name/alt adequacy (it judges accessible name vs the rendered pixels and explicitly does NOT assess long-description completeness); it does not 'loosely cover' description-completeness. No lane locates an aria-describedby long description and judges its completeness, and the idref-presence check is not wired to 1.1.1. This is the same long-description gap as F67/G92, which are NOT_CAPTURED — the prior PARTIAL overclaimed the inert short-alt rubric as touching long-description adequacy.
techniques.gap: No detector for aria-describedby presence/idref wired to 1.1.1; no authoritative or active assessment of long-description adequacy/completeness.
techniques.recommendation: Add an aria-describedby idref detector and build a new long-description-completeness rubric (with image vision) that judges whether name+description together convey the image's information (shared with F67/G92).

techniques.rationale: C9 is the SUFFICIENT technique of including PURELY DECORATIVE images via CSS background (so AT ignores them). Verifying it requires deciding an image is decorative AND that it is delivered via CSS rather than as content — no v3 lane inspects CSS background-image usage or judges decorativeness. The axe image-alt family only inspects DOM img/svg/input/area elements, not CSS backgrounds; the reflow/contrast catalog runners do not look at this.
techniques.gap: No detector enumerates CSS background images or distinguishes decorative-via-CSS from informative content.
techniques.recommendation: New detector to enumerate CSS background-image declarations + an LLM judgment of decorativeness (or accept as guidance-only); low priority given decorative use is the conformant path.

techniques.rationale: C18 (advisory) promotes using CSS margin/padding instead of 1x1 spacer images for layout. The quality it promotes (no spacer-image markup at all) is observable in principle, but no v3 lane detects spacer/layout-image patterns or CSS margin/padding usage. F39 (alt='spacer') is the related failure, not this advisory authoring practice. No axe rule, no rubric, no catalog runner addresses it.
techniques.gap: No detection of spacer-image-for-layout patterns nor of CSS margin/padding adoption.
techniques.recommendation: None practical — advisory authoring practice with weak runtime signal; if desired, fold spacer-image detection into an F39-style heuristic. Otherwise leave as guidance.

techniques.rationale: F3 fails 1.1.1 when INFORMATION is conveyed exclusively through a CSS background-image (incl. style attr / script-set background) with no programmatically-determinable equivalent. Detecting it requires enumerating CSS/inline/script background images, OCR/vision to decide the image carries information, and checking the info is not present elsewhere in text. No v3 lane inspects CSS backgrounds; the axe image-alt family only covers DOM image elements; the contrast/reflow runners are unrelated; the inert alt-text rubric inspects DOM alt/name, not CSS backgrounds.
techniques.gap: No lane inspects CSS/inline/script background images for embedded information, and no equivalence check exists.
techniques.recommendation: New detector to harvest computed background-image URLs + a vision/LLM rubric judging whether the background conveys information with no text equivalent (F3 detector).

lanes: llm-rubric:alt-text-adequacy (shadow,inert — does not compare color semantics)
techniques.rationale: F13 fails when an image conveys information via COLOR DIFFERENCES but the text alternative omits that color-conveyed information (e.g. red bars = below quota). This needs vision of the image's color semantics compared against the alt text — no v3 lane does this. The alt-text-adequacy rubric checks generic name-vs-pixels adequacy but is not prompted to detect color-encoded information loss, and is inert anyway. The 1.4.1/1.4.3 contrast lanes do not compare image color meaning to alt text.
techniques.gap: No vision-driven comparison of image color-encoded information against the text alternative.
techniques.recommendation: Extend the alt-text-adequacy rubric (with image vision) to flag color-conveyed information missing from the alt, or build a dedicated F13 vision detector.

techniques.rationale: F20 fails when non-text content is UPDATED (new chart, rotating images, script-swapped src) but the text alternative is not updated to match, so alt now describes stale content. Detecting it requires comparing current rendered image content against the current alt across a state change — a temporal/vision diff no v3 lane performs (status-detector watches DOM insertions for 4.1.3, not alt-vs-image staleness). Single-snapshot assessment cannot catch this.
techniques.gap: No temporal lane comparing updated image content to its (unchanged) text alternative.
techniques.recommendation: Out of reach for a single snapshot; would need a stateful vision diff. Defer / document as a known gap.

techniques.rationale: F30 fails when the 'text alternative' is not actually an alternative — placeholder text ('spacer','image','picture'), programming refs ('picture 1','0001'), or filenames ('Oct.jpg'). The alt-text-adequacy rubric explicitly targets placeholder/filename ('image','img_1234.png') and mismatched names, so it conceptually captures F30 — but it is shadow + inert. axe image-alt flags empty alt but will NOT flag a present-but-junk filename/placeholder. No authoritative lane.
techniques.gap: The one lane that detects placeholder/filename alts (the rubric) is non-authoritative and off by default; surfaced axe would still miss non-empty junk.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric (it is the intended F30 detector); optionally add a deterministic heuristic for filename-as-alt / common placeholder strings.

techniques.rationale: F38 fails when a DECORATIVE img has neither role='presentation' nor any alt attribute, so AT cannot ignore it. The DOM conditions (no role=presentation AND no alt attribute) are exactly the missing-alt condition axe's image-alt rule detects and that is fully DOM-determinable — but axe findings are DISCARDED for 1.1.1 (not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS), so the capability exists but is not consumed. Deciding the image is 'purely decorative' is a separate judgment, but the markup failure itself is mechanically detectable.
techniques.gap: axe image-alt runs but its missing-alt findings are dropped for 1.1.1; capability not surfaced.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt into v3 (add 1.1.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS); the missing-alt detection then becomes a CAPTURED-shadow signal.

lanes: axe:image-alt (capable,NOT-surfaced — does not flag non-null junk)
techniques.rationale: F39 fails when an image that should be ignored has a NON-NULL placeholder alt (alt='spacer'/'image') instead of alt=''. The presence of a non-null alt is DOM-readable, but the failure requires judging that the alt is junk on a should-be-ignored image — that is precisely what the alt-text-adequacy rubric targets (placeholder detection), and it is inert/shadow. axe image-alt treats a present alt as a pass and will not flag 'spacer'.
techniques.gap: Only the inert rubric flags placeholder alt text; no authoritative lane, and surfaced axe would not catch non-null junk.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric and add a deterministic placeholder-string blacklist (spacer/image/picture) as a shadow signal.

techniques.rationale: F65 is the canonical missing-text-alternative failure on img/area/input[type=image] (no alt AND no aria-labelledby AND no aria-label AND no title). This is exactly the axe image-alt / input-image-alt / area-alt rule set, which RUNS at collection and is fully DOM-determinable — but v3 DISCARDS those findings because 1.1.1 is not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS. So the harness is capable but does not consume it (PARTIAL). The inert rubric also flags missing names.
techniques.gap: The highest-value, fully-deterministic 1.1.1 detector (axe image-alt family) runs but is dropped; not surfaced and not authoritative.
techniques.recommendation: Surface the axe image-alt family into v3 (add 1.1.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS). This is the single highest-impact action for SC 1.1.1.

techniques.rationale: F67 fails when a LONG DESCRIPTION does not serve the same purpose / present the same information as the non-text content (e.g. a map description omitting addresses). This requires vision of the image plus completeness comparison against an associated long description — no v3 lane does this. The alt-text-adequacy rubric is scoped to short alt/name adequacy (name-vs-pixels), not long-description completeness, and is inert; it is not a lane for this technique.
techniques.gap: No lane locates a long description and judges its information-completeness against the image.
techniques.recommendation: New / extended LLM rubric (with image vision) to compare a long description (aria-describedby / adjacent text) against the image's information content.

techniques.rationale: F71 fails when text look-alike glyphs (e.g. Greek/Cyrillic homoglyphs spelling 'cook') are used to represent text with no text alternative, so TTS mis-reads them. This is a Unicode/character-analysis check (detect mixed-script homoglyph runs) — fully deterministic in principle but no v3 lane performs it; axe has no such rule, no rubric targets it, and no catalog runner inspects character scripts.
techniques.gap: No homoglyph / mixed-script detector exists in any lane.
techniques.recommendation: New deterministic detector for mixed-script / confusable-character runs (Unicode confusables) flagging text with no alternative; emit as shadow.

techniques.rationale: F72 fails when ASCII art is used with no text alternative. Detecting it requires recognizing an ASCII-art block (dense punctuation/box-drawing patterns, often in <pre>) and confirming no adjacent text alternative — no v3 lane does this; no axe rule, no active rubric, no catalog runner. The alt-text rubric inspects image alt/name, not text-node ASCII patterns.
techniques.gap: No detector recognizes ASCII-art text blocks or checks for an adjacent text alternative.
techniques.recommendation: New heuristic/LLM detector for ASCII-art blocks (e.g. high punctuation density in <pre>) plus a check for an adjacent alternative; emit as shadow.

techniques.rationale: G68 provides a short text label describing the PURPOSE of LIVE audio-only / video-only content. Identifying a live media stream and judging whether its label conveys its purpose is outside any v3 lane; the harness has no media-element label-purpose detector, no axe rule for this, and the alt-text rubric is image-element scoped (name-vs-pixels) and inert — it is not a lane for live-media labels.
techniques.gap: No lane identifies live audio/video-only elements or assesses a purpose-describing label.
techniques.recommendation: Out of typical scope; if pursued, extend a rubric to judge labels on audio/video / media-region elements. Low priority.

techniques.rationale: G73 supplies a long description in another location with an immediately-adjacent LINK to it (plus a return path). Verifying it requires locating an adjacent long-description link, following it, and judging that the target conveys the same information — no v3 lane traverses adjacency-to-long-description links or judges remote-description equivalence. axe link-name (surfaced for 2.4.4) does not assess long-description equivalence for 1.1.1.
techniques.gap: No lane detects an adjacent long-description link or evaluates the linked description's completeness.
techniques.recommendation: New / extended LLM rubric to detect adjacent long-description links and judge target equivalence; non-trivial (requires navigation).

techniques.rationale: G74 provides the long description as in-page text near the non-text content, with the short alt pointing to its location. Verifying it requires correlating the short alt's pointer to nearby body text and judging information equivalence — no v3 lane does long-description-near-content correlation or equivalence judgment. No axe rule, no active rubric, no catalog runner.
techniques.gap: No lane correlates a short-alt location reference to adjacent long-description text or judges equivalence.
techniques.recommendation: Extend an LLM rubric to evaluate adjacent in-page long descriptions against the image; requires vision + layout reasoning.

techniques.rationale: G82 provides a text alternative that identifies the PURPOSE of interactive non-text content (e.g. an applet/control) when full function can't be conveyed. The alt-text-adequacy rubric explicitly covers the functional-image path ('a linked/iconed control's name must convey the ACTION'), so it conceptually judges this purpose-identification — but it is shadow + inert. There is NO authoritative 1.1.1 lane: the ax-state-diff catalog runner reads names but disposes ONLY 4.1.2 (catalog.js: sc:'4.1.2'), is never wired to 1.1.1, and provides no authoritative 1.1.1 purpose check; it is not a 1.1.1 lane.
techniques.gap: Only the inert/shadow rubric judges whether the name conveys the interactive element's purpose; not authoritative.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric (functional-name path) for interactive non-text controls; surface axe name rules for 1.1.1 to provide a presence shadow signal.

techniques.rationale: G92 provides a LONG description that serves the same purpose and presents the same information as the non-text content (short alt + long alt together substitute for the image). This is a long-description completeness/equivalence judgment requiring image vision; the alt-text-adequacy rubric is scoped to short alt/name (name-vs-pixels) and is inert, so it is not a lane for long-description completeness. No authoritative lane, no axe rule.
techniques.gap: No lane evaluates long-description completeness/equivalence against the image content.
techniques.recommendation: New / extended LLM rubric (image vision) to judge whether short+long alternative together convey the same information as the non-text content.

techniques.rationale: G94 is the core SUFFICIENT technique: a SHORT text alternative that serves the same purpose and presents the same information as the non-text content (and includes essential words in the image). The alt-text-adequacy rubric is precisely aimed at this equivalence/purpose judgment (name-vs-pixels) — but it is shadow + inert. axe image-alt verifies a name is present but cannot judge equivalence, and is not surfaced for 1.1.1. No authoritative lane.
techniques.gap: The lane built to verify G94 (alt-text-adequacy rubric) is non-authoritative and off; surfaced axe only confirms presence, not equivalence.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric as the primary 1.1.1 adequacy signal and surface axe image-alt for presence.

techniques.rationale: G95 provides a SHORT text alternative that briefly DESCRIBES the non-text content (used when full equivalence needs a separate long alt). Its test is only presence of a brief descriptive short alt — presence is detectable by surfaced axe, and brief-description adequacy is judged by the alt-text-adequacy rubric. Both are non-authoritative (axe not surfaced for 1.1.1; rubric inert).
techniques.gap: Presence detector (axe) not surfaced; brief-description adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt for presence and activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric for brief-description quality.

techniques.rationale: G100 provides a short alt that is the ACCEPTED NAME or a descriptive name of the non-text content (esp. for sensory content like artworks/audio). For an image/non-text element the alt-text-adequacy rubric judges name adequacy (name-vs-pixels), so it touches this naming judgment — but it is shadow + inert; no authoritative lane, and axe only checks presence (not surfaced). For pure-audio sensory content the harness has no media-aware check (so coverage is partial even within the technique).
techniques.gap: Only the inert rubric judges name adequacy/appropriateness; no authoritative or active lane; pure-audio sensory content uncovered.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric (extend prompt to recognize accepted/descriptive-name cases for sensory content).

techniques.rationale: G143 provides a text alternative that identifies the content as a CAPTCHA and its task type. Recognizing a CAPTCHA and judging whether its text alternative describes its purpose is outside any v3 lane — no CAPTCHA detector, no axe rule, no active rubric for CAPTCHA purpose, and the alt-text rubric is not framed for CAPTCHA identification.
techniques.gap: No lane recognizes a CAPTCHA or evaluates a CAPTCHA-purpose text alternative.
techniques.recommendation: Niche; if pursued, extend a rubric to recognize CAPTCHA widgets and judge their purpose label. Low priority.

techniques.rationale: G144 requires that the page contain ANOTHER CAPTCHA serving the same purpose in a different modality (e.g. audio + visual). This is a page-composition requirement (two modality-distinct CAPTCHAs) that no v3 lane assesses — there is no CAPTCHA-modality detector, no axe rule, no rubric.
techniques.gap: No lane detects presence of multi-modality alternative CAPTCHAs.
techniques.recommendation: Out of practical scope for the harness; document as a known gap or leave to guidance.

techniques.rationale: G196 puts one group-describing text alternative on a single item of an adjacent image group and null-alts the rest (e.g. star ratings). The DOM pattern (one non-null alt + adjacent null alts) is determinable, and axe image-alt detects null vs present alts — but it is not surfaced for 1.1.1 and cannot judge that the one alt describes the whole group. The group-adequacy judgment is only in the inert rubric, which is not framed for grouped-image semantics.
techniques.gap: No lane evaluates the group-describing alt pattern; axe presence/null detection not surfaced; group adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt (for null/present detection) and extend the alt-text-adequacy rubric to handle adjacent-image-group semantics.

techniques.rationale: H2 combines an icon and text link in one anchor with NULL alt on the icon to avoid duplicate links. Test #1 (every img inside the a has alt='') is DOM-determinable and within axe image-alt's null-detection capability (runs at collection, not surfaced for 1.1.1); test #2 (img alt is null OR meaningfully supplements link text) is an adequacy judgment only the inert rubric touches. No authoritative lane.
techniques.gap: Null-alt-in-anchor pattern detection not surfaced; supplemental-alt adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt (null detection) and activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric for image-in-link cases.

techniques.rationale: H24 requires each <area> of an image map to have an alt that serves the same purpose as its region. Test #1 (area has an alt attribute) is exactly axe's area-alt rule — runs at collection, fully DOM-determinable, but DISCARDED for 1.1.1 (not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS). Test #2 (alt serves the same purpose as the region) is an adequacy judgment only the inert rubric attempts.
techniques.gap: axe area-alt runs but is dropped for 1.1.1; region-purpose adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe area-alt into v3 (add 1.1.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS); route adequacy to the activated rubric.

techniques.rationale: H30 provides link text (or, for an image-only link, an img alt) that describes the link's purpose. The accessible-name-present part is detectable (axe link-name runs and IS surfaced for 2.4.4 — in AXE_SURFACED_SCS — but its findings are bound to 2.4.4, not credited to 1.1.1), and purpose adequacy is judged by the inert link-purpose / alt-text-adequacy rubrics. No authoritative lane for the 1.1.1 framing (image-as-link alt purpose).
techniques.gap: Image-link alt-purpose adequacy only in inert rubrics; axe link-name surfaced but tagged to 2.4.4, not credited to 1.1.1.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the alt-text-adequacy / link-purpose rubrics for image-only links and credit/surface axe name rules for 1.1.1.

techniques.rationale: H36 requires input[type=image] submit buttons to carry a functional alt label. Test #1 (alt present on input[type=image]) is exactly axe's input-image-alt rule — runs, DOM-determinable, but discarded for 1.1.1 (not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS). Test #2 (alt describes the button's function) is a functional-name adequacy judgment only the inert rubric attempts.
techniques.gap: axe input-image-alt runs but is dropped for 1.1.1; functional-label adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe input-image-alt into v3 and activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric (functional-name path).

techniques.rationale: H37 is the core SUFFICIENT technique: meaningful elements carry an alt that conveys the same meaning (incl. essential words). Test #2 (meaningful img has alt) is precisely axe image-alt — runs, fully DOM-determinable, but discarded for 1.1.1 (not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS). Test #3 (alt includes important words / conveys meaning) is an adequacy judgment only the inert rubric attempts.
techniques.gap: axe image-alt (presence) runs but is dropped for 1.1.1; meaning/word-inclusion adequacy only in the inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt into v3 (add 1.1.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS) and activate the alt-text-adequacy rubric for meaning.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — disposes 3.3.2, but assesses the H44 label-association mechanism)
techniques.rationale: H44 associates a label with a form control via label/for=id, which gives the control its accessible name (sufficient for 1.1.1). The authoritative field-label-probe runner runs live by default and verifies a programmatic name IS present AND a visible label exists (catalog.js: programmaticNamePresent + visibleLabelText) — directly and deterministically assessing the exact label-association condition H44 prescribes. Per the dossier's capture definition (does SOME lane ASSESS the condition the technique addresses), this condition is authoritatively assessed even though the runner files its disposition under 3.3.2 rather than 1.1.1. CAPTURED stands; the lane is genuinely authoritative+live for the label-association mechanism.

H53 uses the BODY (fallback content) of an <object> element as the text alternative, shown only when the embedded media is not rendered. This is an in-scope HTML/web-runtime technique (NOT out of domain), but v3 assesses the rendered page, where object fallback content is generally NOT rendered/observable; no lane inspects object fallback bodies, axe object-alt is not surfaced, and the alt-text rubric does not parse object fallback. The condition is essentially invisible at runtime when the object renders.
techniques.gap: No lane inspects <object> fallback body content as a text alternative.
techniques.recommendation: Surface/inspect object-alt and parse object fallback body in a rubric if object content is in-scope; otherwise document as a runtime-visibility gap.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — disposes 3.3.2; name-presence sub-check covers title-derived name)
techniques.rationale: H65 uses the title attribute to name a form control when a label element cannot be used. The field-label-probe runner authoritatively verifies a programmatic name is present (a title-derived accessible name satisfies the programmaticNamePresent check) and runs live, so the name-presence half of H65 is genuinely assessed; but H65 additionally requires that the purpose is clear to sighted users and the title matches the visual purpose — adequacy/visual-match judgments the runner cannot make (and the 3.3.2-oriented runner may even BARRIER-flag title-only for lacking a visible label). Adequacy is only in the inert rubric. Hence PARTIAL, not CAPTURED.
techniques.gap: Title-as-name presence is covered, but title adequacy / visual-purpose match is only in the inert rubric; not authoritatively assessed for the 1.1.1 framing.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the field-label rubric to judge title-as-name adequacy; ensure the name-presence runner credits title-derived names.

techniques.rationale: H67 marks a decorative image with null alt (alt='') and no title so AT ignores it. The DOM conditions (title absent/empty AND alt present-and-empty) are fully deterministic and within axe image-alt's null-handling, but findings are not surfaced for 1.1.1 (not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS). Deciding the image is genuinely decorative is a separate judgment, but the markup pattern this technique prescribes is mechanically detectable; capability exists but is dropped.
techniques.gap: Null-alt + no-title detection not surfaced for 1.1.1.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe image-alt into v3; the null-alt/no-title pattern then becomes an observable shadow signal.

techniques.rationale: H86 provides text alternatives for emojis, emoticons, ASCII art, and leetspeak (e.g. role=img + aria-label on a span, or abbr/title). Recognizing these text-node phenomena (emoji glyphs, emoticon punctuation, ASCII-art blocks, leetspeak) and checking for an equivalent alternative is outside any v3 lane; no axe rule, no active rubric targets text-node emoji/leet/ASCII, and the alt-text rubric is image-element scoped — it is not a lane for this technique.
techniques.gap: No detector for emoji/emoticon/ASCII/leetspeak text and their alternatives.
techniques.recommendation: New detector (emoji unicode ranges, emoticon/leet/ASCII heuristics) + a rubric to check for an equivalent text alternative; overlaps with F71/F72 work.

techniques.rationale: PDF1 applies text alternatives to images via the /Alt entry in tagged PDF documents — a PDF authoring/structure technique. v3 assesses rendered web pages at runtime and neither authors nor inspects PDF tag structures. Conceptually parallel to H37/G94 alt text, but the medium is out of the harness's domain.
techniques.recommendation: None — out of domain (PDF authoring).

techniques.rationale: PDF4 hides decorative images via the /Artifact tag in tagged PDF documents — a PDF authoring/structure technique. v3 does not author or inspect PDF artifact tagging. Conceptually parallel to H67/C9 decorative-image handling, but the PDF medium is outside the rendered-web-page-at-runtime harness.
techniques.recommendation: None — out of domain (PDF authoring).

audit_changes.why: Verdict overclaim. ARIA15's actual test is aria-describedby LONG-DESCRIPTION adequacy/completeness. The alt-text-adequacy rubric (verified at scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/alt-text-adequacy-v0.md) judges only SHORT accessible-name-vs-pixels and explicitly does NOT assess long-description completeness — so 'the rubric loosely covers it' is false. No lane wires the aria-describedby idref to 1.1.1 either. This is the identical long-description gap the analyst correctly scored NOT_CAPTURED for F67 and G92; ARIA15 must match. Removed the inert rubric from the lane list since it does not touch this technique.

Lane-list overclaim (verdict unchanged). Removed the 'deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff (authoritative,live)' lane: verified in catalog.js that ax-state-diff is bound to sc:'4.1.2' and never wired to 1.1.1, so citing it as an authoritative lane in a 1.1.1 verdict implies non-existent authoritative 1.1.1 coverage. Rationale corrected to state 1.1.1 has NO authoritative lane.

Lane-list overclaim (verdict unchanged). Removed the 'deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff (authoritative,live)' lane for the same reason as ARIA6: ax-state-diff disposes 4.1.2 (catalog.js sc:'4.1.2'), not 1.1.1, so it is not an authoritative 1.1.1 lane. Rationale corrected to make explicit there is no authoritative 1.1.1 purpose check.

Lane-label correction (verdict unchanged). The prior lane label 'axe:link-name (capable,NOT-surfaced for 1.1.1)' was imprecise: axe link-name IS surfaced and live (2.4.4 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS per axe-surface.js), it is simply tagged to 2.4.4 and not credited to 1.1.1. Relabeled to 'live+surfaced for 2.4.4, NOT credited to 1.1.1' so the liveness/authority state is accurate.

scs.title: Info and Relationships
scs.summary: SC 1.3.1 has NO authoritative deterministic catalog runner; its only LIVE signal is axe's DECIDED+SURFACED findings (axe surfacing keys on the violation's own wcag131 tag and 1.3.1 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS), a shadow cross-signal that never gates conformance — covering data-table header relationships (td-headers-attr/th-has-data-cells/td-has-header/table-fake-caption), list/dl structure (list/listitem/definition-list/dlitem), the p-as-heading pseudo-heading failure, and composite-widget child/parent integrity (aria-required-children/parent); everything else (landmark/region naming, heading semantics, emphasis markup, role=presentation misuse, plain-text/pre pseudo-tables, structural-markup-misuse, emulated-link role exposure) is touched only by the INERT info-relationships rubric, guidance skills, and a band of capable-but-NOT-surfaced axe rules (region/landmark-unique/heading-order/empty-heading/presentation-role-conflict), so the SC is broadly PARTIAL with several genuinely unmonitored gaps.

techniques.rationale: Advisory: attach descriptive info to a control via aria-describedby and verify the referenced id(s) exist and actually describe the control. No catalog runner assesses description relationships; the 4.1.2 ax-state-diff lane checks name/role/state, not aria-describedby content, and exp-runners only reads aria-describedby as a side input for error/label channels, never validating IDREF resolution or description adequacy. No axe rule tagged wcag131 inspects aria-describedby (aria-required-attr etc. are wcag412). The info-relationships rubric (inert) defers to the runner on structure; no skill emits a signal. Confirmed in-domain (client-side, runtime-observable) but uncovered.
techniques.gap: No lane verifies an aria-describedby reference resolves to a real element nor judges that the description adds useful info.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic detector for dangling aria-describedby/aria-labelledby IDREFs and surface as a 1.3.1 shadow finding; optionally extend the info-relationships rubric to judge description adequacy.

techniques.rationale: Advisory: when a field is VISUALLY shown as required (asterisk/text/color), also expose aria-required so the required state is programmatically determinable. Verified axe aria-required-attr carries wcag412 (NOT wcag131) and only checks that roles MANDATING aria-required have it — not visual-vs-programmatic parity; aria-required-children/parent (which DO carry wcag131) are about composite-widget containment, irrelevant here. v3's 3.3.2 field-label-probe checks name+visible label, not required-state parity. No lane correlates a visual required cue with the programmatic required state — the crux of the technique.
techniques.gap: Nothing detects the mismatch between a visually-indicated required field and a missing programmatic required state.
techniques.recommendation: Add a detector flagging fields with a visual required cue (asterisk/'(required)'/styling) but no aria-required/required attribute; surface as 1.3.1/3.3.2 shadow.

lanes: llm-rubric:1.3.1 info-relationships (shadow,inert — but PUNTS landmark presence)
techniques.rationale: Sufficient: use ARIA landmark roles so page regions are programmatically identified, named where required, with unique names for duplicate types. Verified axe HAS region ('all content contained by landmarks') and landmark-unique ('unique role/label combination') rules that are CAPABLE of this exact check, but both carry NO wcag131 tag (best-practice only), so they are NOT surfaced and would drop even when decided. CORRECTION: the cited info-relationships rubric does NOT actually assess landmark presence — its prompt states 'missing landmark is a best-practice concern, NOT automatically a 1.3.1 failure' — so the inert-rubric touch is tangential. The legitimate PARTIAL basis is the capable-but-NOT-surfaced axe landmark rules (dossier: capable-but-not-surfaced = PARTIAL, recommend surfacing); no live decided signal today.
techniques.gap: No live lane verifies landmark roles are present, correctly applied, named where required, and uniquely named; the capable axe landmark rules are not surfaced and the inert rubric explicitly excludes landmark presence.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe's region/landmark-unique rules into v3 (or add a landmark inventory detector for role-presence + dup-name uniqueness) as a 1.3.1 shadow signal.

lanes: llm-rubric:2.4.6 heading-descriptive / 1.3.1 info-relationships (shadow,inert — descriptiveness only, NOT level validity)
techniques.rationale:
Sufficient: use role=heading + aria-level so an element is exposed as a heading at the right level. CORRECTION to the analyst: p-as-heading detects the INVERSE (a

styled as a heading); it does NOT verify that a role=heading technique is correctly satisfied, so it is not a touch of ARIA12 and is removed from the lanes. The capable touch is axe heading-order ('levels only increase by one') + empty-heading, which assess heading-level validity but are best-practice tagged (no wcag131) so NOT surfaced. The descriptiveness rubrics explicitly judge meaning only, not level/presence. Coverage is capable-but-not-surfaced + inert.
techniques.gap: No live lane confirms role=heading carries a valid aria-level (capable axe heading-order is not surfaced); heading-content appropriateness is an unjudged quality.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe heading-order/empty-heading (or add a heading-structure detector collecting role=heading/aria-level from the AX tree) and run the 2.4.6 rubric for heading appropriateness.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: name regions/landmarks with aria-labelledby pointing to on-page text that accurately labels the section. Same profile as ARIA11/ARIA20: capable axe landmark-unique (checks role/label/title uniqueness) and region exist but are best-practice tagged (no wcag131) and NOT surfaced; no live decided signal. The IDREF resolution + label-accuracy judgment is not performed by any live lane, and the info-relationships rubric (inert) explicitly excludes landmark presence — it is a tangential touch. PARTIAL rests on the capable-but-not-surfaced axe rules.
techniques.gap: No live lane resolves a landmark/region aria-labelledby IDREF and judges whether the referenced text accurately names the section.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe landmark-unique/region and/or add a landmark-name detector (resolve aria-labelledby IDREFs, confirm a non-empty accessible name); let the info-relationships rubric judge label accuracy once activated.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — form controls, programmatic name + visible label)
techniques.rationale: Sufficient: name a UI control via aria-labelledby referencing on-page text whose content accurately labels the control. The 4.1.2 ax-state-diff and 3.3.2 field-label-probe lanes DO authoritatively verify an accessible NAME is present (field-label-probe additionally checks programmatic name + visible label for form fields) — a genuine authoritative touch of the presence half. Verified the capable axe name rules (label/button-name) carry wcag412, not wcag131, so they are NOT surfaced for 1.3.1. Neither runner resolves the aria-labelledby chain nor judges that the concatenated label text accurately labels the control — that accuracy judgment lives in the inert 3.3.2/2.4.4 rubrics. Presence partly covered authoritatively; accuracy not.
techniques.gap: Label-text accuracy and aria-labelledby IDREF resolution for the NAME are not authoritatively assessed; only name PRESENCE is.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the 3.3.2/2.4.4 rubrics for name-accuracy and add dangling-IDREF detection; otherwise presence is adequately covered.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: mark related controls as a group via role=group/radiogroup with an accessible name so the grouping is programmatically exposed. CORRECTION (factual): the analyst dismissed aria-required-children/parent as not-surfaced/irrelevant, but I verified both carry wcag131 (RUNS=true under the eval config) and 1.3.1 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, so they ARE surfaced as decided shadow findings. A malformed role=radiogroup missing its required radio children would trip aria-required-children — a real (if narrow) live shadow proxy for broken radiogroup integrity (parallel to the F46 table-rule proxy). This raises the verdict above NOT_CAPTURED. Still PARTIAL: nothing detects whether related controls that SHOULD be grouped were grouped, role=group (no required children) is unchecked, and group naming is unverified.
techniques.gap: No lane detects whether related controls that should be grouped are wrapped in a named group/radiogroup; only a malformed radiogroup's missing required children is caught (shadow). The 'should these be grouped' and group-name judgments are unmonitored.
techniques.recommendation: Add a grouping detector (fieldset/legend or role=group|radiogroup with an accessible name around related controls) as a 1.3.1 shadow signal; the deeper 'should these be grouped' judgment needs the LLM rubric.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: use role=region (with a programmatic name) for a significant section when no standard landmark fits. As with ARIA11/13: axe's region rule is CAPABLE but best-practice tagged (no wcag131) and NOT surfaced; no live decided signal. The 'important enough / no standard landmark / has a name' judgment is exactly the kind of structure-meaning call the inert info-relationships rubric conceptually addresses, but the current rubric prompt excludes landmark presence, so that touch is tangential. PARTIAL rests on the capable-but-not-surfaced region rule.
techniques.gap: No live lane checks role=region has a programmatic name and is used appropriately; the capable axe region rule is not surfaced.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe's region rule and/or add a named-region detector; defer the appropriateness judgment to the info-relationships rubric once activated.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient (advisory in practice): tag a font-icon span with role=img + a text alternative so font-override users perceive meaningful icon glyphs and AT differentiates icon fonts from text. Verified niche pattern (CSS ::before content glyph + role=img). No catalog runner, no surfaced axe rule (image-alt/svg-img-alt target real /
techniques.gap: No lane detects icon-font glyphs (CSS content) and whether they carry role=img with an accessible name; the font-override-survivability concern is unmonitored.
techniques.recommendation: Low priority: a deterministic detector for elements with icon-font classes / pseudo-element content lacking role=img — likely defer (rare in the 22-page corpus).

lanes: axe:p-as-heading (capable,SURFACED — catches the styled-heading edge only)
techniques.rationale: Advisory: use CSS (not images) for visual text presentation, with the caveat that styling MUST NOT convey information/structure without backing markup. The positive 'used CSS to style text' is near-always-true and not a discrete assessable pass. The accessibility-relevant edge — styling that conveys meaning without semantics (the F2/G117 concern) — IS partly touched live by surfaced p-as-heading (the styled-paragraph-as-heading sub-case), with the broader case in the inert info-relationships rubric. So one variant is caught live (shadow); the general case is inert.
techniques.gap: Only the CSS-pseudo-heading variant of style-conveying-meaning is detected live; other style-only-meaning cases are inert-rubric only; the bare 'uses CSS for text' condition is not a discrete signal.
techniques.recommendation: Cover the meaningful edge via the F2/G117 path (extend/activate the info-relationships rubric to flag style-only meaning); the bare 'uses CSS for text' condition needs no detector.

techniques.rationale: Failure: using a change in text presentation to convey structure WITHOUT appropriate markup. Verified axe p-as-heading carries wcag131 and 1.3.1 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, so it flows into v3 as a decided shadow finding — directly catching the canonical CSS-styled-paragraph-as-heading case (live shadow). The image-of-text-as-heading variant and general 'styled text conveys info' variant are NOT caught by p-as-heading and need the inert info-relationships/1.4.5 rubric. So the failure is detected for the p-as-heading sub-case only (shadow, never authoritative).
techniques.gap: Only CSS-pseudo-heading paragraphs are detected (shadow, not authoritative); images-of-text-as-headings and other presentation-conveys-meaning variants are not detected.
techniques.recommendation: Keep p-as-heading surfaced; extend/activate the info-relationships / 1.4.5 images-of-text rubric to flag image-of-text headings and other styled-meaning cases.

techniques.rationale: Failure (shared 1.3.1/1.3.2): using whitespace characters to fake multiple text columns in plain text, breaking reading order. Verified no whitespace-column heuristic exists in any lane: order-check.js operates on the NAVIGATION sequence of interactive/transcript items by geometry (column-aware via x-overlap union-find), not on whitespace-aligned characters inside a text node, and it is uncalibrated triage anyway. No axe wcag131 rule and no rubric address whitespace pseudo-columns. In-domain (text is in the DOM) but no lane inspects intra-text-node whitespace layout.
techniques.gap: No lane detects whitespace-character pseudo-columns in plain text content.
techniques.recommendation: Add a text-node heuristic (aligned runs of spaces/tabs forming columns) or an LLM rubric over the rendered text block; low priority given rarity in modern pages.

techniques.rationale: Failure (shared 1.3.1/1.3.2): using whitespace characters to format a TABLE in plain text instead of real <table> markup, destroying cell/header relationships. Same as F33 — no lane inspects whitespace-aligned tabular text. Verified axe table rules (th-has-data-cells/td-headers-attr/td-has-header) all select real <table> elements, so a whitespace 'table' is invisible to them; the reading-order instruments analyze interactive-item geometry, not plain-text grids; no rubric covers it.
techniques.gap: No lane detects whitespace-aligned pseudo-tables in plain text.
techniques.recommendation: Add a heuristic/LLM check for whitespace-grid tabular text in <pre>/text nodes; low priority.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live — covers the 2.1.1 half, NOT the 1.3.1 condition)
techniques.rationale: Failure across 1.3.1/2.1.1/4.1.2: a scripted span/div/img emulating a link that is NOT exposed with role=link. DOWNGRADE from PARTIAL: the analyst listed ax-state-diff role-exposure as authoritative,live coverage, but I confirmed NO lane scans the page for click-handler-bearing non-anchors lacking role=link — ax-state-diff verifies name/role/state ARE EXPOSED on a control it is pointed at; it does not flag an emulated link's role MISMATCH, and the analyst itself conceded 'ax-state-diff is not framed to flag emulated link missing role=link'. The keyboard-activation runner covers the 2.1.1 half only, and link-name is wcag244/wcag412 (not surfaced for 1.3.1). The cited authoritative lanes are ADJACENT-SC coverage, not the 1.3.1-specific role-exposure failure, which no lane detects.
techniques.gap: No lane flags a JS-emulated link (onclick on span/div/img, pointer-cursor styling) that lacks role=link; the 1.3.1 role-mismatch is unasserted. (The 2.1.1 keyboard half is covered by the keyboard-activation runner, but that is a different SC.)
techniques.recommendation: Add a detector: non-native-control elements with click handlers (or pointer-cursor styling) lacking role=link/button → 1.3.1/4.1.2 shadow flag; the keyboard half is already covered by 2.1.1.

techniques.rationale:
Failure: using structural markup for a presentational effect, implying relationships that don't exist (h4 to make an address big/bold, blockquote for indentation, heading levels for font sizing, fieldset/legend for a border). Verified this is a semantics-vs-intent MISMATCH requiring content judgment. The surfaced axe wcag131 rules catch the INVERSE (unmarked content) or malformed structure, not OVER-marked content; p-as-heading catches a styled

, not a heading misused for visual effect. Only the inert info-relationships rubric and guidance skill conceptually apply; neither is live nor emits a signal alone.
techniques.gap: No live lane detects structural markup misused for presentation (blockquote-for-indent, heading-for-font-size, fieldset-for-border); requires content-meaning judgment.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the 1.3.1 info-relationships rubric and extend its prompt to flag structural-markup-without-real-relationship cases.

techniques.rationale: Failure: using th, caption, summary, scope, or headers in a LAYOUT table. The hard part is classifying the table as layout-only; once known, structural markup in it is a failure. Verified the surfaced wcag131 table rules partially proxy this: th-has-data-cells flags a <th> with no data cells it describes (a strong signal of th misused in a non-data/layout table), and table-fake-caption flags caption misuse — both surfaced as decided shadow findings. But axe does not reason about 'this whole table is layout-only', so a layout table with a populated-looking th structure passes axe while still failing F46. Coverage is partial/proxy.
techniques.gap: No lane authoritatively classifies a table as layout-only then flags th/caption/summary in it; only structural-anomaly proxies (orphan th, fake caption) are caught.
techniques.recommendation: Keep axe table rules surfaced; add an LLM/heuristic layout-vs-data table classifier to the info-relationships rubric to catch the intent-dependent F46 cases.

techniques.rationale: Failure: using a <pre> element to mark up TABULAR information (whitespace-aligned columns inside <pre>), so cell/header relationships are lost. Verified detecting this requires judging that the text INSIDE a <pre> is tabular — a content judgment. No catalog runner inspects <pre> content; axe table rules select real <table> elements only, so <pre>-as-table is invisible. Only the inert info-relationships rubric conceptually applies (non-live, no signal alone). In-domain (the <pre> is in the DOM) but no live lane assesses it.
techniques.gap: No live lane detects tabular data laid out inside <pre> via whitespace.
techniques.recommendation: Extend the info-relationships rubric (or a heuristic) to inspect <pre> blocks whose content is columnar/tabular; low-to-medium priority.

techniques.rationale: Failure: incorrectly associating headers and data via headers/id (a td's headers attribute referencing the wrong or a non-th id). Verified axe td-headers-attr is tagged wcag131 and surfaced, and its check is exactly 'each cell using the headers attribute refers only to other <th> elements in that table' — directly catching faulty id/headers wiring (the F90 condition presupposes headers attributes exist). th-has-data-cells corroborates. Real, decided, live (shadow) detection of the exact failure. Caveat: SHADOW cross-signal scored vs gold, never an authoritative obligation disposition; per the dossier framing, surfaced+decided axe = CAPTURED-shadow.

lanes: axe:th-has-data-cells (capable,SURFACED — decided,shadow,live, but requires a <th> to be present)
techniques.rationale: Failure: a data table that does not mark up headers (all td, no th/scope/headers-id/role=columnheader-rowheader). DOWNGRADE from CAPTURED: I verified the canonical F91 example (all-td, ZERO th) trips NEITHER surfaced rule for a small table — th-has-data-cells only validates <th>/columnheader/rowheader elements that EXIST (a table with no th has nothing to flag, so it passes), and td-has-header applies only to tables LARGER than 3x3 (dataTableLargeMatches). So a <=3x3 all-td data table slips both rules. Large all-td tables ARE caught (td-has-header) and a malformed th IS caught (th-has-data-cells), so coverage is real but partial, not full. Shadow-tier only.
techniques.gap: Small (<=3x3) all-td data tables with no <th> at all — the canonical F91 case — trip neither rule (th-has-data-cells needs a th present; td-has-header needs >3x3); coverage is shadow-tier, not authoritative.
techniques.recommendation: Add a runner-tier (or surfaced) confirmation for small data tables lacking any th/scope/role=columnheader to close the size-gate / no-th blind spot.

techniques.rationale: Failure: applying role=presentation to an element whose semantics DO convey information (e.g. role=presentation on a real data <table>), suppressing needed semantics. VERIFIED axe presentation-role-conflict carries tags [cat.aria, best-practice, ACT] with NO wcag131 — so it is NOT in the surfaced set and resolves to null/drop even when it fires. No catalog runner detects role=presentation on semantic content. The 'these suppressed semantics should have conveyed info' judgment is content-level, handled only by the inert info-relationships rubric. No live lane catches it.
techniques.gap: presentation-role-conflict is not surfaced (no wcag131 tag); no live lane flags role=presentation on a data table or other semantic content.
techniques.recommendation: Add an explicit rule-id->1.3.1 mapping to surface axe presentation-role-conflict (note it is best-practice tagged, so tag-based surfacing alone won't pick it up), OR add a detector for role=presentation on <table>/list/heading carrying real structure.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — form controls, programmatic name + visible label)
techniques.rationale: Failure across 1.3.1/2.5.3/4.1.2: a control has VISIBLE label text but NO accessible name (or aria-labelledby pointing to a non-existent id). For FORM controls, field-label-probe authoritatively verifies programmatic name present + visible label, and ax-state-diff verifies a name on activatable controls — so a form input with a visible label but empty accessible name IS caught authoritatively, including the dangling-aria-labelledby variant (empty name). Verified axe label carries wcag412, not wcag131, so it is NOT surfaced for 1.3.1. However: (a) broader F111 scope (links, image-in-link controls) is only covered for controls in the catalog runners' reach, and (b) check #3 (accessible name CONTAINS the visible label text) is a match judgment in the inert 3.3.2 rubric, not authoritative.
techniques.gap: Check #3 (accessible name must contain the visible label text) is not authoritatively assessed; non-form controls with a visible-but-unassociated label may fall outside catalog-runner reach.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the 3.3.2 field-label rubric for the name-contains-visible-label judgment; ensure the no-accessible-name check covers links/buttons, not just inputs.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: mark up structure with appropriate semantic elements (em/strong/cite/blockquote, lists, tables, headings, phrase-level semantics). Verified list/listitem/definition-list/dlitem all carry wcag131 and are surfaced — they verify list/dl well-formedness as live shadow signal, and the surfaced table rules verify table structure. But verifying that ALL content with a semantic function uses the right element (the actual G115 test) requires content judgment from the inert info-relationships rubric. Partial: structural well-formedness of lists/tables is checked live; completeness of semantic markup is not.
techniques.gap: No live lane verifies that all semantically-meaningful content (emphasis, citations, quotes) uses appropriate semantic markup; only list/table well-formedness is checked.
techniques.recommendation: Keep list/table axe rules surfaced; activate the info-relationships rubric to judge whether semantic content is correctly marked up.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: when information is conveyed by a variation in text presentation, ALSO state it explicitly in text. This is the positive counterpart to F2/F43 failures and requires judging whether visually-conveyed meaning is mirrored in text — content judgment. Surfaced p-as-heading catches the one heading sub-case live (shadow); the general case is only the inert info-relationships rubric + guidance skill. No authoritative lane.
techniques.gap: No live lane verifies that meaning carried by text-presentation variation (beyond the pseudo-heading case) is also available as explicit text.
techniques.recommendation: Activate/extend the info-relationships rubric to detect presentation-only meaning lacking a text equivalent.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: separate information/structure from presentation (HTML structural elements + CSS, or tagged PDF). For the HTML-with-CSS example this is in-domain and is essentially the same 'structure is encoded, not just visually implied' goal as G115 — assessable as a content/structure judgment by the inert info-relationships rubric, with surfaced axe list/table rules corroborating well-formedness of specific structures live. The tagged-PDF example is out of our domain. Net: partial, with a live well-formedness touch plus inert meaning judgment.
techniques.gap: No live lane confirms structure is logically separated from presentation across the whole page; only specific structures (lists/tables) are well-formedness-checked via surfaced axe.
techniques.recommendation: Cover via the info-relationships rubric (structure-vs-presentation separation); the PDF path is out of scope.

lanes: llm-rubric:2.4.6 heading-descriptive / 1.3.1 info-relationships (shadow,inert — descriptiveness only, NOT nesting)
techniques.rationale: Advisory: organize the page with headings that identify each section, properly nested (h1>h2>h3...). Verified axe heading-order ('levels only increase by one') + empty-heading are CAPABLE of the nesting/presence check but best-practice tagged (no wcag131) so NOT surfaced. CORRECTION: the cited 2.4.6 rubric explicitly judges DESCRIPTIVENESS only ('missing heading/nesting is 1.3.1, not here'), and the 1.3.1 rubric punts heading-skip to best-practice — so the rubric touch on nesting/organization is tangential. The legitimate PARTIAL basis is the capable-but-NOT-surfaced heading-order/empty-heading rules.
techniques.gap: No live lane inventories headings, checks each section has one, and validates nesting/order; the capable axe heading rules are not surfaced and the rubric only judges descriptiveness.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe heading-order/empty-heading into v3 (or add a heading-outline detector) and run the 2.4.6 rubric for descriptiveness.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — label PRESENCE only, NOT position)
techniques.rationale: Advisory: POSITION form labels predictably (before text fields; after checkboxes/radios; above/side per language direction). Verified field-label-probe confirms a label EXISTS and is visible but does NOT evaluate the geometric POSITION of the label relative to its field — the entire point of G162. No lane performs the positional/geometry analysis; the collector has geometry capability but no lane applies it to label placement. No rubric covers label position. The label-presence check is necessary-but-not-sufficient and addresses a different obligation, so the technique's specific condition is uncovered.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses the spatial position of labels relative to their fields (the predictability-of-position quality).
techniques.recommendation: Add a geometry-based detector comparing label bounding box to field bounding box against the expected pattern (before for inputs, after for checkboxes/radios); low priority (advisory).

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: use semantic markup (em, strong, cite, blockquote, q, sub, sup, code) to mark emphasized/special text so it is programmatically determinable; the accessibility-relevant test is whether content conveying meaning through presentation USES this markup (inverse is F2/G117). Verified no authoritative runner checks for phrase-level semantics and no surfaced axe wcag131 rule targets em/strong/sub/sup/cite (the surfaced wcag131 set is table/list/dl/p-as-heading/aria-required-children/parent). Only the inert info-relationships rubric and guidance skill conceptually assess it. No live decided signal.
techniques.gap: No live lane verifies emphasized/special text is marked with appropriate phrase-level semantic elements.
techniques.recommendation: Activate/extend the info-relationships rubric to flag visually-emphasized text lacking semantic markup (the H49/F2/G117 cluster).

techniques.rationale: Sufficient: use native semantic HTML region elements (header/nav/main/section/form/aside/footer) to implicitly create landmarks, naming section/form where required. Same coverage profile as ARIA11 (its ARIA twin): no authoritative landmark verifier, and axe's region/landmark-unique rules are CAPABLE but best-practice tagged (no wcag131) so NOT surfaced. CORRECTION: the cited info-relationships rubric does not assess landmark presence (explicitly best-practice in its prompt), so that touch is tangential; PARTIAL rests on the capable-but-NOT-surfaced axe landmark rules.
techniques.gap: No live lane confirms native landmark elements are used correctly and that section/form landmarks needing names have them; the capable axe landmark rules are not surfaced.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe region/landmark-unique rules into v3 and/or add a native-landmark inventory detector; defer correctness-of-element judgment to the info-relationships rubric.

audit_changes.why: Factual correction: the analyst dismissed axe aria-required-children/aria-required-parent as not-surfaced/irrelevant, but I verified (axe-core 4.12.1) both carry the wcag131 tag and 1.3.1 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, so they ARE surfaced as decided shadow findings. A malformed role=radiogroup missing its required radio children trips aria-required-children — a narrow but real live shadow proxy for broken radiogroup grouping integrity (parallel to F46's table-rule proxy). That raises the verdict above NOT_CAPTURED.

Overclaim: the analyst credited ax-state-diff role-exposure (authoritative,live) and keyboard-activation as covering F42, but verified NO lane scans for a click-handler-bearing non-anchor lacking role=link. ax-state-diff verifies name/role/state ARE EXPOSED on a control it is pointed at; it does not flag an emulated link's role MISMATCH (the analyst itself conceded this). keyboard-activation covers only the 2.1.1 half, link-name is wcag244/wcag412 not surfaced for 1.3.1. The cited authoritative lanes are adjacent-SC coverage, not the 1.3.1-specific role-exposure failure, which is uncovered.

Overclaim: verified the canonical F91 case (all-td, zero th) trips NEITHER surfaced rule for a small table — th-has-data-cells only validates th/columnheader/rowheader elements that EXIST (a no-th table passes), and td-has-header applies only to tables LARGER than 3x3 (dataTableLargeMatches). So a <=3x3 all-td data table slips both rules. Large all-td tables and malformed-th tables ARE caught, so coverage is real but partial, not full.

scs.title: Meaningful Sequence
scs.summary: SC 1.3.2 is touched by exactly one substantive harness signal — the shared visualOrderDivergence detector exposed as the VSR reading-order check (vsr-analysis, sc:'1.3.2', kind:'reading-order'); it is SHADOW, opt-in (opts.runInstruments+resolveUrl), and explicitly UNCALIBRATED high-recall triage (review:true, calibrated:false) that ONLY flags within-column backward jumps and never cross-column moves, so it cannot verify or fail any technique; no authoritative catalog runner, no LLM rubric, and no surfaced axe rule exists for 1.3.2. So the CSS/element-reordering techniques C27, F1, G57 get PARTIAL coverage via this triage; F49 (layout-table linearization) is NOT_CAPTURED because its failure is the cross-column interleaving the detector is built to never flag; the plain-text/within-word whitespace failures F32/F33/F34 are NOT_CAPTURED (no character/text-level detector); PDF3 is out of domain.

lanes: instrument:kbd-graph tab-order, emits sc:'2.4.3' — same algorithm, co-signal only (shadow,opt-in,uncalibrated)
techniques.rationale: C27 verifies that DOM/source order matches visual presentation order. The vsr-analysis reading-order lane delegates to visualOrderDivergence with sc:'1.3.2', comparing the DOM-driven reading order against visual (row-banded) geometry — exactly the DOM-vs-visual-order question C27 addresses. But it is opt-in, SHADOW, and INTENTIONALLY high-recall uncalibrated triage (review:true, calibrated:false): it only flags within-column backward jumps, never cross-column moves, and its absence is explicitly NOT a pass. So it cannot authoritatively VERIFY that DOM order matches visual order, which a sufficient technique requires. The kbd-graph signal is the same algorithm but emits under sc:'2.4.3' (focus order), so it is only a conceptual co-signal here, consistent with C27 also flagging keyboard focus-prediction as an affected modality.
techniques.gap: No authoritative or calibrated lane confirms DOM order equals visual order; cross-column/Z-order/RTL geometry is undecidable by the x-overlap column model, and a clean run does not establish the technique is satisfied.
techniques.recommendation: Add an LLM rubric for 1.3.2 reading-order that judges DOM-vs-visual order on the VSR transcript + screenshot, using the order-check findings as a prior; treat as PROVISIONAL fill, not authoritative.

techniques.rationale: F1 is CSS absolute-positioning that visually reorders content so the visual sequence differs from the programmatic (source) reading order, changing meaning. The reading-order triage compares DOM-driven reading order to visual geometry and flags within-column backward steps — conceptually the divergence F1 produces. In F1's own worked example the source-order Wisconsin/Idaho swap is a within-column (right-column) inversion the detector CAN flag, so at least some F1 instances surface. But it is uncalibrated SHADOW triage: cross-column reorderings are deliberately never flagged, so column-to-column F1 instances are missed, and any flag is a review prompt, not a detected-failure verdict; absence is not a pass.
techniques.gap: Cross-column CSS-positioning reorderings are not flagged; the lane is uncalibrated and cannot decide whether the divergence actually changes meaning; absence is not a pass.
techniques.recommendation: Surface the vsr reading-order findings into v3 as a 1.3.2 triage signal and pair with an LLM rubric that judges whether CSS-positioned visual order diverges meaningfully from source order.

techniques.rationale:
F32 is white-space characters (space,  , line break) inserted WITHIN a single word to control letter spacing, so a screen reader spells it out or mis-reads it (e.g. 'W e l c o m e', the kanji '東 京' read as 'Higashi Kyo', or
-stacked vertical text). This is a character/text-string-level condition inside a text node. order-check/vsr-analysis operate at the element/geometry level on distinct leaf rects (and require >=3 comparable leaves) and never inspect intra-word whitespace; there is no LLM rubric, no axe rule, and no skill detector for this. It is runtime-observable in the DOM (so in domain) but nothing in the harness assesses it.
techniques.gap:
No lane inspects text-node content for runs of whitespace/ /
that fragment words; the failure is completely undetected.
techniques.recommendation:
Add a deterministic text-content detector: scan visible text nodes for intra-word whitespace/ /single-char
runs (with an initialism/inter-word exemption per the technique) and emit a 1.3.2 triage finding.

techniques.rationale: F33 is using white-space characters to fake multiple text columns inside a single plain-text block (e.g. a <pre> with two columns of WCAG prose), so the screen reader reads across both columns and interleaves the lines. The faux columns live inside ONE text node with one rect, so order-check (which needs >=3 distinct positioned/leaf ELEMENTS) sees nothing to compare; no axe rule, no rubric, only the guidance skill conceptually relates. Note the technique covers both 1.3.1 and 1.3.2.
techniques.gap: No detector for multi-space/tab column gaps within a single plain-text/<pre> block; the interleaved reading-order failure is not assessed.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic plain-text-layout detector that flags <pre>/text blocks with repeated multi-space or tab runs forming column gutters, as a 1.3.2 (and 1.3.1) triage signal.

techniques.rationale: F34 is white-space characters used to lay out a TABLE in plain text (e.g. a <pre> menu with day/meal columns) with no table structure, so reading order is meaningless. Same family as F33: the layout lives inside one text node, so nothing in the harness inspects whitespace-formatted tabular layout inside a text block. order-check/vsr operate on distinct elements/geometry, not internal whitespace; no axe rule, no rubric; only the guidance skill is conceptually adjacent. Covers both 1.3.1 and 1.3.2.
techniques.gap: No detector for whitespace-aligned tabular layout in plain text (<pre>/text blocks); the failure is undetected.
techniques.recommendation: Extend the proposed plain-text-layout detector (see F33) to recognize multi-row/multi-column whitespace alignment characteristic of faux tables and emit a 1.3.2/1.3.1 triage finding.

techniques.rationale: F49 is an HTML layout table whose source linearization (row-by-row, with rowspan/nested-table interleaving) does not match the meaningful visual sequence (museum example: a left-column nav-link list interleaved with a right-column image/placard/heading/description). The vsr reading-order lane derives order from the DOM and compares to visual geometry, but it clusters items into x-overlap COLUMNS and ONLY flags within-column backward jumps — it deliberately NEVER flags cross-column moves. F49's failure is precisely the cross-column interleaving (left nav vs right content): within each column the items stay in source=visual top-to-bottom order, so the detector flags nothing on the canonical F49 example. The one thing the lane can detect (within-column inversion) is not what F49 is about, so the link is tangential rather than partial; the grouping-and-reading-order skill is guidance only and, as with F32/F33/F34, does not by itself lift this above NOT_CAPTURED.
techniques.gap: No authoritative linearization check; the only order signal is structurally blind to F49's cross-column/rowspan interleaving, and no lane judges whether the linearized order preserves the meaningful sequence.
techniques.recommendation: Add a layout-table linearization triage (detect presentation-role/no-header tables, linearize cell source order, and compare to visual geometry across columns — NOT gated by the within-column rule) plus an LLM rubric to judge whether the linearized order preserves the meaningful sequence.

lanes: instrument:kbd-graph tab-order, emits sc:'2.4.3' — same algorithm, co-signal only (shadow,opt-in,uncalibrated)
techniques.rationale: G57 is the general 'order content in a meaningful sequence' technique; its test linearizes the content and checks the order yields the same meaning. The vsr reading-order triage addresses the order-divergence half, and the grouping-and-reading-order skill provides judge guidance. But verifying a SUFFICIENT technique requires confirming the linearized order preserves MEANING — a semantic judgment no harness lane makes — and the only signal is uncalibrated SHADOW triage whose absence is explicitly not a pass and which never flags cross-column moves. The kbd-graph signal is the same algorithm under sc:'2.4.3' (focus order), a conceptual co-signal only.
techniques.gap: No lane judges whether the linearized reading order preserves meaning; no authoritative or calibrated confirmation that the sequence is meaningful; cross-column order is undecided.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 1.3.2 LLM rubric that evaluates whether the VSR/linearized reading order preserves meaning vs the visual layout, consuming the order-check triage findings as priors; keep PROVISIONAL/shadow, not authoritative.

techniques.rationale: PDF3 concerns tab and reading order in tagged PDF documents, set in authoring tools (Word/OpenOffice/Acrobat Pro) via tag/structure order. The harness assesses rendered web pages at runtime and does not author or assess PDFs, so this is outside its domain. Conceptually it is the PDF analogue of C27/G57 (reading and tab order must follow the logical/visual order), but no runtime-web signal applies.
techniques.recommendation: None — out of domain (PDF authoring/tagging).

audit_changes.why: Overclaim. The vsr reading-order detector clusters items into x-overlap columns and ONLY flags within-column backward jumps, deliberately never flagging cross-column moves (verified in order-check.js lines 60-80). F49's failure is exactly cross-column interleaving — in the canonical museum example the left nav-link column and the right image/placard/description column are each in source=visual order, so the detector flags nothing. The single thing the lane can detect is not what F49 is about, so the link is tangential, not partial; the guidance skill alone does not lift it (consistent with F32/F33/F34 NOT_CAPTURED). Dropped the vsr-analysis lane and kept only the guidance skill.

Verdict unchanged, but corrected the kbd-graph lane label: kbd-graph's tabOrderFindings calls visualOrderDivergence with sc:'2.4.3', kind:'tab-order' (kbd-graph.js line 69), so it emits a 2.4.3 focus-order finding, not a 1.3.2 finding. Relabeled it as a same-algorithm 2.4.3-scoped co-signal rather than a 1.3.2 lane to remove the implied liveness/scope overclaim.
Verdict unchanged; same kbd-graph lane-label correction as C27 (the tab-order signal emits under sc:'2.4.3', not 1.3.2) and added the cross-column-undecidability caveat to the gap.

scs.title: Use of Color
scs.summary: SC 1.4.1 Use of Color has NO authoritative deterministic runner and NO LLM rubric in v3; its only mechanical signal is axe's link-in-text-block rule (carries wcag141, runs at collection, computes the 3:1 surrounding-text luminance test and presence of a non-color distinction), but v3 DROPS it because 1.4.1 is not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4} — so the three color-only-LINK techniques (F73, G182's link subset, G183's contrast half) are capable-but-not-surfaced (PARTIAL), IBM r_color is an INERT review-only triage prior, and the color-in-image (F13/G111), redundant-text (G14), and required/error-field-color (F81/G205) techniques have no detecting lane at all (NOT_CAPTURED).

techniques.rationale: C15 is an advisory CSS technique: enhance a component's visual appearance (background-color, outline) on :focus AND :hover so interactivity/scope is signalled. The catalog focus-visual-retry runner (bound to 2.4.7, authoritative+live) detects whether a focus-DEPENDENT visible indicator appears on real keyboard focus — that genuinely assesses the focus half of C15's quality. But C15 explicitly also covers the pointer-HOVER path, and v3 has no hover-feedback detector for interactive elements (the catalog hover-content runner is content-on-hover for 1.4.13, not focus/hover style enhancement). So one of the two dimensions is assessed and the runner is bound to 2.4.7, not surfaced as a 1.4.1 advisory signal.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses the hover/pointer visual-feedback half of C15; the focus half is covered by the 2.4.7 runner but is not bound to 1.4.1 as an advisory quality signal.
techniques.recommendation: None required for an advisory; optionally extend focus-visual-retry (or a new hover-state vision probe) to also capture pointer-hover enhancement on interactive elements and surface it as a 1.4.1 advisory cross-signal.

techniques.rationale: F13 fails when an image conveys information via color differences (e.g. red bars = below quota) but the text alternative omits that color-conveyed meaning. Detecting it requires reading the image pixels for color-encoded information AND comparing against the alt text — a vision+semantic judgment. The 1.1.1 alt-text-adequacy rubric is the closest mechanism but it is INERT, not mapped to 1.4.1, and scoped to general alt adequacy (missing/placeholder/mismatched), not 'is color-conveyed information present in the alt'. No axe rule (color-contrast is text-vs-background readability, not color-meaning-in-image) and no authoritative runner evaluates color-info-in-alt. The color-and-visual-text skill is guidance only.
techniques.gap: No lane detects the failure of an image's text alternative to convey color-encoded information; even the alt-text rubric (inert) does not test the color-information dimension.
techniques.recommendation: Extend the 1.1.1 alt-text-adequacy rubric prompt to flag when an image visibly encodes information by color (charts, status colors) yet the alt text omits it, and cross-tag the finding to 1.4.1; or add a dedicated 1.4.1 color-in-image rubric.

techniques.rationale: F73 fails when an in-text link is distinguished from surrounding text by color (hue) alone — no underline/bold/italic and <3:1 luminance difference. This is exactly axe-core's link-in-text-block rule, which carries the wcag141 tag, runs at collection, and computes the 3:1 surrounding-text luminance threshold plus presence of a non-color distinction. The capability EXISTS and RUNS, but surfaceAxeFindings drops it because 1.4.1 is not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS (verified {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4} + prefix 3.1.); the finding never reaches v3. IBM's r_color maps to 1.4.1 only as an INERT, review-only triage prior (IBM_PRIOR_SCS, never pass/fail). No authoritative runner, no rubric.
techniques.gap: axe directly detects this failure but v3 discards the result; there is no surfaced or authoritative signal. axe also only covers links inside text blocks, not other color-only link contexts.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe link-in-text-block into v3 (add 1.4.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS, or a dedicated 1.4.1 surfacing path) so the decided finding becomes a shadow cross-signal scored vs gold.

techniques.rationale: F81 fails when a required field or error field is indicated by color difference ONLY (e.g. red label, red text) with no non-color cue (asterisk, '(required)', icon, bold, or 3:1 lightness difference). Detecting it requires correlating which fields are required/in-error with whether their styling difference is color-only. v3's authoritative form runners are scoped elsewhere: field-label-probe (3.3.2) checks name/visible-label presence; form-error-probe (3.3.1) only fires BARRIER when an invalid submit produces NO error surface of ANY channel — it does not analyse whether the indication is color-only. axe color-contrast is text-vs-background readability, not color-only-meaning. IBM's r_color is an inert review prior. No rubric covers color-only required/error marking.
techniques.gap: No lane detects required/error fields distinguished by color alone; the existing form runners assess label/error presence, not the color-only nature of the indication.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 1.4.1 detector/rubric for color-only required/error markers (compare required/aria-invalid fields' styling deltas to detect color-only differences with <3:1 lightness and no text/glyph cue); could extend the forms-instructions-errors reasoning and the 3.3.1 rubric.
