techniques.rationale: G14 is sufficient when information conveyed by color difference is ALSO conveyed explicitly in (non-conditional) text — e.g. track color plus 'T1/T2/T3', required-red plus '*', green-Go plus the word 'Go'. Verifying this requires identifying every color-coded distinction and confirming a redundant text equivalent exists. v3 has no detector that enumerates color-coded information and checks for a text fallback; there is no authoritative runner, no axe rule, and no LLM rubric for 1.4.1 (confirmed: no rubric file). IBM's r_color is an inert review-only prior, not a verification of text redundancy. Only the color-and-visual-text skill (guidance) addresses the concept.
techniques.gap: No lane verifies that color-conveyed information has a redundant text equivalent.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 1.4.1 LLM rubric that judges whether color-encoded distinctions (status colors, color-coded legends/labels) are redundantly available in text; this is the core sufficient-technique check 1.4.1 currently lacks.

techniques.rationale: G111 is sufficient when, within non-text content (charts, maps, game pieces, flow charts), information conveyed by color is ALSO conveyed by patterns (hatching, distinct icons/shapes, line styles) that do not depend on color. Verifying this requires pixel/vision analysis of an image to confirm redundant non-color patterning per color-coded category. v3 has no image-pattern analysis, no authoritative runner, no axe rule, and no LLM rubric bound to 1.4.1 for color-coding-in-images. The color-and-visual-text skill is guidance only.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses whether color-coded non-text content includes redundant patterns/shapes.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 1.4.1 vision rubric for color-coded images (charts/maps/legends) that judges whether each color category is also distinguished by a non-color pattern, shape, or text label.

techniques.rationale: G182 is sufficient when colored text that conveys information carries an ADDITIONAL non-color visual cue (underline, bold, italic, font-style/size change). Its FIRST canonical case — scattered link words in a paragraph distinguished by color and needing a redundant cue (e.g. underline) — is exactly what axe-core link-in-text-block evaluates (it checks for a non-color distinction on links inside text blocks). That rule carries wcag141 and RUNS at collection, but v3 drops it (1.4.1 not in AXE_SURFACED_SCS), so the in-text-link subset is capable-but-not-surfaced. This is the SAME capable-but-not-surfaced lane that makes F73 and G183 PARTIAL, so G182's link subset must be PARTIAL for consistency. The broader scope (any color-conveying text run, e.g. status-colored list items, colored markup-language identifiers) is beyond axe and has no lane. No authoritative runner, no LLM rubric for 1.4.1.
techniques.gap: The in-text-link subset is detectable via axe but the finding is discarded by v3; the broader 'any colored-text-with-meaning has a redundant non-color style cue' verification (non-link text) has no lane at all.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe link-in-text-block (add 1.4.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS) for the link case, AND add a 1.4.1 rubric covering non-link colored text whose meaning needs a redundant non-color style cue.

techniques.rationale: G183 is sufficient when a color-only link has (1) a 3:1 relative-luminance difference from surrounding TEXT AND (2) an additional visual cue on hover (e.g. underline reintroduced). axe link-in-text-block computes exactly the 3:1 surrounding-text-vs-link luminance test (distinct from 1.4.3's text-vs-background), so it is capable of the contrast half — but v3 drops the finding (1.4.1 not allow-listed), making it capable-not-surfaced. The hover-cue half has no detector: the focus-visual-retry runner covers KEYBOARD FOCUS indicator presence (2.4.7), not pointer hover or color-only-link contrast, so it assesses neither G183 condition and is removed from the lane list. No authoritative runner or rubric is bound to 1.4.1.
techniques.gap: The 3:1 surrounding-text contrast condition is computed by axe but discarded; the on-hover-cue condition is unassessed by any lane.
techniques.recommendation: Surface axe link-in-text-block for the contrast condition (add 1.4.1 to AXE_SURFACED_SCS), and add a hover-state probe/rubric to confirm the additional on-hover visual cue.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — name presence only, not color-cue)
techniques.rationale: G205 is sufficient when a colored form-control label includes a text/character cue (e.g. '(required)') AND that cue is part of the programmatically determinable name. The catalog field-label-probe (3.3.2, authoritative+live) verifies a programmatic name + visible label EXIST, but it does NOT verify that a color-conveyed distinction (e.g. red = required) is mirrored by a text cue within that name — it cannot tell that the label is color-coded or that a cue compensates for color. So the relevant 1.4.1 condition (color meaning redundantly present as text in the accessible name) is not assessed. No axe rule and no rubric bound to 1.4.1.
techniques.gap: No lane verifies that the color-conveyed meaning of a colored label (e.g. required state shown only in red) is carried as a text cue inside the programmatic name.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 1.4.1 check/rubric that, for color-distinguished form labels, confirms a text/character cue conveying the same meaning is present in the accessible name (could reuse field-label-probe's name extraction plus a color-coding signal).

audit_changes.why: Inconsistent under-claim. The analyst's own lane list and rationale acknowledge that G182's in-text-LINK subset is evaluated by axe link-in-text-block (carries wcag141, runs at collection). That is the identical capable-but-not-surfaced lane that the analyst correctly rated PARTIAL for F73 and G183. Per the dossier convention 'axe-capable but NOT surfaced = PARTIAL', G182's link subset must also be PARTIAL, not NOT_CAPTURED. The broader non-link colored-text scope remains unassessed, which is why it stays PARTIAL (not CAPTURED) — a real subset of the technique is detectable by an existing-but-disconnected lane.

Verdict unchanged (the axe 3:1-surrounding-text contrast half is genuinely capable-but-not-surfaced, so PARTIAL is correct), but removed the overclaimed lane 'deterministic-catalog:focus-visual-retry'. That runner is bound to 2.4.7 and only detects keyboard-focus indicator presence; it assesses NEITHER of G183's two conditions (color-only-link 3:1 surrounding-text contrast / on-hover cue). Listing it inflated the lane inventory; rationale updated to state explicitly why it does not apply.

scs.title: Contrast (Minimum)
scs.summary: SC 1.4.3's flat-opaque-backdrop contrast is fully covered by the AUTHORITATIVE text-contrast-pixel runner (G18 4.5:1 + G145 3:1, with size class/exemptions), the non-uniform-backdrop failure (F83) sits only in the inert/shadow complex-backdrop rubric (PARTIAL), and the four author-specification/capability/alternate-version techniques (F24, G148, G156, G174) are genuinely uncaptured because they are code-inspection or re-render/cross-page conformance conditions no lane assesses; axe color-contrast runs but is discarded (not surfaced).

techniques.rationale: F24 fails content when an author specifies a foreground color WITHOUT a background color (or vice versa), leaving one color to be resolved from the user agent / user stylesheet — an asymmetry that creates a contrast RISK rather than a definite measurable failure. The authoritative text-contrast-pixel runner and axe color-contrast both evaluate the RENDERED, fully-resolved flat-bg contrast (including the cascaded/UA-default background), so they measure the as-rendered ratio and cannot see that only one of the two colors was author-specified. The Tests procedure is explicitly 'examine the code' for presence/absence of an author-specified fg vs bg — a CSS-cascade inspection with no rendered-contrast signal that distinguishes it from a pass. No lane inspects the fg/bg specification asymmetry. (In domain — a rendered HTML/CSS page condition — so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.)
techniques.gap: No lane checks whether an element (or its ancestor chain) has an author-specified foreground color but no author-specified background color, or vice versa. The contrast runner resolves the missing color from defaults and reports a (likely passing) rendered ratio, masking the F24 risk.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic collector check: for text nodes, walk the computed-style cascade for author-origin (non-UA) color vs background-color/background-image; flag elements where exactly one of fg/bg is author-specified and the other falls back to UA/inherited default. Surface as a SHADOW triage prior for 1.4.3.

techniques.rationale: F83 is text over a BACKGROUND IMAGE whose varied/patterned regions do not contrast with the letters. This is exactly outside the authoritative text-contrast-pixel runner: its CLEAR (NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED) path requires backdropIsSolidUniform, and over a varied image the contrast is not reducible to a single computable ratio, so the runner cannot fail-prove it either — it falls to auto-PARTIAL. The inert LLM rubric contrast-over-complex-backdrop is the explicit residue lane for this case; its charter names 'a photo, a gradient, a video frame, a patterned/semi-transparent overlay' and instructs that the WORST region governs (crisp over the dark third but vanishing over the bright third IS a barrier), which mirrors F83's per-letter and quickcheck tests precisely. But that rubric is INERT by default (needs opts.runLlm + injected agent) and is non-authoritative PROVISIONAL/shadow, so the failure is only assessed when the LLM lane is enabled and never gates conformance. axe color-contrast cannot evaluate image backgrounds and is unsurfaced anyway.
techniques.gap: The only lane that assesses F83 (text over a non-uniform image background) is the inert, non-authoritative LLM rubric; there is no live or authoritative detector for image-background contrast failure. When the runner hits a non-flat backdrop it auto-PARTIALs, and absent the LLM lane the failure goes unassessed.
techniques.recommendation: Promote the contrast-over-complex-backdrop rubric to a live shadow lane for the auto-PARTIAL (image/gradient backdrop) cases the flat-bg runner cannot dispose; ensure those PARTIAL slots are populated when opts.runLlm is on. Optionally add a deterministic 'text overlaps a background-image / gradient' detector to mark these cases for review even without the LLM.

techniques.rationale: G18 is the core sufficient technique: ensure a >=4.5:1 contrast ratio between text and the background behind it (the procedure IS the WCAG relative-luminance + ratio formula with the 4.5:1 check). The authoritative text-contrast-pixel runner computes exactly this against a flat opaque backdrop with the correct size class (small text 4.5:1) and exemptions (the catalog's NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED path requires foregroundResolved/backgroundResolved/backdropIsSolidUniform/contrastComputable/thresholdMet/notExemptText), directly verifying the technique for the cases that dominate real pages. The complex-backdrop / halo / per-letter-shading portion of G18 (text over a varying image) is handled by the inert LLM rubric as residue. The verification mechanism is live and authoritative for the principal case, so CAPTURED; axe color-contrast also computes this ratio but is discarded by v3 (capable, not surfaced).

G145 is the large-text relaxation: ensure >=3:1 for text that is at least 18pt (or 14pt bold). The authoritative text-contrast-pixel runner applies the WCAG size class via sizeClassResolved — it distinguishes large-scale text and applies the 3:1 threshold rather than 4.5:1 — so it directly verifies this technique for flat opaque backgrounds. The dossier and the catalog applicability (requires sizeClassResolved) confirm the runner's size-class handling. The complex/patterned-background portion (fogged plate, halo, per-letter shading at 3:1) is the inert LLM rubric's residue. CAPTURED via the live authoritative runner; axe color-contrast computes the same but is unsurfaced.

G148 is satisfied by the AUTHOR specifying NEITHER text color NOR background (and not using technology features that change defaults), so all colors are determined by the user agent — avoiding any contrast measurement at all. The text-contrast-pixel runner measures the as-rendered contrast (which for UA defaults would be black-on-white = pass), but it does NOT verify the TECHNIQUE: that no author-origin color/background was specified. A rendered pass does not confirm G148 (an author could specify a compliant fg/bg and still pass the runner while flunking G148's 'specify nothing' condition). The Tests procedure is a pure code/cascade inspection ('look in all places color can be specified; check none is specified') with no distinguishing rendered signal. No lane checks for the absence of any author-origin color declaration. (In domain — a rendered-page authoring condition — so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.)
techniques.gap: No lane inspects whether the page declares any author-origin text-color or background (color or image) at all. Distinguishing 'author specified nothing, relies on UA' (G148-satisfied) from 'author specified compliant colors' (G18-satisfied) requires reading the computed-style author-origin layer, which no lane does.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic collector check for the absence of any author-origin color / background-color / background-image declaration on text-bearing elements and their ancestors; emit it as a SHADOW prior for the G148 satisfaction route. Largely a confirmatory/authoring check — low priority since G18/G145 already cover the conformance need.

techniques.rationale: G156 promotes using a technology whose commonly-available user agents can change the foreground/background of blocks of text, with the author NOT overriding those user controls — its test is to set browser color overrides and confirm they take effect on the page. This requires simulating a user color-override stylesheet / forced-colors and observing whether author CSS resists it. No v3 lane re-renders the page under a user/UA color override or under forced-colors mode; the contrast runner and axe both evaluate the author's rendered colors only. The skill color-and-visual-text gives human/LLM guidance on color/text but emits no signal and does not simulate overrides. Nothing assesses the override-honoring quality. (In domain — an HTML/CSS rendered-page advisory — so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.)
techniques.gap: No lane re-renders or evaluates the page under a user color-override stylesheet or forced-colors / high-contrast mode to confirm the author does not defeat user color controls.
techniques.recommendation: Add an opt-in instrument that reloads the page under forced-colors: active (or an injected user color stylesheet) and compares text/background resolution to detect author CSS that overrides user color preferences. Advisory-tier, low priority; conceptually overlaps 1.4.8/forced-colors work.

techniques.rationale: G174 satisfies 1.4.3 via the alternate-version conformance route: provide a prominent, itself-sufficiently-contrasting control/link on the original page that switches to (or links to) a fully conforming alternate version with 4.5:1/3:1 contrast. Verifying this requires (a) detecting a style-switch/high-contrast control, (b) confirming THAT control meets contrast, and (c) confirming the alternate page conforms across all SC. v3 assesses a single rendered page state; it has no notion of a conforming-alternate-version, no detector for a contrast-switch control, and no cross-page conformance roll-up. The text-contrast-pixel runner would simply measure the original page's (possibly failing) contrast and would not credit the alternate-version route. No lane covers this. (In domain — a rendered HTML/CSS technique — so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.)
techniques.gap: No lane detects a presentation-switching control or evaluates a conforming alternate version; the harness has no alternate-version / style-switcher conformance model.
techniques.recommendation: Out of practical scope for now: add (if pursued) a heuristic detector for a high-contrast/style-switch control plus an LLM rubric to assess the alternate-version claim, but the multi-page conforming-alternate-version model is a large addition. Note as a known structural gap rather than building tooling.

scs.title: Images of Text
scs.summary: SC 1.4.5 turns on one meaning judgment — is meaningful text baked into image pixels when it could be real (live) text, modulo logotype/essential exceptions — and the harness has exactly ONE lane that addresses it: the LLM atomic rubric images-of-text-v0 (scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/images-of-text-v0.md), which is SHADOW and INERT by default; there is no authoritative/deterministic lane and no axe rule (axe-core has no images-of-text check), and the CSS advisory techniques (font-size units, letter-spacing, style-off positioning) plus C30's switcher and PDF7's OCR are not assessed by any lane, so best realistic coverage is SHADOW_OR_INERT.

techniques.rationale: C6 promotes positioning content with CSS over structural markup so meaning/reading order survives when stylesheets are removed (test: turn off CSS, confirm structural relations survive). No lane in the dossier strips CSS and re-checks that structural meaning persists. The 1.4.5 images-of-text rubric judges whether image PIXELS contain text; it explicitly does not read CSS positioning declarations nor verify a style-off fallback. The color-and-visual-text skill is guidance-only. Conceptually closer to 1.3.1 (structure programmatically determinable), but no lane assesses the 'meaning preserved with style off' condition this technique addresses. In domain (rendered-web CSS technique), just uncovered.
techniques.gap: No detector turns off CSS / styling and re-verifies that structural relationships and reading order survive; no inspection of CSS positioning declarations against structural markup.
techniques.recommendation: Out of practical scope for an images-of-text SC; if pursued, a style-off DOM/structure re-check belongs under 1.3.1 tooling rather than 1.4.5. No 1.4.5-specific action.

techniques.rationale: C8 advises using CSS letter-spacing to control intra-word spacing instead of inserting blank characters between letters (which corrupts the word and its pronunciation). Its test inspects whether CSS letter-spacing (vs injected whitespace) produced the spacing — a CSS-source / text-content authoring check. No lane parses CSS letter-spacing declarations or detects blank characters injected inside words. The images-of-text rubric judges pixels-as-text, not character-level spacing technique. Skill color-and-visual-text is guidance-only.
techniques.gap: No lane distinguishes letter-spacing CSS from blank characters inserted between letters within a word; no character-integrity / word-tokenization check on rendered text.
techniques.recommendation: Low value as an automated detector; no concrete tooling recommended for 1.4.5. None.

techniques.rationale: C12 checks that the CSS font-size value is expressed as a percentage so text scales with user/browser settings — a CSS-declaration unit check. No lane inspects computed or authored font-size units; the catalog runners cover contrast/reflow/focus/keyboard/labels, not font-size unit choice. The images-of-text rubric judges rendered pixels, not CSS units. The scalability concern overlaps 1.4.4 Resize Text, but no lane assesses font-size unit type for either.
techniques.gap: No lane reads font-size CSS declarations or classifies their units (%, em, named, px); no resize/scale verification.
techniques.recommendation: If text-scalability is wanted, add a CSS computed-style probe (font-size unit / resize-to-200% reflow check) under 1.4.4 — not strictly a 1.4.5 obligation. None for 1.4.5.

techniques.rationale: C13 checks that font-size uses a named keyword (xx-small … larger/smaller) so the user agent can scale relative to inherited size. Identical situation to C12: a CSS font-size declaration/unit inspection with no lane consuming it. No deterministic runner, no surfaced axe rule, and the images-of-text rubric does not read CSS. Skill is guidance-only.
techniques.gap: No lane inspects font-size keyword usage in CSS declarations.
techniques.recommendation: None — no automated lane planned for font-size-keyword inspection; covered (if at all) under 1.4.4 scalability tooling, not 1.4.5.

techniques.rationale: C14 checks that font-size is expressed in em units so text scales with font size. Same class as C12/C13: a CSS unit-of-declaration check that no lane performs. The harness has no font-size-unit probe; the images-of-text rubric judges pixels not CSS; skill is guidance-only.
techniques.gap: No lane reads font-size declarations or detects em-unit usage.
techniques.recommendation: None for 1.4.5; any font-scalability check belongs to a future 1.4.4 resize probe, not this SC.

techniques.rationale: C22 is the central SUFFICIENT technique: use real HTML text styled with CSS (font-family, color, size, etc.) instead of images of text. The harness's 1.4.5 images-of-text rubric is the direct counterpart — it judges whether an image element's rendered pixels are meaningful text that could be real text (REPRODUCED = barrier) vs a logo/essential/photo (NOT REPRODUCED). A NOT REPRODUCED verdict on image elements is the runtime cross-signal that text is real-text-via-CSS rather than image-of-text, i.e. C22 satisfied. But the lane is SHADOW and INERT by default (requires opts.runLlm + injected agent), only fills an auto-PARTIAL slot, and inspects image elements rather than affirmatively verifying CSS-styled text everywhere. The technique's quality is touched but neither authoritatively nor live.
techniques.gap: The only lane covering C22's condition is a non-authoritative LLM rubric that is inert by default; there is no live/authoritative verification that meaningful text is real text styled by CSS rather than baked into images, and the rubric only flags image-of-text barriers (no affirmative C22-satisfaction signal across all text).
techniques.recommendation: Activate the images-of-text rubric (opts.runLlm + agent) so its NOT REPRODUCED verdicts on image elements serve as the C22 cross-signal; keep it shadow/PROVISIONAL. No new rubric needed — extend coverage by ensuring the collector screenshots all role=img/svg/canvas/background-image text candidates.

techniques.rationale: C30 requires TWO things: (1) a UI control that switches between an images-of-text presentation and a real-text presentation, and (2) verification that activating the control yields programmatically-determined text wherever images of text had been. No lane detects a presentation/style-switcher affordance, activates it, and diffs the two renderings. The images-of-text rubric judges a single image's pixels in one rendered state — it cannot identify a switch control or confirm an alternate text view. No catalog runner, no surfaced axe, skill is guidance-only. The switch may use server-side or client-side scripting, but the technique itself is a rendered-web-page client-side affordance, so it is IN domain — just uncovered (not OUT_OF_DOMAIN).
techniques.gap: No lane discovers/operates a style-switching control or compares the image-of-text view against the switched real-text view to confirm equivalent programmatic text.
techniques.recommendation: Out of practical reach for automated detection; if pursued, a heavyweight instrument would need to find a style-switcher, activate it, and diff renderings. No 1.4.5 action — treat as a manual/LLM-agent judgment if ever needed.

techniques.rationale: G140 is the general sufficient technique of separating information/structure from presentation so semantics are programmatically determinable rather than only visually implied — applied here as the means to avoid images of text by using real text plus structure. Its core 'structure programmatically determinable' principle is a 1.3.1 condition, touched indirectly by axe findings surfaced for 1.3.1 (live, shadow) and the info-relationships rubric (shadow, inert) plus structure skills; and its 1.4.5-specific 'use real text instead of images of text' outcome is touched by the images-of-text rubric (shadow, inert). All touching lanes are non-authoritative and none assesses G140's full structure-vs-presentation separation directly; the structure lanes are only indirect to the images-of-text purpose. PDF/tagged-PDF arm of G140 is out of domain.
techniques.gap: Only indirect, non-authoritative lanes touch G140: surfaced axe 1.3.1 + inert info-relationships rubric for the structure-determinability facet, and the inert images-of-text rubric for the real-text-vs-image facet. Nothing authoritatively verifies that structure is separated from presentation in service of avoiding images of text.
techniques.recommendation: No new 1.4.5 tooling — rely on the images-of-text rubric (activate it) for the real-text outcome and existing 1.3.1 coverage (keep axe 1.3.1 surfaced; activate info-relationships rubric) as the structure-separation cross-signal. None specific to 1.4.5.

techniques.rationale: PDF7 is an authoring-time technique for scanned PDF documents: run OCR (e.g. in Adobe Acrobat Pro) to convert images of text into actual, tagged text, then verify with a screen reader / accessibility API. The harness assesses RENDERED WEB PAGES at runtime and does not author or assess PDFs. Conceptually the PDF analogue of the images-of-text obligation (replace image-of-text with real text), but the medium and the authoring workflow are entirely outside this harness's domain.
techniques.recommendation: None — out of domain (PDF authoring/OCR workflow, not a rendered-web-page runtime signal).

audit_changes.why: Verdict and authority/liveness labels are correct (PARTIAL via indirect, non-authoritative lanes). Refined the lane list only: added the images-of-text-v0 rubric (shadow, inert, indirect) as the most direct harness signal for G140's 1.4.5 application ('use real text instead of images of text'), which the analyst omitted while citing only the 1.3.1 structure-separation lanes. The 1.3.1 lanes touch G140's generic structure-determinability principle but are tangential to its images-of-text purpose; the rubric is the closer (though still inert/non-authoritative) signal. No verdict downgrade — the structure-separation link is genuine, not a false CAPTURED/authoritative claim.

scs.title: Reflow
scs.summary: SC 1.4.10 has the harness's strongest layout lane: an AUTHORITATIVE, live, page-level catalog runner (reflow-overflow-probe) that loads at a 320x256 CSS px viewport and measures HORIZONTAL overflow (scrollWidth>clientWidth), locating non-exempt overflow sources to clear, flag a BARRIER, or route 2-D/exempt overflow to an auto-PARTIAL the inert LLM rubric (reflow-no-hscroll-v0) fills; this directly captures the width-at-320 outcome of the layout/wrap/image techniques (C31/C32/C33/C37/C38) and addresses the 2-D-exemption techniques (G224/G225) at shadow/inert PARTIAL — but the probe measures only horizontal overflow (it never assesses vertical/256px sticky occlusion C34, text-only 200% resize SCR34, cross-viewport content disappearance F102, or author layout-switcher activation G206), so those are NOT_CAPTURED or guidance-only; axe/IBM contribute no 1.4.10 rule.

techniques.rationale: C31 satisfies the SC by using CSS Flexbox + media queries so layout regions wrap and content presents without a horizontal scrollbar at 320 CSS px width. The authoritative page-level reflow-overflow-probe verifies exactly that end-state: at the 320x256 viewport it computes horizontalScrollPresent (scrollWidth>clientWidth) and, if overflow exists, locates the source and either clears (noHorizontalScrollClear) or flags a barrier. The runner is mechanism-agnostic (it does not assert flexbox was used), but for a sufficient technique CAPTURED means verifying the technique-or-an-equivalent achieves clean reflow, which the runner does directly. The technique's flex order/reverse keyboard caveat is a 1.3.2 concern outside this runner.

Identical end-state to C31 but via CSS Grid + media queries: columns collapse to a single column at 320px so no horizontal scroll is required. The authoritative reflow-overflow-probe measures the same width-at-320 outcome the grid layout is meant to achieve (clean reflow vs barrier vs exempt-2D routed to the inert rubric). The runner does not assert grid was used but verifies the equivalent satisfied condition, so the technique's target is captured authoritatively.

C33 uses overflow-wrap/word-wrap:break-word so a long unbreakable URL/string does not push content past 320 CSS px. A long string in ordinary text flow (no overflow-x:auto/scroll ancestor, no table/grid/svg/map ancestor) is NOT exempt in the runner's isExempt heuristic, so when it overflows the probe sets horizontalScrollPresent + overflowSourceLocated and marks it anyNonExempt -> overflowBarrierObserved; when it wraps the probe clears. This is the runner's prototypical positive-detect case, so both the technique-satisfied and the failure state are captured authoritatively, and a wide text run is correctly not misrouted to the 2-D PARTIAL.

C34 un-fixes sticky headers/footers via min-height/max-height/min-width media queries so a sticky region does not consume most of a limited-HEIGHT viewport (256px tall / landscape). The condition this advisory promotes is vertical-dimension sticky occupancy plus focus-occlusion-behind-sticky. The catalog runner does load at 320x256 (it is NOT width-only at the viewport level), but it only MEASURES horizontalScrollPresent (scrollWidth>clientWidth) — it never measures vertical overflow, how much viewport height a sticky region occupies, or focus behind a sticky region, so it does not assess C34's actual condition at all. The only lane that touches sticky/height is the reflow-and-pointer-affordances skill, which is GUIDANCE-ONLY (judge instructions, emits no signal alone) and per the dossier is not a detector. With no deterministic lane, no rubric, and no axe/IBM rule assessing the height/occlusion condition, this is NOT_CAPTURED, not PARTIAL — a guidance-only skill does not constitute partial assessment of the condition.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses sticky-region vertical occupancy at the 256px-height / landscape constraint: the probe is horizontal-overflow-only even though the viewport is 320x256, the LLM rubric is scoped to horizontal-scroll readability, and there is no height/sticky-occupancy detector. The keyboard-focus-behind-sticky caveat (a 2.4.11 focus-obscured concern) is also not wired here.
techniques.recommendation: Add a sticky-occupancy probe at the 320x256 viewport (measure the painted height of position:sticky/fixed regions as a percentage of the 256px viewport, and/or detect vertical overflow that the current probe ignores), or extend the reflow rubric prompt to judge sticky-header/footer occlusion at constrained height; optionally cross-link the 2.4.11 focus-obscured runner for focus-behind-sticky.

techniques.rationale: C37 uses max-width:100% (+ auto height) so images shrink to their layout area and do not force horizontal scroll at 320 CSS px. An oversized image that overflows the 320px width is an overflow source the authoritative runner detects (horizontalScrollPresent + overflowSourceLocated on the image); a plain overflowing img is not auto-exempt (the isExempt heuristic only spares svg/map/table-grid/overflow-x:auto ancestors), so a layout-breaking photo is flagged anyNonExempt while a constrained image clears. The runner verifies the width-at-320 outcome this technique targets. Its secondary 256px-height-for-horizontally-scrolling-content sub-aspect is not measured, but the technique's primary mechanism maps onto the horizontal check, so CAPTURED holds.

C38 uses width/max-width + flexbox so labels and inputs stack vertically rather than overflowing horizontally at 320 CSS px. This is squarely the width-at-320 outcome the authoritative reflow-overflow-probe measures: form controls/labels spilling past 320px set horizontalScrollPresent with the control as overflowSourceLocated (a control is not in the runner's exempt set), otherwise it clears. The runner verifies the equivalent satisfied condition authoritatively.

F102 is a CONTENT-LOSS failure: content available at a wide viewport (sidebar links, labels replaced by placeholders, sections, info-images, a global search field) DISAPPEARS at 320px with no equivalent (disclosure, dialog, link, icon-menu). Detecting it requires comparing the content/affordance set across two viewport widths (e.g. 1280 vs 320) and confirming each lost element has a reachable equivalent. The authoritative reflow-overflow-probe runs at a single 320x256 viewport and only measures horizontal overflow — it would CLEAR a page that reflowed tidily precisely BECAUSE content was dropped, which is the failure. The LLM reflow rubric judges exempt-vs-barrier for OVERFLOWING content, not missing content, and is inert anyway. No axe/IBM rule covers this. So the failure is detected by no lane.
techniques.gap: No cross-viewport content-equivalence diff exists: nothing inventories content/controls at a wide width, re-checks presence/equivalent-availability at 320px, and flags elements that vanished without a disclosure/dialog/link/icon reveal mechanism.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic cross-viewport content-delta probe (capture interactive + textual content inventory at ~1280px and at 320px, diff for elements present-at-wide / absent-at-narrow with no disclosure/dialog/link/icon equivalent) and/or a paired LLM rubric judging whether vanished content remains reachable after reflow; F102 is the canonical reflow failure and is currently a blind spot.

techniques.rationale: G206 is satisfied either (a) by an in-content control that SWITCHES to a no-horizontal-scroll layout, or (b) by a layout where horizontal scrolling is needed only between columns/regions but never to read an individual line (e.g. spreadsheet columns). The harness has no lane that detects an author-provided layout-switcher control nor reasons about per-column line-readability. The authoritative reflow-overflow-probe measures the page's current/default overflow state at 320px; it neither finds nor activates the switch control, and it cannot credit the spreadsheet per-column exemption (a wide table routes to the 2-D exempt PARTIAL, which is the G225-style data-table/2D path, not G206's switcher mechanism). The skill only offers judge guidance and emits no signal alone, so the technique's actual mechanism is unassessed.
techniques.gap: No detection of an in-page style/layout-switcher affordance, no activate-then-re-measure flow, and no per-column line-readability reasoning for the spreadsheet sub-case.
techniques.recommendation: Add an instrument that detects candidate layout-switch controls, activates them, and re-runs reflow-overflow-probe on the switched state; and/or extend the reflow rubric to assess the spreadsheet per-column 'no horizontal scroll to read a line' sub-case. Mark guidance-only until then.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:reflow-overflow-probe (authoritative,live — detects overflow, routes 2-D/exempt content to auto-PARTIAL via allOverflowExemptOr2D)
techniques.rationale: G224 covers meaningful text indentation (nested lists, code blocks) where preserving indentation may require localized two-dimensional scrolling of that section, with CSS adjusting indentation per breakpoint. The runner detects the overflow; where the overflowing section sits under an overflow-x:auto/scroll ancestor (the author's 2-D affordance) the isExempt heuristic marks it allOverflowExemptOr2D and, because code cannot adjudicate whether indented code/nested-list overflow is a legitimate 2-D exception or a real barrier, the page-level reflow-no-hscroll obligation becomes an auto-PARTIAL the LLM rubric fills. The rubric prompt names 'code' as exempt content (partially covering G224's code sub-case) but does NOT explicitly name nested-list/meaningful-indentation. So the condition is assessed only by an INERT, non-authoritative rubric over a code-suppressed barrier — PARTIAL (shadow capability, default-off).
techniques.gap: The judging lane (LLM reflow rubric) is non-authoritative and inert by default (needs opts.runLlm + agent); the runner detects overflow but its 2-D exemption is mechanism-based (overflow-x:auto/scroll or table/grid/svg/map ancestor) and cannot adjudicate G224's meaningful-indentation semantics, and the rubric prompt names code but not nested-list indentation. By default no live lane resolves it beyond an auto-PARTIAL.
techniques.recommendation: No new tooling strictly required — capability exists; to activate, enable the reflow-no-hscroll rubric (opts.runLlm) so the auto-PARTIAL for indented-code/nested-list overflow gets a PROVISIONAL fill. Optionally extend the rubric prompt to explicitly name 'meaningful text indentation / nested-list hierarchy' as an exemption signal.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:reflow-overflow-probe (authoritative,live — detects overflow, routes 2-D panel content to auto-PARTIAL via allOverflowExemptOr2D)
techniques.rationale: G225 is the carousel/section-panel case: a horizontally-scrolling section is acceptable for 1.4.10 as long as each individual panel fits within 320 CSS px so no horizontal scroll is needed to read a panel (height may exceed 256px). The runner detects horizontal overflow on such a page; because the carousel typically has an overflow-x:auto/scroll ancestor, isExempt marks it allOverflowExemptOr2D and routes the page obligation to an auto-PARTIAL. The LLM rubric judges generic exempt sideways-scrolling content but is NOT calibrated to verify each panel is <=320px wide. So the condition is only partially assessed by the runner's mechanism-based exempt-routing plus the inert rubric; no live lane confirms the per-panel-fits-320 design.
techniques.gap: No deterministic per-panel-width measurement (confirm each scroll-snap panel/card is <=320 CSS px wide so individual panels read without horizontal scroll); the only judging lane is the inert, non-authoritative rubric and it is not panel-fit-calibrated. The runner's exemption is triggered by any overflow-x:auto/scroll ancestor regardless of per-panel width.
techniques.recommendation: Extend reflow-overflow-probe (or add a sub-probe) to measure individual panel/scroll-item widths within a horizontally-scrolling section against 320px, and/or sharpen the reflow rubric prompt to verify the G225 'each panel fits 320px' pattern; enable opts.runLlm to activate the existing judging lane.

techniques.rationale: SCR34 computes element size/position with JS offsetWidth/offsetHeight/offsetLeft/offsetTop so containers grow with TEXT SIZE; its test increases TEXT size to 200% via the browser's text-size adjustment (explicitly NOT zoom) and checks no text is clipped or lost. This is a text-resize/1.4.4-flavored condition, not the width-at-320 overflow the authoritative reflow runner measures. The runner loads at a 320x256 viewport (a width/zoom-equivalent check) and only measures horizontal overflow; it performs no text-only 200% resize and does not detect text clipping from containers that fail to scale. The LLM reflow rubric is also scoped to horizontal-scroll-at-320, not text-resize clipping, and is inert. So no lane assesses this technique's condition; the only listed lane is a guidance-only skill that emits no signal alone.
techniques.gap: No text-resize lane: nothing applies a 200% text-only size increase and detects clipped/overflowed/disappeared text in containers whose size was calculated rather than scaled. This overlaps the 1.4.4 Resize-Text capability the harness also lacks.
techniques.recommendation: Add a text-resize probe (set text size to 200% without zoom, then detect text clipping/overlap/loss) shared with 1.4.4; the existing 320x256 reflow runner cannot substitute because it is a viewport-width/zoom instrument measuring horizontal overflow, not a text-only resize one.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim. The analyst gave PARTIAL on the basis that the skill 'touches sticky/reflow as judge guidance' and the runner is width-only. But (1) a guidance-only skill is explicitly NOT a detector and emits no signal alone, so it cannot constitute partial assessment of C34's condition; (2) the runner does load at 320x256 (analyst's 'does not load at 256px height' is factually wrong) yet only MEASURES horizontalScrollPresent and never assesses sticky-region vertical occupancy or focus-behind-sticky — it assesses an unrelated condition, not a partial version of C34's. With no deterministic lane, no rubric, and no axe/IBM rule on the height/occlusion condition, the correct verdict is NOT_CAPTURED. Lanes trimmed to the guidance-only skill; rationale corrected on the 320x256 viewport fact.

scs.title: Non-text Contrast
scs.summary: SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast is GUIDANCE_ONLY for its core obligation (3:1 contrast of graphical objects/icons and UI-component visual boundaries): no authoritative non-text-contrast runner, no axe non-text-contrast rule, and no dedicated 1.4.11 LLM rubric exist — only the color-and-visual-text skill (judge guidance, no signal) names G207/G209; the shared focus-indicator slice (F78/G195) gets PARTIAL coverage where the authoritative focus-visual-retry runner catches the missing-indicator case but no lane measures the indicator's 3:1 contrast, thickness, or area, and G174's conforming-alternate-version equivalence is an in-domain but uncaptured gap.

techniques.rationale: F78 fails when the UA focus indicator is turned off (:focus{outline:none}) OR rendered non-visible by competing styling (a look-alike author outline, or a thick same-color border occluding the ring). The authoritative 2.4.7 focus-visual-retry runner (catalog claimFamily 'focus-indicator-visible') directly catches the primary case: it forces real keyboard focus and asserts a focus-DEPENDENT, obviously-visible change, so 'no visible indicator on focus' is caught authoritatively and live. The occlusion case is partly addressed by the focus-visible-clear rubric, whose text explicitly covers 'an indicator hidden behind/clipped by another element' — but that rubric is shadow and inert by default AND explicitly disclaims contrast judgment ('Do not judge contrast ratios... here'). So the look-alike/occluded-border cases that turn on the indicator's 1.4.11 3:1 contrast vs adjacent colors are not measured by ANY lane: the runner computes no ratio/thickness, and the rubric is told not to.
techniques.gap: The 1.4.11 3:1-contrast-of-the-indicator aspect and the look-alike/same-color-border occlusion failures are not measured by any active lane: the authoritative runner only proves indicator presence/absence (no ratio), and the focus-visible-clear rubric (inert) is explicitly told not to judge contrast.
techniques.recommendation: Activate/score the focus-visible-clear rubric for the visual-confusability cases, and extend the focus-visual-retry runner (or add a check) to diff focused vs unfocused pixels and compute the indicator's contrast ratio + thickness so look-alike/occluded-border failures are caught deterministically.

techniques.rationale: G174 satisfies the SC via the Conforming Alternate Version clause: a sufficiently-contrasting link/control on the rendered page that switches to (or links to) a fully conforming alternate page. This is a general/HTML/client-side technique acting on a single rendered web page (a visible link or style-switcher control), so it is IN the harness's domain — not OUT_OF_DOMAIN (which is reserved for PDF/Flash/Silverlight/SMIL/server-side/pure-authoring). It is simply NOT CAPTURED: no lane verifies condition (a) the control itself meets contrast AS PART OF G174, and the harness has no conforming-alternate-version / cross-page-equivalence mechanism to verify conditions (b) the alternate carries the same information/functionality and (c) the alternate conforms. The cross-page equivalence is an unimplemented coverage gap, not a non-web-runtime artifact. (Conceptually G174 is also more a 1.4.3/1.4.6 contrast-remediation pattern than a 1.4.11 non-text-contrast detector, but it remains in domain.)
techniques.gap: No lane verifies the switch/link control's own contrast in the G174 context, and there is no conforming-alternate-version / two-page-equivalence mechanism to confirm the alternate carries the same info+functionality and conforms.
techniques.recommendation: Out of current reach but in domain: would require a cross-page conforming-alternate-version comparator (detect a style-switcher/alternate-version link, follow it, and diff information/functionality + re-run conformance on the target) plus contrast verification of the control itself; track as a coverage gap rather than dismissing as out of domain.

techniques.rationale: G195 is an author-supplied visible focus indicator with quantitative Tests: indicator area >= a 1px border (or >=4px along the shortest side), focused/unfocused contrast CHANGE >=3:1 over the minimum area, else >=2px thick. The authoritative focus-visual-retry runner verifies a focus-DEPENDENT, obviously-visible indicator EXISTS on real keyboard focus (covering the first/existence test step, live), and the focus-visible-clear rubric judges adequacy (shadow, inert). But no lane computes the specific 1.4.11/2.4.13 numbers — the 3:1 focus-state contrast change, the >=2px thickness fallback, or the minimum-area sizing (no icon/box geometry-contrast detector exists in the codebase). So the technique's quantitative pass/fail thresholds are not actually computed.
techniques.gap: No lane computes the 3:1 contrast change of the focus indicator, its >=2px thickness fallback, or the minimum-area requirement; only indicator presence is authoritatively verified and adequacy is left to an inert rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic focus-indicator contrast/geometry measurement (diff focused vs unfocused pixels, compute contrast ratio + indicator thickness/area) extending the focus-visual-retry runner, and/or activate the focus-visible-clear rubric for the qualitative judgment.

techniques.rationale: G207 is the core 1.4.11 obligation: graphical objects/icons required for understanding must have >=3:1 contrast against the adjacent background (including gradient handling — test against the least-contrasting adjacent color — and the recognizability-after-removal check for overlapping-contrast gradients). No automated/authoritative/shadow lane assesses this: the authoritative text-contrast-pixel runner measures TEXT vs a flat opaque backdrop only (catalog claimFamily 'text-contrast'; it does not segment icons/graphical objects), axe-core ships no non-text-contrast rule and 1.4.11 is not on the surface allow-list {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.x}, no graphical-object/icon contrast detector exists in scripts/v3/lib, and there is no 1.4.11 LLM rubric (grep of rubric sc: tags confirms none). The ONLY relevant lane is the color-and-visual-text skill, which explicitly instructs a judge to assess whether 'a graphical object meant to be perceived clears 3:1' at the 1.4.11 threshold — but it is GUIDANCE-ONLY (emits no signal alone), so automated capture is still NOT_CAPTURED. The analyst's 'lanes:[none]' understated the relevant guidance lane.
techniques.gap: No detector identifies icons/graphical objects, segments them from background, and computes 3:1 contrast (including gradient least-contrast and still-recognizable-after-removal). The only relevant lane, the color-and-visual-text skill, is guidance-only and emits no automated signal.
techniques.recommendation: Add a dedicated 1.4.11 LLM rubric ('graphical-object / non-text contrast') that identifies meaning-bearing icons/graphics and judges >=3:1 vs adjacent/gradient background, and/or a deterministic non-text-contrast runner (locate icon/SVG/canvas regions, sample foreground vs least-contrasting adjacent pixels, apply 3:1); the color-and-visual-text skill can supply the judge prompt.

techniques.rationale: G209 requires >=3:1 contrast at boundaries between adjoining color segments within a graphic (pie-chart segments, map regions), or, where adjoining segments are <3:1, a separating border with >=3:1 against each color. No automated lane measures this: the text-contrast-pixel runner is text-only over a single flat backdrop, axe-core has no non-text-contrast rule (and 1.4.11 is off the surface allow-list), no adjoining-color/segment-boundary detector exists in the codebase, and there is no 1.4.11 rubric. The only relevant lane is the color-and-visual-text skill, which names 1.4.11 and instructs judging 'a UI-component boundary' / 'a non-text-contrast boundary that needs an eye on the crop' — but it is GUIDANCE-ONLY (no signal), so automated capture is NOT_CAPTURED. The analyst's 'lanes:[none]' understated this guidance lane.
techniques.gap: No lane measures contrast between adjoining color segments of a graphic, nor detects/validates a >=3:1 separating border. The only relevant lane, the color-and-visual-text skill, is guidance-only and emits no automated signal.
techniques.recommendation: Cover under a new 1.4.11 non-text-contrast LLM rubric extended to judge adjoining-color/segment-boundary contrast and border-separation cases, and/or a deterministic detector that samples contrast across segment boundaries in chart/map-like graphics; the color-and-visual-text skill supplies the judge guidance.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim of out-of-domain. G174 is a general/HTML/client-side technique about a control (link or style-switcher) on a single RENDERED web page — squarely in the harness's domain. OUT_OF_DOMAIN is reserved for PDF/Flash/Silverlight/SMIL/server-side/pure-authoring. The harness merely lacks a conforming-alternate-version / cross-page-equivalence mechanism and does not verify the control's own contrast in the G174 context — that is an uncaptured coverage gap, not a non-web-runtime artifact.

Lane overclaim/omission: the analyst listed 'none' but the color-and-visual-text skill explicitly targets G207's exact obligation ('a graphical object meant to be perceived clears 3:1' at the 1.4.11 threshold). It is guidance-only (no signal), so the NOT_CAPTURED verdict stands, but the relevant guidance lane must be surfaced rather than denied.

Lane overclaim/omission: 'none' is wrong — the color-and-visual-text skill names 1.4.11 and instructs judging UI-component / non-text-contrast boundaries (G209 territory). Guidance-only (no signal), so NOT_CAPTURED is retained, but the lane list is corrected to surface the skill.

Added skill:color-and-visual-text (guidance) as a relevant lane for the 1.4.11 contrast angle, and corrected the rationale: the focus-visible-clear rubric DOES cover the occlusion/clipped case per its own text but EXPLICITLY disclaims contrast judgment, so the 1.4.11 3:1-contrast slice is captured by NO active lane. Verdict remains PARTIAL.

scs.title: Content on Hover or Focus
scs.summary: 1.4.13 has a strong AUTHORITATIVE/live lane, but it is BARRIER-ONLY and open-scope-never-clearable: hover-content-tri can only DETECT a hoverable/dismissible/persistent failure, never affirmatively VERIFY the sufficient behavior — so it fully captures the F95 failure but only partially covers the sufficient SCR39 (whose satisfaction, plus the entire focus-triggered limb, falls to the inert shadow LLM rubric).

techniques.rationale: F95 fails when additional content shown on pointer hover disappears as soon as the pointer moves off the trigger toward the content (test #1), unless its appearance is UA-controlled (test #2). hover-content-tri (exp-runners.js runHoverContentTri) does exactly this on a live, authoritative lane: after hover reveals additional content it re-shows it and moves the pointer onto the ACTUAL revealed content region (tip.cx/tip.cy), re-reading the visible-text signature; if the content vanished it sets o.hoverable=false, which makes anyPropertyFails=true → BARRIER_OBSERVED. The lane is BARRIER-ONLY (catalog supports only BARRIER_OBSERVED; registry marks 1.4.13/NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED open-scope-never-clearable), which is the CORRECT shape for a failure technique: detecting F95's barrier is precisely what a barrier-only probe is for. F95 test #2 (UA-controlled exemption) is honored by the nativeTitleOnly gate (contentIsAdditional=false → no barrier), exempting the browser's own title= tooltip. F95 is a pointer-hover-only failure, so the runner's deliberate pointer-only triggering exercises the whole technique. The failure condition is directly DETECTED by a live, authoritative lane.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:hover-content-tri (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY — detects negation only, cannot verify satisfaction)
llm-rubric:hover-content-v0 (shadow,inert — the only lane that can affirmatively judge satisfaction)
techniques.rationale: SCR39 is SUFFICIENT by making hover/focus content hoverable, persistent, and dismissible (e.g. via Esc). Capturing a sufficient technique requires a lane to VERIFY the technique (or an observable equivalent) is satisfied. The authoritative lane cannot do this: hover-content-tri is BARRIER-ONLY (catalog 'hover-content-tri' defines only a BARRIER_OBSERVED support clause, accessibilitySupportDependent:{BARRIER_OBSERVED:false}, and registry 1.4.13/NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED is 'open-scope-never-clearable'). It computes dismissible/hoverable/persistent as typed-outcome diagnostics, but on success it emits NOTHING — silence (no detected barrier) is not a positive verification that SCR39's three-part behavior is satisfied. So the authoritative lane is inversely related to this sufficient technique (it would fire only if SCR39 were violated), not a verifier of it. The lane that CAN affirmatively judge dismissible/hoverable/persistent as MET is the hover-content-v0 LLM rubric, which is SHADOW and INERT by default (needs opts.runLlm + injected agent). Additionally the runner deliberately never calls el.focus() (to keep the rest baseline pristine), so SCR39's explicit keyboard-FOCUS Tests limb (onfocus reveal + Esc/dismiss without moving focus) is not exercised deterministically at all, and the persistence check uses a fixed ~1.6s dwell. The technique's specific condition (sufficient behavior is present) is therefore only PARTIALLY assessed: the pointer limb is probed only for its negation, the focus limb is unprobed, and affirmative verification lives only in an inert shadow lane.
techniques.gap: No authoritative lane verifies SCR39's satisfaction: (1) the runner is BARRIER-ONLY/open-scope-never-clearable, so it can never positively confirm hoverable+persistent+dismissible are met — it only detects their failure; (2) SCR39's keyboard-FOCUS Tests limb (onfocus reveal, then Esc/dismiss without moving focus) is never exercised (runner never calls el.focus()); (3) the persistence dwell is a fixed ~1.6s, so a slow auto-dismiss timer >1.6s would be mis-read as persistent. Affirmative judgment of all three properties (and the focus limb) currently falls only to the inert hover-content-v0 LLM rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Treat SCR39 as PARTIAL until an affirmative verification path exists. Concretely: (a) surface the hover-content-v0 rubric as a live shadow lane (opts.runLlm) so the focus limb, the persistence-timer residue, and the satisfied-state judgment are at least recorded/scored; (b) add a focus-triggered limb to hover-content-tri (real el.focus() to reveal, measured against a separately-captured pristine baseline, then probe dismiss-without-moving-focus) to cover SCR39's focus path; (c) parameterize/lengthen the ~1.6s persistence dwell to catch slow auto-dismiss timers. Authoritative CLEAR remains intentionally undecidable (open-scope-never-clearable), so SCR39 cannot be promoted to CAPTURED via the deterministic lane alone.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim. The analyst credited hover-content-tri with verifying SCR39's hoverable/persistent/dismissible as satisfied ('anyPropertyFails===false and no BARRIER_OBSERVED is set — the runtime-observable equivalent of SCR39's Tests procedure'). But the catalog/registry show the runner is BARRIER-ONLY and 1.4.13/NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED is open-scope-never-clearable: it emits nothing on success, so silence is not a positive verification of a SUFFICIENT technique. The only lane that can affirmatively judge satisfaction is the INERT shadow LLM rubric, and SCR39's explicit keyboard-focus Tests limb is never exercised (runner never calls el.focus()). Authoritative coverage of the sufficient behavior is therefore partial, not complete.

scs.title: Keyboard
scs.summary: 2.1.1 has a genuine AUTHORITATIVE lane (catalog keyboard-activation, live) but it is BARRIER-ONLY by registry decree — the clearing direction is WITHDRAWN (open-scope-never-clearable), so the runner can ONLY flag a BARRIER on a reached, focusable, finite-contract activation control whose real Enter/Space produces no observable effect; it can NEVER positively confirm keyboard operability, which caps the sufficient (G90/G202) and advisory (SCR29) techniques at PARTIAL. The runner is gated twice — the obligation enrolls only for focusable elements (oracle), and activation runs only for isActivationControl (role/native button/link/input) — so the canonical 2.1.1 failures (F42 bare span/img, F54 mouse-only handler, F55 onfocus=blur) and even F42's own focusable-but-roleless img are below the gate and undetected; kbd-graph records tab order but never enumerates keyboard-orphan clickables, axe contributes nothing, and there is no 2.1.1 LLM rubric.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — fires only on a focusable element that is ALSO an isActivationControl (role=button/checkbox/... or native button/A[href]/INPUT)
kbd-graph tab-order walk (shadow,opt-in) — records the focus ring; emits no keyboard-orphan signal
techniques.rationale: F42's 2.1.1 half is 'emulated link cannot be activated by keyboard.' Two gates block detection of F42's own examples. (1) The bare / (no tabindex) is not focusable, so oracle familiesFor never enrolls a keyboard-operable obligation (oracle line 105 requires focusable===true). (2) F42's keyboard-support example (, no role, no href) IS focusable and IS enrolled, but it is NOT an isActivationControl (exp-runners 941-943 require enterSpaceRole OR native BUTTON/A[href]/INPUT) — an IMG with no role/href fails, so the runner returns valid:false ⇒ auto-PARTIAL, never reached for activation. Only a focusable element carrying an interactive ROLE (e.g. ) would be reached and could BARRIER (noKeyEffectStable) — that narrow variant is the only authoritatively touchable slice, and even it can only BARRIER, never clear. kbd-graph walks the actual focus ring and emits no signal for clickables missing from it. The F42 role-emulation half (1.3.1/4.1.2) is out of this SC's scope.
techniques.gap: No lane detects a non-focusable pointer-only emulated link (below the focusable enrollment gate), nor a focusable-but-roleless emulated link (below the isActivationControl gate). No lane flags 'interactive-looking element missing from the keyboard order.' Only a focusable+interactive-role variant is touchable, and that only in the BARRIER direction.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic keyboard-orphan detector: at collection, enumerate elements carrying activation handlers (onclick/onmousedown/pointer*) or interactive ARIA roles that are NOT in the kbd-graph focus ring (no tabindex / not natively focusable), and emit a 2.1.1 BARRIER candidate. Independently, relax the keyboard-activation enrollment/applicability so a focusable element bearing an activation handler is enrolled even without an interactive role/native tag.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — catches only the focusable + isActivationControl subset
kbd-graph tab-order walk (shadow,opt-in) — no keyboard-orphan signal
techniques.rationale: F54 is the canonical 2.1.1 failure: a pointing-device-specific handler (onmousedown/up, gesture) is the only way to invoke a function, with no keyboard equivalent and no path-dependence exception. The keyboard-activation runner is the right authoritative consequence-lane (real Enter/Space yields no effect ⇒ BARRIER), but F54's literal example ( with no tabindex) is non-focusable, so the obligation is never enrolled (oracle requires focusable===true) and the element is never activated. Even a focusable img/div would fail the isActivationControl gate. The runner observes only whether real key activation has an effect on already-focusable activation controls; it does not inspect that the handler set is mouse-only, and it cannot reason about the path-dependence exception.
techniques.gap: The single most common 2.1.1 failure — a pointer-only handler on a non-focusable element — is undetected: such elements are below both the focusable enrollment gate and the isActivationControl gate, and no lane flags pointer-only handlers lacking a keyboard counterpart. The path-dependence exception is also unassessed.
techniques.recommendation: Add a collection-time detector that flags elements whose ONLY activation affordance is a pointing-device handler (mousedown/up, pointer*, gesture) with no onkeydown/keyup/keypress and no native keyboard activation, emitting a 2.1.1 BARRIER/review prior. Pair it with the keyboard-orphan detector recommended for F42.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — at best incidental; the onfocus=blur defeats the runner's own focusable check so the obligation likely never even enrolls
kbd-graph tab-order walk (shadow,opt-in) — ring-walk disrupted by self-blur, but no explicit 'focus did not persist' signal
techniques.rationale: F55 fires when script removes focus on receipt (onfocus=this.blur()), so focus cannot rest and the element is operable only by pointer. The test is: focus an element, then verify focus REMAINS until the user moves it. No lane runs that specific post-focus-stability assertion. The analyst said the activation runner 'could indirectly surface it,' but the linkage is weaker than claimed: the runner's own gate does el.focus() then checks document.activeElement===el (exp-runners 949) — onfocus=blur makes that FALSE, so targetIsFocusable=false; and the oracle only enrolls the obligation when the collector recorded focusable===true, which the same self-blur defeats. So F55 most likely produces neither enrollment nor a barrier — coverage is incidental at best. The 2.4.7 focus-visual-retry runner observes the focus-indicator side, not the scripted-blur mechanism.
techniques.gap: No lane performs F55's specific test — focus an element, then verify focus persists (no scripted blur on focus). The self-blur actually defeats the runner's own focusability detection, so even the incidental path is unreliable.
techniques.recommendation: Add an instrument that, for each focusable element, programmatically focuses it and checks document.activeElement still equals it after a microtask/short delay; flag a 2.1.1 (and 2.4.7/2.4.13/3.2.1) BARRIER when focus is auto-removed (onfocus=blur pattern). This is the only lane that would reliably catch F55.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — can only flag a dead control; CANNOT positively confirm a control is keyboard-operable
techniques.rationale: G90 is the sufficient technique 'provide keyboard-triggered event handlers so every non-keyboard handler also has a keyboard path (or a redundant keyboard mechanism)'; its test is the broad 'all functionality can be accessed using only the keyboard.' Verifying a SUFFICIENT technique requires a clearing/pass signal, but 2.1.1 is BARRIER-ONLY in the registry (NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED is WITHDRAWN, open-scope-never-clearable) — so the authoritative runner can NEVER confirm a control is keyboard-operable; it can only flag a focusable activation control whose real keys do nothing. (The analyst's claim that the runner 'authoritatively verifies the per-control half — NO_BARRIER with singleModeControl' is the overclaim: that pass verdict is structurally impossible here.) On top of that, G90's full claim is page-wide ALL-functionality including drag/drop with a redundant keyboard mechanism, which no lane verifies, and mouse-only features have no focusable control to enroll.
techniques.gap: No lane can affirm G90's positive condition: the authoritative lane is barrier-only and cannot confirm any control IS keyboard-operable, let alone that EVERY function has a keyboard path or a redundant keyboard equivalent for drag/drop and mouse-only features.
techniques.recommendation: Treat G90 as an obligation that aggregates keyboard-activation BARRIER signals over all enrolled controls plus the keyboard-orphan/pointer-only detectors (recommended for F42/F54); add an LLM rubric to judge whether mouse-only/drag features have a documented redundant keyboard mechanism. Note that, given 2.1.1's barrier-only registry, this can at most surface 'no barrier found' (absence of evidence), never a positive G90 pass.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — can only flag a dead control; CANNOT confirm per-control operability
techniques.rationale: G202 'ensure keyboard control for ALL functionality' is the most general sufficient technique for 2.1.1: identify every function, then verify each is operable by keyboard or keyboard interface (alternate methods for the same function allowed). The keyboard-activation runner reaches enrolled focusable activation controls and presses real Enter/Space, but because 2.1.1 is BARRIER-ONLY it can only flag a dead control — it CANNOT positively confirm a control responds (the analyst's 'the per-control operability half is genuinely covered' overclaims a pass the registry forbids). Beyond that, G202's distinguishing requirements — building the full functional inventory and reasoning about alternate-equivalent keyboard paths — are performed by no lane, and mouse-only functions with no focusable control are missed (same blind spot as F54).
techniques.gap: No lane builds/validates the functional inventory or reasons about alternate-equivalent keyboard paths, and the authoritative lane cannot even positively confirm individual focusable controls operate (barrier-only). Mouse-only functionality with no focusable control is undetected.
techniques.recommendation: Aggregate keyboard-activation BARRIER results into a 2.1.1 obligation, feed in the keyboard-orphan/pointer-only detector output, and add an LLM whole-obligation pass to judge functional-inventory completeness and alternate keyboard equivalence — recognizing the deterministic lane contributes only barrier evidence, never a G202 pass.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:keyboard-activation (authoritative,live,BARRIER-ONLY) — applicability IS satisfied for SCR29's <span role=button tabindex=0> example, but 2.1.1 cannot CLEAR, so the runner can only flag the failure case, not confirm SCR29's success
deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff 4.1.2 (authoritative,live) — for the companion name/role/state note
kbd-graph tab-order walk (shadow,opt-in) — confirms the control is in the tab order (check #3)
techniques.rationale: SCR29 makes a static span/div operable via tabindex=0 + onkeyup/onkeypress alongside onclick. Its example (<span id=active role=button tabindex=0>) IS focusable AND IS an isActivationControl, so applicability is genuinely satisfied: the runner enrolls it, reaches it, and presses real Enter/Space (page.keyboard.press fires keyup, so the onkeyup handler runs). The analyst correctly identified the mechanics. The OVERCLAIM is the verdict: SCR29's test (checks #4-5) is to CONFIRM that focusing the control and pressing Enter/Space DOES execute the scripted action — a positive/pass verification. But 2.1.1 is BARRIER-ONLY (registry: NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED WITHDRAWN, open-scope-never-clearable), so the authoritative runner CANNOT emit the NO_BARRIER the analyst cited; it can only flag a BARRIER when the key handler is missing/broken. So the technique's specific positive condition is verified by no authoritative lane — only its negation surfaces. That is PARTIAL, not CAPTURED. (kbd-graph still confirms tab-order presence; ax-state-diff covers the 4.1.2 companion note.)
techniques.gap: No lane can positively confirm SCR29 is correctly applied (Enter/Space DOES invoke the action). The authoritative runner is barrier-only and can only catch a broken/missing key handler; the success case yields no clearing verdict.
techniques.recommendation: If a positive SCR29 affirmation is desired, it must come from outside the deterministic catalog (which is barrier-only for 2.1.1) — e.g. an LLM/whole-obligation pass that, given the runner observed an effect from real Enter/Space, records a PROVISIONAL confirmation. Absent that, scope SCR29 to 'no keyboard-activation barrier observed on this in-order control' rather than a confirmed pass.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim: the analyst said the keyboard-activation runner 'confirms an observable stable effect (NO_BARRIER) — exactly check #5,' but registry.js makes 2.1.1 BARRIER-ONLY (NO_BARRIER_OBSERVED is WITHDRAWN / open-scope-never-clearable). The runner can never emit the NO_BARRIER that would positively verify SCR29's success condition; it can only flag a BARRIER if the key handler is broken. SCR29's test is a positive verification that the action executes, which no authoritative lane provides — so PARTIAL, not CAPTURED.

Verdict unchanged, but corrected an embedded overclaim: the rationale/lanes asserted the runner 'authoritatively verifies the per-control half — NO_BARRIER with singleModeControl.' 2.1.1 is barrier-only, so that pass verdict is structurally impossible; the runner can only flag dead controls. Lanes relabeled BARRIER-ONLY and the false NO_BARRIER pass claim removed.

Verdict unchanged, but corrected an embedded overclaim: 'the per-control operability half is genuinely covered' implied a pass the barrier-only registry forbids. Relabeled the lane BARRIER-ONLY and clarified the runner can only flag failures, never confirm per-control operability.

Verdict unchanged, but rationale corrected: the analyst implied F42's focusable img variant is 'reached and presses real Enter/Space' — in fact a focusable (no role/href) fails the isActivationControl gate (exp-runners 941-943) and is never activated. Only a focusable element with an interactive ROLE is touchable, and even that only in the BARRIER direction (barrier-only). Lane label corrected.

Verdict unchanged, but the 'indirect coverage' claim was tightened: onfocus=blur defeats the runner's own el.focus()/activeElement focusability check and the oracle's focusable===true enrollment gate, so F55 most likely never even enrolls — coverage is incidental at best, weaker than the analyst stated.

scs.title: No Keyboard Trap
scs.summary: SC 2.1.2 "No Keyboard Trap" is AUTHORITATIVELY covered for the in-DOM case by the live catalog runner keyboard-trap-escape (Tab/Shift+Tab/Esc + an advised-key probe that also detects in-region escape instructions), reinforced by kbd-graph LOTUS / vsr-graph cursor-trap shadow instruments; residual gaps are G21 path-(c) "move-to-parent documented BEFORE entry" / instruction-adequacy judgment and the opaque plug-in / non-HTML-embed (SMIL/XForms/applet) trap that exposes no probeable focusable DOM.

techniques.rationale: F10's observable failure condition is generic: keyboard focus enters a region and cannot exit via the keyboard without closing/restarting the user agent. That exact condition is what the AUTHORITATIVE, live catalog runner keyboard-trap-escape detects (runKeyboardTrapEscape in exp-runners.js: tags the trapping region, real-keyboard-reaches into it, then proves escape via forward Tab, Shift+Tab, Esc, or an advised key; trapProven is asserted only when no mechanism escapes and focus cycles back), reinforced by the kbd-graph LOTUS directional-trap and vsr-graph cursor-trap shadow instruments. F10 is IN domain — it is a rendered-page failure condition, not a PDF/Flash/server-side authoring technique. However, F10 is SPECIFICALLY framed around combining multiple content FORMATS (HTML+SVG+SMIL+XForms+plug-ins) where focus gets stuck inside a PLUG-IN. The runner is purely DOM/AX-driven: it operates over targetIsFocusable nodes located by XPath, and has no iframe/embed/object/foreign-format handling. So the failure is captured for the in-DOM case (custom JS widget, focusable HTML in an iframe) but only partially for a trap living entirely inside an opaque plug-in surface that exposes no probeable focusable DOM nodes.
techniques.gap: No coverage of focus trapped inside an opaque plug-in / embedded non-HTML format (SMIL, XForms, applet, legacy media plug-in) whose surface exposes no probeable DOM/AX focusable nodes; the catalog runner can only assert trap/escape over DOM-focusable elements located by XPath.
techniques.recommendation: None for the in-DOM trap case (authoritatively captured by keyboard-trap-escape). For the plug-in/embedded-format residue, treat as largely out of domain; optionally have the harness emit a triage prior when an <object>/<embed>/<iframe> with foreign content is present ('plug-in present — manual keyboard-exit review') so the runner's DOM-only limitation is surfaced rather than silently passed.

techniques.rationale: G21 offers three satisfaction paths: (a) Tab advancing past the final location exits the subset; (b) a keyboard function moves focus out of the subset, documented in-region; (c) the technology's native 'move to parent' command documented BEFORE entry. Paths (a) and (b) are directly verified by the AUTHORITATIVE, live keyboard-trap-escape runner: it confirms focus CAN leave via Tab/Shift+Tab/Esc, AND — contrary to a zero-coverage reading — it explicitly handles documented in-region escapes (exp-runners.js lines 867-890): it detects advisory text ('press X to leave/exit/close') and the advised key, presses that key (advisedKeyEscapes), and refuses to assert trapProven whenever in-region advisory text is present (!advice.advised is a conjunct of trapProven). So a trap that is 'rescued' by an in-region documented escape is NOT auto-failed. The kbd-graph/vsr-graph shadow instruments corroborate the no-trap condition. The genuine residual is narrower than 'no documentation lane': (i) path (c) requires the move-to-parent command to be documented BEFORE the user enters the subset — the runner only reads text INSIDE the region, never validates that instructions PRECEDE it; (ii) the runner pattern-matches only simplistic advisory phrasings / single-letter keys and does not JUDGE whether the instructions are correct, complete, or keyboard-reachable. Those meaning judgments are made by no lane today.
techniques.gap: The runner partially covers the documentation path (it detects an in-region documented escape key and will not auto-fail a trap that advertises one) but does NOT assess: (i) G21 path (c) / Tests step 3's precedence requirement — that escape instructions PRECEDE the trapping subset; (ii) whether the instructions are correct, complete, and keyboard-reachable (it only regex-matches phrasing + a single-letter key). As in F10, a trap inside an opaque plug-in exposing no probeable focusable DOM is also not reachable by the runner.
techniques.recommendation: The core escape-mechanism paths (a/b) and the in-region documented-escape case are adequately captured by keyboard-trap-escape — no action there. To close the residual, add a 2.1.2 LLM rubric (or extend a focus-management rubric) that, on a runner-flagged candidate trap, judges whether keyboard-accessible escape instructions are present, correct, and PRECEDE the trapping subset (G21 path c / Tests step 3) — surfaced as shadow/PROVISIONAL so a documented-escape case is not auto-failed; do NOT premise this on the runner ignoring documented escapes, since it already detects in-region advisory keys.

audit_changes.why: Verdict unchanged, but the rationale/gap/recommendation contained a coverage UNDER-claim that is factually wrong: they asserted 'No lane assesses whether escape instructions exist' and that 'the runner would simply report a BARRIER for content rescued by documented instructions.' The authoritative runner (exp-runners.js runKeyboardTrapEscape, lines 867-890) DOES detect in-region advisory text + the advised key, presses it (advisedKeyEscapes), and gates trapProven on !advice.advised so a documented-escape trap is never auto-failed. Corrected to scope the real gap to G21 path (c) precedence ('documented BEFORE entry') and instruction-adequacy judgment, and to rebase the LLM-rubric recommendation on that narrower, accurate gap.

Verdict, lanes, authority labels and OUT_OF_DOMAIN handling all correct; tightened the rationale to (1) state explicitly that F10 is IN domain (a rendered-page failure condition, not a PDF/Flash/server-side authoring technique) and (2) ground the plug-in gap in the verified runner mechanism (DOM/AX-only, XPath-located targetIsFocusable nodes, no iframe/embed/object handling).

scs.title: Page Titled
scs.summary: 2.4.2 presence is AUTHORITATIVE (catalog page-title slot presence, live), but title DESCRIPTIVENESS — the substance of every technique here — is covered ONLY by the SHADOW/INERT LLM rubric, and the G127 collection-relationship path has no lane at all; best realistic coverage is SHADOW_OR_INERT.

techniques.rationale: F25 is a descriptiveness failure: a title EXISTS but does not identify the page's contents/purpose (authoring-tool defaults like 'Untitled Document'/'New Page 1', non-descriptive filenames, empty/filler text, or the same templated title reused across pages). Verified in code: the authoritative lane is pageTitleSlotPresent (applicability-oracle.js L66-71), which returns true if a `title` key exists AT ALL — 'even an empty title' per its own comment — so it provably cannot detect a present-but-generic title; build-v3.js L135-137 confirms 'today the lane is LLM-provisional only' for descriptiveness. The 2.4.2 page-title rubric (page-title-v0.md L16-21) targets exactly F25's named conditions — empty/boilerplate ('Untitled','Home','Document') and topic-mismatch — but it is SHADOW and INERT by default (opts.runLlm + injected agent) and never authoritative. The 'same title across templated pages' variant is additionally uncovered: the rubric judges one page against its own viewport (L34 explicitly says 2.4.2 does NOT require a unique/cross-site title), and the harness has no cross-page corpus comparison. So the failure is addressed only by an inert, non-authoritative lane, and the cross-page-duplicate facet not at all.
techniques.gap: No authoritative/live detector for non-descriptive titles; the only lane that addresses it (LLM rubric) is inert and shadow, so the failure is never detected in a default run. The 'identical title across templated pages' facet is uncovered — single-page harness, no cross-page corpus comparison.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the 2.4.2 page-title LLM rubric (opts.runLlm + agent) so the descriptiveness failure produces a shadow/PROVISIONAL signal filling the auto-PARTIAL slot; treat it as the de facto F25 detector. For the templated-duplicate facet, add a corpus-level title-uniqueness check (out of single-page scope today) — note as a known coverage gap.
