techniques.rationale: G88 has three tests: (1) the page has a title — CAPTURED authoritatively by catalog page-title slot presence (pageTitleSlotPresent / collector document.title, live); (2) the title is relevant to the content; (3) the page can be identified using the title. Tests (2) and (3) are the substantive descriptiveness/identification checks, handled ONLY by the 2.4.2 page-title rubric (page-title-v0.md L14-32, which reads the page's real topic from the viewport h1/main heading and compares it against the effective title) — and that lane is SHADOW and INERT by default. Verified: no deterministic descriptiveness runner exists (build-v3.js L137 'LLM-provisional only') and no axe rule for 2.4.2 is surfaced (axe-surface allow-list = 1.3.1/1.3.5/1.4.4/2.4.4/3.1.x; 2.4.2 excluded). Net PARTIAL — presence authoritative, descriptiveness shadow/inert.
techniques.gap: The descriptiveness and 'page can be identified using the title' checks — the real substance of this sufficient technique — are assessable only via the inert LLM rubric; in a default run nothing authoritative verifies the title is descriptive, only that one is present.
techniques.recommendation: Activate the 2.4.2 page-title LLM rubric to fill the auto-PARTIAL slot with a PROVISIONAL descriptiveness verdict; keep slot-presence as the authoritative prerequisite. No deterministic descriptiveness check is feasible, so accept the calibrated rubric as the verification lane.

techniques.rationale: G127 is advisory: identify the page's relationship to a LARGER COLLECTION, either by encoding that relationship in the title (sub-site/chapter/edition naming) OR programmatically via the HTML link rel attribute / collection metadata. No lane assesses this. The 2.4.2 page-title rubric is scoped to single-page topic descriptiveness and explicitly states 2.4.2 does NOT require a unique/collection-positioned title (page-title-v0.md L34), so it deliberately does not judge collection-relationship. Verified by grep: no lane inspects rel=next/prev/up/contents links or collection metadata; the harness assesses one rendered page in isolation with no cross-page corpus signal to establish 'the collection'. No axe rule (2.4.2 not in the surface allow-list) and no deterministic runner covers it. In domain (an HTML/rendered-page technique, not PDF/Flash/server-side), but unaddressed by any current lane.
techniques.gap: No detection of collection-relationship signals: neither the title-encodes-collection-position pattern (needs cross-page corpus awareness) nor the programmatic rel link / collection-metadata path is inspected by any lane.
techniques.recommendation: Add a shadow detector for navigational rel relationships (link rel=next/prev/up/contents and collection metadata) and/or extend the page-title rubric prompt to optionally note collection-position cues, gated as advisory. Cross-page title-collection inference requires corpus-level analysis out of single-page scope — flag as a known limitation.

scs.title: Focus Order
scs.summary: 2.4.3 has NO authoritative lane, NO axe rule, and NO LLM rubric; the ONLY 2.4.3-tagged signal is the opt-in, uncalibrated, shadow kbd-graph tab-order divergence triage (which does partly assess the static F44/G59 source-vs-tab-order case), while the dynamic dialog/menu focus-management failure F85 is touched by NO detector — only a guidance-only skill names it — so F85 is NOT_CAPTURED and F44/G59 are at best PARTIAL.

lanes: kbd-graph collectTabOrder + order-check visualOrderDivergence, kind:tab-order sc:2.4.3 (shadow, opt-in via opts.runInstruments, uncalibrated triage; review:true, calibrated:false)
techniques.rationale: VERIFIED: kbd-graph.collectTabOrder drives REAL forward Tab keypresses from the top of the document, records the actual focus order, and tabOrderFindings feeds it to order-check.visualOrderDivergence tagged sc:'2.4.3', kind:'tab-order'. F44's prototypical case (positive tabindex 1,4,3,2 reordering the list) produces exactly the within-column backward jump this detector flags, so a lane DOES partly assess the condition. But it is opt-in (runInstruments+resolveUrl), shadow (never gates conformance), and explicitly high-recall UNCALIBRATED (review:true, calibrated:false) — it surfaces divergence for review, not a decided failure; the x-overlap column heuristic is not a true logical-order judgment; and absence of a flag is NOT a pass. No authoritative runner, no surfaced axe rule, and no LLM rubric exist for 2.4.3 (confirmed: no focus-order/2.4.3 rubric file). So PARTIAL, not CAPTURED. Lane correction: the analyst's 'vsr-analysis reading-order' entry is hardcoded sc:'1.3.2' (Meaningful Sequence), not a 2.4.3 signal, so it is not credited as a 2.4.3 lane here.
techniques.gap: No authoritative or calibrated detector DECIDES that a tabindex-reordered tab order violates content relationships; the kbd-graph triage only flags within-column backward jumps for review and there is no logical-order/meaning judgment (no LLM rubric for 2.4.3).
techniques.recommendation: Calibrate the kbd-graph tab-order divergence triage against gold and/or add a 2.4.3 LLM rubric that judges whether the recorded Tab traversal preserves content meaning/operability (compare DOM/reading order vs traversal order; flag positive-tabindex reordering).

techniques.rationale: F85 is a DYNAMIC focus-management failure: a dialog/menu opened by a trigger is not adjacent to the trigger in the nav order AND focus is not moved into it on open (nor returned to the trigger / a logical successor on dismiss). The WCAG test procedure requires a state transition: activate trigger -> observe focus location -> dismiss -> observe focus restoration. VERIFIED against kbd-graph.js + run-instruments.js: the tab-order instrument is STATIC — it Tabs from document top over the page as rendered and never activates triggers, opens dialogs, or tracks focus-on-open/focus-return; detectKeyboardTraps and the 4.1.3 status-detector cover different conditions (escape-trap, status insertion), not adjacency/focus-return. So NO detector, rubric, or authoritative lane assesses F85's specific condition. The analyst's own rationale concedes 'at best guidance-only touches it,' yet rated it PARTIAL — a guidance-only skill emits no signal and is not a detector, so the condition is not actually assessed by any lane. Downgraded to NOT_CAPTURED. In-domain (client-side rendered dialog/menu behavior), so not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.
techniques.gap: No lane simulates trigger activation -> focus-on-open -> dismiss -> focus-restoration; the dynamic dialog/menu focus-management condition has no automated detector, no LLM rubric, and no authoritative runner — only a guidance-only skill names 2.4.3.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic focus-management probe (activate dialog/menu triggers, assert focus lands in the widget or next-in-order, then on dismiss assert focus returns to the trigger or a logical successor) and/or a 2.4.3 LLM rubric covering dialog/menu open-and-dismiss focus behavior.

lanes: kbd-graph collectTabOrder + order-check visualOrderDivergence, kind:tab-order sc:2.4.3 (shadow, opt-in, uncalibrated triage; review:true, calibrated:false)
techniques.rationale: G59 is satisfied when interactive elements are placed so the default Tab order follows the content's sequences/relationships (source/visual/logical order agree). The kbd-graph tab-order instrument DOES partly assess this: it records the real Tab traversal and flags within-column divergence from visual order, so a gross mismatch would surface. But VERIFYING a SUFFICIENT technique requires affirmatively confirming the order is correct, and this lane is opt-in, shadow, and uncalibrated (review:true, calibrated:false) — absence of a divergence flag is explicitly NOT a pass, it cannot set a pass disposition, has no authoritative anchor, and the x-overlap column model cannot judge the multi-column logical grouping in G59's applicant/spouse example (it never flags cross-column moves). No axe rule and no LLM rubric exist for 2.4.3. So PARTIAL. Lane correction: the analyst's 'vsr-analysis reading-order' entry is sc:'1.3.2'-tagged (Meaningful Sequence), not a 2.4.3 signal, so it is not credited as a 2.4.3 lane here.
techniques.gap: No lane can affirmatively VERIFY that source/tab order matches logical/visual reading order; the kbd-graph triage only flags within-column divergence for review (uncalibrated, no pass authority) and cannot judge multi-column logical grouping; no LLM rubric or authoritative anchor exists.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 2.4.3 LLM rubric (and/or calibrate the kbd-graph tab-order vs visual-order comparison, including cross-column grouping) to judge whether the Tab traversal follows the content's logical/reading order, so G59 satisfaction can be assessed rather than only triaged.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim. The analyst's own rationale says 'at best guidance-only touches it,' but a guidance-only skill emits no signal and is not a detector. Verified in kbd-graph.js/run-instruments.js that the only 2.4.3-tagged instrument (tab-order) is STATIC — it never activates triggers, opens dialogs, or tracks focus-on-open/focus-return — so no detector, rubric, or authoritative lane assesses F85's dynamic trigger->dialog adjacency / focus-restoration condition. PARTIAL implies a non-authoritative detector partly assesses the condition; none does. In-domain, so NOT_CAPTURED rather than OUT_OF_DOMAIN.

Verdict unchanged, but lane list corrected: removed 'vsr-analysis reading-order' as a 2.4.3 lane because readingOrderFindings in vsr-analysis.js hardcodes sc:'1.3.2' (Meaningful Sequence), so it emits no 2.4.3 finding. The load-bearing 2.4.3 lane is the kbd-graph collectTabOrder + order-check tab-order check (sc:'2.4.3', review:true, calibrated:false), which genuinely flags F44's positive-tabindex reordering as a within-column backward jump.

Verdict unchanged, but lane list corrected: removed 'vsr-analysis reading-order' as a 2.4.3 lane (it is sc:'1.3.2'-tagged in vsr-analysis.js, not a 2.4.3 signal). The 2.4.3 triage is the kbd-graph tab-order check; PARTIAL stands because it is opt-in/shadow/uncalibrated, cannot set a pass disposition for a sufficient technique, and cannot judge G59's multi-column grouping (the detector never flags cross-column moves).

scs.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
scs.summary: For SC 2.4.4 the only LIVE lane is axe's link-name/area-alt rules surfaced as a non-authoritative shadow cross-signal (2.4.4 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS; both rules verified to carry the wcag244 tag), detecting only the hard "link/area has no accessible name" failure (F89) and the name-presence half of G91/H24/H30; there is NO authoritative catalog runner for link purpose (ax-state-diff is scoped to 4.1.2, not 2.4.4), the purpose/context-adequacy judgment lives only in the SHADOW+INERT link-purpose/alt-text rubrics, and the new-window/redundant-link advisories (G201, SCR24, H2) have no lane at all.

techniques.rationale: F63 fails when the ONLY context disambiguating an unclear link sits in unrelated content (not the same sentence/paragraph/list-item/table-cell and not via aria-label/labelledby/describedby). Detecting it needs judging (a) link text alone is insufficient and (b) whether disambiguating context is programmatically determined and locally associated. The surfaced axe link-name lane checks NAME PRESENCE only (a named-but-vague 'Read More' passes link-name), so it cannot see this. The link-purpose rubric is the only conceptually-matching lane and does reason over name+context (it mentions same-list-item/heading context), but it is shadow and inert by default and its prompt does not encode F63's explicit same-sentence/paragraph/list-item/table-cell locality test.
techniques.gap: No authoritative detector; the only matching lane (link-purpose rubric) is INERT and does not explicitly encode F63's 'context must be in the same sentence/paragraph/list-item/table-cell or via aria-*' locality rule.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the link-purpose rubric for 2.4.4 and extend its prompt with F63's locality test: flag vague link text whose disambiguating context lies outside the same sentence/paragraph/list-item/table-cell and is not bound via aria-label/labelledby/describedby.

lanes: axe:link-name (shadow,live,surfaced — 2.4.4 in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, rule verified to carry wcag244)
techniques.rationale: F89 fails when a link's only content is non-text (image with alt=""/presentation) and the link has no accessible name from any other source. axe's link-name rule detects exactly 'link element with no computed accessible name', carries the wcag244 tag, and 2.4.4 IS in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, so this violation is consumed by v3 as a live shadow finding scored against gold. The exact failure condition is detected. NOTE: the catalog ax-state-diff runner is bound to SC 4.1.2 (lib/catalog.js: sc:'4.1.2'), not 2.4.4 — it computes an AX name internally but produces no 2.4.4 disposition, so it is NOT a 2.4.4 lane and was removed; there is no authoritative 2.4.4 lane.

G53 is satisfied when an otherwise-unclear link's purpose becomes clear from its text COMBINED WITH the enclosing sentence — a semantic judgment over link text plus sentence context. The surfaced axe link-name lane confirms only that a name exists, never that text+sentence conveys purpose. The link-purpose LLM rubric is the right mechanism but is shadow and inert by default; it reasons over name+context but its prompt centers on aria/list-item/heading context and would need the enclosing sentence treated as valid context.
techniques.gap: Technique-verification (purpose readable from link text + enclosing sentence) is possible only in the INERT link-purpose rubric, with no authoritative confirmation.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the link-purpose rubric for 2.4.4 and ensure its prompt evaluates link text together with the enclosing sentence (not just aria/heading context) when the link text alone is insufficient.

techniques.rationale: G91 is satisfied when the link TEXT ITSELF describes the link's purpose. The surfaced axe link-name lane verifies a name is present (a necessary precondition) and runs live, but cannot judge whether that text DESCRIBES the purpose ('click here'/'read more' pass link-name yet fail G91). That descriptiveness judgment lives only in the link-purpose LLM rubric, which is shadow and inert by default.
techniques.gap: Descriptiveness of the link text — the heart of G91 — is assessed only by the INERT link-purpose rubric; the live axe lane covers presence only.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the link-purpose rubric for 2.4.4 so it judges whether the link's accessible name self-describes its purpose; keep surfaced axe link-name as the presence pre-filter.

techniques.rationale: G201 advises giving advance warning (visual + programmatic) when a link/button opens a new window/tab on regular activation (target=_blank etc.). No lane assesses new-window behaviour or whether a warning is present: no catalog runner, no axe rule in the 2.4.4 surface set, no link-purpose rubric clause about new windows, no signal-emitting skill. The condition (does an open-in-new-window control carry an advance warning?) is runtime-observable on a rendered page (target attribute + name/describedby text + visual icon) but nothing in the harness looks for it. IN domain (HTML/rendered page), so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.
techniques.gap: No detector for target=_blank / window.open links lacking an 'opens in new window' warning in their accessible name or description.
techniques.recommendation: Add a shadow detector (or extend the link-purpose rubric) flagging links/buttons opening a new window/tab (target=_blank or scripted window.open) whose accessible name/description gives no 'opens in new window' warning.

techniques.rationale: H2 advises combining an adjacent image link and text link to the SAME resource into a single anchor (image given null alt) to avoid redundant/duplicate links. Assessing it means detecting two adjacent anchors with the same href where one is an image and one is text — a redundant-link / DOM-structure pattern. No lane does this: not the catalog runners, not the surfaced axe set (axe's duplicate-link heuristics are not in the 2.4.4 surface; H2 is advisory good practice, not a violation), not the link-purpose rubric, no signal-emitting skill.
techniques.gap: No detector for adjacent duplicate same-href image+text link pairs that should be merged.
techniques.recommendation: Optional: add a shadow heuristic flagging adjacent anchors sharing an href (one image-only, one text-only) as a redundant-link candidate; low priority since H2 is advisory.

lanes: axe:area-alt (shadow,live,surfaced — rule verified to carry wcag244, 2.4.4 in AXE_SURFACED_SCS)
techniques.rationale: H24 requires each image-map <area> element to (1) have an alt attribute and (2) that alt serve the SAME PURPOSE as the selectable region. axe's area-alt rule carries the wcag244 tag (verified) and 2.4.4 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS, so a missing/empty area accessible name IS detected as a live shadow finding — covering check #1. Check #2 (the alt actually describes the region's purpose) is a semantic adequacy judgment no live lane makes; the link-purpose rubric is inert and is not oriented to image-map area descriptiveness.
techniques.gap: Presence of an area accessible name is surfaced (shadow); the descriptiveness/equivalence of that alt — H24 check #2 — is judged by no live lane.
techniques.recommendation: Treat surfaced axe area-alt as the presence signal, and extend/enable the link-purpose (or alt-text) rubric to judge whether each <area> alt describes the purpose of its region.

techniques.rationale: H30 requires an anchor's text or its image's text alternative to DESCRIBE the link's purpose (text-only, image-only, and mixed text+image links). The surfaced axe link-name lane verifies a name is present and runs live (covering the necessary precondition and the image-only-with-no-name case), but the core requirement — that the name/alt actually describes the purpose — is assessed only by the inert link-purpose and alt-text rubrics.
techniques.gap: Descriptiveness of the link's name/alt (the substance of H30) is covered only by INERT rubrics; the live axe lane gives presence only.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the link-purpose rubric (and alt-text rubric for image-only links) for 2.4.4 so descriptiveness is judged, with surfaced axe link-name as the presence pre-filter.

techniques.rationale: H80 is satisfied when an unclear link's purpose is resolved by the PRECEDING HEADING combined with the link text. Verifying it needs associating a link with its preceding heading and judging whether heading+link text conveys purpose — structural + semantic. The link-purpose rubric is the matching lane and its prompt does reason over heading context (it cites 'same list item, heading'), but it is shadow and inert by default. The surfaced axe link-name lane only checks name presence and cannot do heading-context reasoning. Note: this is the role given in /tmp/sc-tech/2.4.4.json (advisory); the W3C technique mapping treats H80 as sufficient-with-context, but the verdict reflects the same lane reality either way.
techniques.gap: Heading-context purpose verification exists only in the INERT link-purpose rubric; no authoritative or live lane evaluates it.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the link-purpose rubric for 2.4.4 and confirm its prompt incorporates the preceding heading (and aria-labelledby-to-heading patterns) as link context.

techniques.rationale: SCR24 advises using scripted progressive enhancement to open new windows on user request, appending an 'opens in a new window' warning, using device-independent handlers, and falling back to same-window if window.open fails. Same new-window-warning domain as G201 plus a scripting-correctness check. No lane assesses new-window behaviour, the warning, or handler device-independence: no catalog runner, no surfaced axe rule, no rubric clause, no signal-emitting skill. The warning text and target behaviour are runtime-observable on a rendered page (client-side-script IS in domain), so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.
techniques.gap: No detector for scripted new-window links / their advance warning / device-independent activation.
techniques.recommendation: Optional shadow detector for window.open-on-click links lacking an 'opens in new window' warning (shares implementation with the G201 recommendation); device-independence of handlers overlaps the 2.1.1 keyboard-activation runner.

audit_changes.why: Verdict unchanged, but removed the overclaimed lane 'deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff (authoritative,live)'. lib/catalog.js binds ax-state-diff to sc:'4.1.2', not 2.4.4 — it computes an AX name internally but emits no 2.4.4 disposition, so listing it as an authoritative/live 2.4.4 lane falsely implies an authoritative 2.4.4 lane exists. F89 stays CAPTURED purely on the live surfaced axe link-name shadow finding (which I verified carries wcag244 and that 2.4.4 is in AXE_SURFACED_SCS). Added an explicit note that there is NO authoritative 2.4.4 lane.

scs.title: Headings and Labels
scs.summary: SC 2.4.6 is a descriptiveness/clarity criterion for headings (G130) and labels (G131) plus two advisory new-window-warning techniques (G201, SCR24); the only lane touching the core quality is the shadow+inert LLM rubric `heading-descriptive` (sc:2.4.6, covers headings AND labels), with IBM excluded as noise, no axe descriptiveness rule, the authoritative 3.3.2 probe checking only name-presence/visible-match (not clarity), and zero lane for the advisory new-window techniques.

techniques.rationale: G130 Test #2 requires that each heading IDENTIFIES its section — a descriptiveness/meaning judgment, not presence. Confirmed against scripts/v3/llm-rubrics/heading-descriptive-v0.md (sc:2.4.6): the only lane that assesses this is the inert/default-off shadow LLM rubric, which explicitly judges whether 'the headings ... DESCRIBE their topic/purpose' and defers presence/nesting to runners. No authoritative catalog runner judges heading descriptiveness; IBM is explicitly OUT for 2.4.6 (noise); axe has no descriptiveness rule (only empty-heading/heading-order for presence/structure, which is also outside the v3 surface allow-list {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.*}). Because the sole assessing lane is shadow+inert and the skill is guidance-only, PARTIAL is correct.
techniques.gap: No authoritative or live lane assesses whether a heading's text actually identifies its section; the descriptiveness judgment lives only in a default-off shadow LLM rubric that fires nothing by default.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the `heading-descriptive` LLM rubric as a PROVISIONAL fill (opts.runLlm + injected agent), kept shadow/non-authoritative, so heading descriptiveness is scored vs gold rather than untouched.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:3.3.2 field-label-probe (authoritative,live — presence/visible-match only, NOT clarity)
techniques.rationale: G131 Test #2 requires that each label MAKES THE COMPONENT'S PURPOSE CLEAR — a clarity/descriptiveness judgment. The `heading-descriptive` rubric explicitly covers the 'AND form labels' half ('do the headings and form labels DESCRIBE their topic/purpose?') but is shadow+inert. The authoritative 3.3.2 field-label-probe verifies a programmatic name exists and matches a visible label — it does NOT judge whether the label clarifies the control's purpose, so it cannot satisfy this technique and is correctly listed but NOT credited for the clarity condition. axe `label` is presence-only and is not in the v3 surface allow-list anyway. Thus only an inert shadow rubric + guidance skill assess the actual condition → PARTIAL.
techniques.gap: No live/authoritative lane judges label CLARITY/purpose; 3.3.2 only confirms a name exists and matches the visible label, with clarity delegated to the default-off shadow LLM rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the `heading-descriptive` LLM rubric (covers label descriptiveness) as a non-authoritative PROVISIONAL fill so label clarity is scored; do not credit 3.3.2 field-label-probe for this judgment.

techniques.rationale: Advisory technique requiring both an AT-spoken warning AND a visual indication that a control opens a new window/tab (G201 Tests #1 and #2). No lane assesses new-window warnings: no catalog runner pairs target=_blank/window.open with a warning, no surfaced axe rule covers it (axe has none, and the v3 surface allow-list is {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.*}), and no in-scope LLM rubric covers it (heading-descriptive is about heading/label meaning; link-purpose is a different SC and not in this technique set). The harness DOES capture a `newTab: target==='_blank'` flag in drive-page.js's 4.1.2 activation probe, but it is raw navigation metadata never consumed by any 2.4.6/new-window obligation, so it does not constitute a lane. The signal is runtime-observable (target/rel attributes + accessible name text or aria-describedby + a visible cue), but nothing consumes it. G201 is `general` technology about a rendered page → IN domain, so NOT_CAPTURED, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN.
techniques.gap: No detector or rubric assesses whether links/buttons opening new windows carry a programmatic (AT-spoken) + visual 'opens in new window' warning.
techniques.recommendation: Add a shadow detector or LLM rubric: flag elements with target=_blank / scripted window.open and check that the accessible name (or aria-describedby) plus a visible cue convey a new-window warning; the harness already extracts the target=_blank navTo flag in drive-page.js as a starting signal.

techniques.rationale: Advisory client-side-script technique requiring scripted new-window openings to (a) indicate the link opens a new window, (b) use device-independent event handlers, and (c) fall back to same-window if the popup is blocked (SCR24 Test #2). The new-window-indication part is runtime-observable but, like G201, has no lane (no catalog runner, no surfaced axe rule, no in-scope rubric). The device-independent-handler and same-window-fallback parts are JS implementation/authoring details with no discrete runtime signal in this harness. It runs in a rendered web page (not a separate medium like PDF/Flash/SMIL), so NOT_CAPTURED is correct rather than OUT_OF_DOMAIN — the harness simply lacks any mechanism that touches it.
techniques.gap: No lane checks the new-window warning, device-independent event handling, or same-window fallback for scripted popups.
techniques.recommendation: Cover the runtime-observable portion via the same new-window-warning detector/rubric proposed for G201 (flag scripted window.open / target=_blank links lacking a programmatic + visual new-window indication); the device-independent-handler and progressive-enhancement fallback specifics are authoring concerns with no reliable runtime signal.

scs.title: Focus Visible
scs.summary: The AUTHORITATIVE focus-visual-retry runner soundly clears OUTLINE/BORDER/SHADOW-based focus indicators (C45, G149, G165) via real keyboard Tab + dual-channel agreement (computed outline/box-shadow/border signature AND pixel diff), but its computed channel ignores the element's OWN background-color, so background-shift indicators (C15's bg variant, SCR31) hit a channel conflict and only reach inconclusive PARTIAL; it cannot retain-test blur-on-focus (F55) nor compute the contrast/size thresholds (G195, C40) or judge look-alike/occluded indicators (F78), which live only in the shadow/inert rubric and skill.

techniques.rationale: C15 demonstrates two focus-feedback mechanisms: (a) an outline/border change on :focus(-visible), and (b) a change to the element's OWN background-color on :focus (its second/checkbox+input examples). focus-visual-retry soundly clears the OUTLINE/BORDER variant — both its computed signature (which reads outlineStyle/width/offset/color, box-shadow, and per-side border) and its pixel diff fire, agreeing. But the computed channel does NOT read the element's own background-color: readIndicator's bgVisible is gated on `!!pseudo` (pseudo-element backgrounds only), and the base signature string excludes background-color. A pure own-background focus shift therefore changes pixels but leaves the computed signature/anyVisible unchanged → computedFocusDependent=false while pixelChanged=true → conflict=true → usable=false → INCONCLUSIVE (auto-PARTIAL), NOT a confident clear. So C15 is only authoritatively captured for its outline/border form; its background-color form is not soundly cleared.
techniques.gap: The element's own (non-pseudo) background-color focus change — one of C15's two documented mechanisms — is invisible to the runner's computed channel, so it conflicts with the pixel channel and yields inconclusive/PARTIAL rather than a clear. Only the outline/border variant is soundly cleared.
techniques.recommendation: Add the base element's own background-color (alpha-aware) to readIndicator's computed signature/anyVisible so a focus-driven background shift registers on both channels and agrees with the pixel diff; this also fixes SCR31.

techniques.rationale: C45 uses :focus-visible to show a keyboard-only focus indicator (its example draws `outline: 5px solid red`); its test sets focus via Tab/Shift+Tab and verifies a visible indicator appears. focus-visual-retry drives REAL keyboard focus (realKeyboardReach walks the tab ring), the exact path browsers use to trigger :focus-visible, then confirms the outline indicator is present and focus-dependent via both the computed outline signature and the pixel diff (which agree for an outline). This matches the technique's procedure. (Note: the runner does not separately verify that the indicator is SUPPRESSED on pointer focus — the distinguishing :focus-visible behavior — but that suppression is not part of 2.4.7's obligation, which only requires a visible indicator on keyboard focus, so the criterion-relevant condition is captured.)

SCR31 uses onfocus/onblur script to toggle the element's OWN background color or border. The runner is indeed technology-agnostic on the pixel side (it measures the rendered delta regardless of CSS-vs-JS origin). But its dual-channel design requires the computed channel to AGREE: focusDependentIndicator = pixelChanged AND computedFocusDependent. SCR31's documented example (`el.style.backgroundColor = 'yellow'` on focus) changes the element's OWN background-color, which the computed channel does NOT read (bgVisible is pseudo-only; base signature omits background-color) → computedFocusDependent=false, pixelChanged=true → conflict=true → usable=false → INCONCLUSIVE/PARTIAL, not a clear. Only the border-toggle form of SCR31 is soundly cleared (border IS in the computed signature). The canonical background-toggle form the technique is named for is not authoritatively cleared.
techniques.gap: SCR31's primary mechanism — a scripted toggle of the element's own background-color on focus — defeats the runner's dual-channel agreement (computed channel ignores own background) and lands inconclusive rather than cleared. Only the border-toggle variant is captured authoritatively.
techniques.recommendation: Include the base element's own background-color in the computed indicator signature/anyVisible so a focus-driven background change satisfies both channels; until then this is an inert-rubric/skill judgment only for the background variant.

techniques.rationale: G149 relies on the user agent's own highlight of standard controls on focus. focus-visual-retry runs in headless Chromium with default UA styling, so tabbing to a standard control (link/button/input) paints the UA default outline ring, producing a focus-dependent computed-outline signature change AND a pixel delta that agree → cleared. This is the platform-highlight condition the technique addresses. (Edge note: a text field whose only UA indication is the blinking caret is a minor non-outline case, but standard interactive controls receive an outline ring that both channels detect.)

G165 is satisfied by using the platform DEFAULT focus indicator so OS/AT customizations carry over. The runtime-observable substance — a default, focus-dependent visible (outline-ring) indicator present on each control — is exactly what focus-visual-retry confirms with default UA styling via agreeing computed-outline + pixel channels. The native-vs-author-supplied distinction (that being native is what lets OS-level customization carry over) is an authoring-intent property with no distinct runtime signal; the harness verifies the visible-default-indicator condition that underlies it.
techniques.gap: Carry-over of OS/AT focus-indicator customization is not (and cannot be) re-verified at runtime; only that a default, focus-dependent indicator is present is checked. The harness cannot distinguish a native ring from a pixel-identical author-supplied one.
techniques.recommendation: None — the runtime-observable condition (visible default focus indicator) is adequately captured; the native-vs-author distinction is authoring intent with no runtime signal.

techniques.rationale: G195's test procedure adds quantitative checks: indicator area >= a 1 CSS px border (or >= 4 CSS px on the shortest side), AND a >=3:1 contrast change between focused/unfocused states (or >=2px thickness as a fallback). focus-visual-retry CAPTURES the criterion's own bar — a focus-dependent visible indicator is present (it measures ring extent, minThicknessPx, and pixel change). But it does NOT compute the 3:1 contrast-change ratio (spatialStatsInPage hardcodes maxContrastChange:0), the minimum-area threshold, or the 2px fallback — these are Focus Appearance (2.4.11)-style quantitative tests. The shadow/inert LLM rubric explicitly excludes contrast ratios and size, so G195's quantitative checks are unmeasured.
techniques.gap: No lane computes the focus indicator's 3:1 contrast-change ratio, its area threshold, or the 2px-thickness fallback that G195's test procedure requires. The authoritative runner detects presence (and raw thickness), not these quantitative qualities; the rubric explicitly defers contrast/size.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic focus-indicator contrast/size measurement (reuse the 1.4.3 pixel-contrast helper to compute the focused-vs-unfocused contrast change over the indicator ring extent, and a CSS-px thickness/area check) — effectively a 2.4.11-style runner that also strengthens G195/C40 evidence for 2.4.7.

techniques.rationale: C40 builds a two-color (outline+box-shadow) indicator and its test requires: (1) the two indicator colors have >=9:1 contrast with EACH OTHER, (2) each color band is >=2 CSS px thick, (3) the indicator sits over a single solid background at a time. focus-visual-retry detects that a focus-dependent indicator (outline + box-shadow) appears (presence captured), but has NO logic to extract the two indicator colors, compute their 9:1 inter-color contrast, measure per-band 2px thickness, or check single-solid-background placement — exactly the quantitative properties the technique is about (maxContrastChange is hardcoded 0). The LLM rubric explicitly excludes contrast ratios and size.
techniques.gap: No lane measures the 9:1 inter-color contrast of a two-color indicator, the >=2px per-band thickness, or single-solid-background placement. Only indicator presence is authoritatively detected.
techniques.recommendation: Extend a focus-indicator measurement runner (or new 2.4.11-style runner) to sample the indicator ring's two-color composition and compute inter-color contrast + per-band CSS-px thickness; alternatively extend the focus-visible-clear rubric prompt to assess two-color-indicator adequacy as a shadow signal.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:focus-visual-retry (authoritative,live) — collapses to non-focusable/unreachable, no labeled barrier
techniques.rationale: F55 is a failure where script (onFocus=this.blur()) removes focus the instant an element receives it; the failing condition is specifically that focus does NOT REMAIN on the element until the user moves it. No lane tests focus RETENTION. In focus-visual-retry the synthetic targetIsFocusable probe does `el.focus(); activeElement===el; el.blur()` — but onFocus=this.blur() fires synchronously during .focus(), so activeElement!==el and the element reads as simply NON-FOCUSABLE; equivalently realKeyboardReach never stably lands on it (reached=false). BARRIER_OBSERVED requires realKeyboardFocus=true + stableIndicatorAbsence, which is never satisfied, so the runner emits NO labeled barrier — it goes inconclusive/auto-PARTIAL, indistinguishable from a genuinely non-focusable element. The 2.1.1 keyboard-activation lane tests operability/reachability, not whether focus is retained, so it does not detect the F55 condition either. The analyst's own gap note (cannot attribute to scripted blur vs non-focusable) actually negates the CAPTURED claim: the failing condition is not surfaced as a detected failure.
techniques.gap: No lane detects the F55 condition (focus does not remain after the element receives it). Blur-on-focus collapses to 'non-focusable'/'unreachable' with no labeled barrier; 2.1.1 tests operability not retention. The failure is invisible, not merely unattributed.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic focus-retention probe: programmatically focus the target, then on the next frame/microtask check document.activeElement still equals it (and that no blur was forced); a retained=false here is the labeled F55 (blur-on-focus) barrier signal.

techniques.rationale: F78 has three sub-cases. (1) Default indicator turned off (outline:none) with no author replacement — focus-visual-retry CAPTURES this as BARRIER_OBSERVED (stableIndicatorAbsence after real keyboard focus, both channels agreeing on no change). (2) A non-focus outline identical to the focus indicator, making the focused element indistinguishable. (3) A thick same-color border occludes the drawn focus indicator. In (2) and (3) an indicator IS computed/drawn and pixels likely DO change between blur/focus, so the deterministic runner would NOT flag a barrier — it cannot judge visual indistinguishability or occlusion, and has no contrast logic (maxContrastChange:0). The shadow/inert LLM rubric is designed to judge these ('indicator hidden behind/clipped, or change so faint/ambiguous the element is indistinguishable IS a barrier') but is non-authoritative and off by default and excludes contrast ratios. So only the pure-removal sub-case is authoritatively caught.
techniques.gap: The ambiguous-but-present (look-alike outline) and occluded-by-border sub-cases are not authoritatively detected; only the outline:none removal is. The perceivability judgment that catches them lives in a shadow/inert rubric and is not surfaced/gated.
techniques.recommendation: Promote/calibrate the focus-visible-clear-v0 rubric to a surfaced shadow signal for the occluded/ambiguous F78 cases, and/or add a deterministic check that the focus-dependent pixel change is spatially distinct from any always-on border/outline of the same element (border-vs-focus-ring discriminability).

audit_changes.why: The runner's computed channel ignores the element's OWN (non-pseudo) background-color (readIndicator bgVisible is pseudo-only; base signature omits background-color). C15's documented background-shift variant therefore changes pixels but not the computed signature → conflict → usable=false → inconclusive, not a confident clear. Only the outline/border :focus variant is soundly captured.

SCR31's only documented mechanism is a scripted toggle of the element's OWN background-color on focus. The dual-channel runner requires computed AND pixel channels to agree, but the computed channel does not read own background-color → conflict → inconclusive/PARTIAL. 'Technology-agnostic pixel delta' is true but insufficient because the AND-gate with the computed channel fails. Only the border-toggle variant is cleared.

No lane tests focus RETENTION (the F55 failing condition). onFocus=this.blur() makes the synthetic focus probe and real-keyboard reach read the element as non-focusable/unreachable, so BARRIER_OBSERVED (which requires realKeyboardFocus + stableIndicatorAbsence) never fires — the runner emits no labeled barrier and cannot distinguish F55 from a genuinely non-focusable element. 2.1.1 tests operability, not retention. The failure is undetected, not merely unattributed.

scs.title: Section Headings
scs.summary: SC 2.4.10 Section Headings (AAA): both sufficient techniques (G141, H69) address the same semantic-structure condition — each logical content/navigational section begins with a properly nested heading — for which v3 has NO catalog runner, NO surfaced/capable axe rule, and NO LLM rubric; the only lane is the guidance-only page-structure skill (names 2.4.10 in scope, emits no signal), so both are PARTIAL / GUIDANCE_ONLY.

techniques.rationale: G141's test procedure is narrow and verified by reading the technique HTML: 'Examine a page with content organized into sections; check that a heading for each section exists.' Verifying this requires (a) determining the page's logical content sections and (b) confirming each has a heading marking its start — plus the descriptive guidance to nest levels (h1>h2>h3). This is a semantic structure/meaning judgment, runtime-observable on a rendered page (IN domain). Confirmed against the codebase: grep of scripts/v3 for 2.4.10/section-heading returns nothing, so no AUTHORITATIVE catalog runner exists. No axe rule is surfaced or even capable of the section-to-heading COVERAGE judgment — axe's heading-order/empty-heading rules check heading validity/order (serving 1.3.1), not 'every section has a heading', and 2.4.10 is not in the axe-surface allow-list {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.x} anyway. No LLM rubric exists for 2.4.10: the rubric dir has none for it, and heading-descriptive-v0.md is sc:2.4.6 and explicitly disclaims presence ('missing heading is 1.3.1/3.3.2, not here'). (Note: a 2.4.10 string in scripts/add-findings-to-samples.js is a dataset gold-label annotation for an empty-heading sample, not a v3 lane.) The sole lane is the guidance-only skills/page-structure.md, whose wcag: frontmatter lists '2.4.10 Section Headings (AAA)' in scope; it shapes a human/LLM judge's reasoning but emits no automated signal. Guidance-only touching the SC = PARTIAL.
techniques.gap: No automated lane determines the page's logical content sections and verifies each begins with a heading; heading nesting/hierarchy is also unchecked. Only a guidance doc that emits no signal addresses it — no pass/fail and no shadow finding for this technique.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 2.4.10 LLM rubric (section-headings: do the visually/semantically distinct content sections each begin with a heading, are heading levels hierarchically nested), fed by the heading outline + section/landmark map the collector already extracts; optionally add a deterministic shadow triage that maps detected sections/landmarks to headings and flags sections lacking a leading heading (review-only, uncalibrated). Keep both non-authoritative given AAA and the meaning judgment.

techniques.rationale: H69 uses HTML heading elements to convey structure: indicate start of main content, mark up section headings within main content, demarcate navigational sections (top/main/secondary/footer nav), and let users jump by section — with the same nest-levels-hierarchically guidance as G141. Its 2.4.10 test is the section-coverage check: content divided into sections AND each section starts with a heading. This is runtime-observable on a rendered HTML page (IN domain — not OUT_OF_DOMAIN). Confirmed in the codebase that v3 has no lane performing it: no catalog runner for 2.4.10 (grep empty), no surfaced/capable axe rule for 'each section starts with a heading' (axe serves heading validity/order under 1.3.1; 2.4.10 not in the surface allow-list), and no LLM rubric for 2.4.10 (heading-descriptive-v0 is sc:2.4.6 descriptiveness, not section coverage). The only lane is the guidance-only page-structure skill, which names 2.4.10 in its wcag: frontmatter scope but emits no signal. Hence PARTIAL (guidance-only). H69's prose also references navigation/skip-block use, which overlaps 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks — a separate SC; only the section/heading checks count for 2.4.10.
techniques.gap: No automated detector verifies that each content/navigational region begins with a heading element; heading-level nesting is also unchecked. Guidance-only coverage with no emitted signal — no pass/fail and no shadow finding for this technique.
techniques.recommendation: Author a 2.4.10 section-headings LLM rubric (shadow) judging whether each distinct content and navigational region begins with a heading and whether levels are nested, using the collector's heading outline + landmark/region map; optionally a deterministic shadow triage flagging landmark/section regions lacking a leading heading (uncalibrated, review-only). Keep non-authoritative (AAA, meaning judgment).

audit_changes.why: Verdict and lanes upheld after codebase verification (no runner, no surfaced/capable axe, no rubric; only guidance-only page-structure skill which names 2.4.10 in its wcag: frontmatter). Rationale tightened only to clarify that the 2.4.10 string in scripts/add-findings-to-samples.js is a dataset gold-label annotation for an empty-heading sample, not a v3 detector lane — so it does not constitute coverage. No verdict change.

Verdict and lanes upheld after verification. Confirmed IN domain (HTML rendered-page technique, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN), no authoritative/axe/rubric lane, only guidance-only skill. Rationale unchanged in substance. No verdict change.

scs.title: Error Identification
scs.summary: SC 3.3.1's only authoritative lane is the catalog form-error-probe, which is barrier-only (it detects when an invalid submit surfaces NO error message of any channel and reads aria-invalid/describedby/live-region only as part of that absence test); every affirmative quality requirement (error in TEXT, identifies the field, programmatic association, alertdialog/aria-invalid correctness) sits in the inert 3.3.1 rubric and guidance skill, the 4.1.3 status-detector does NOT apply (it skips form-submit triggers), and axe's aria-* rules run but are dropped (not surfaced) by v3.

techniques.rationale: Advisory technique: enhance the programmatic indication that a visually-required field is mandatory via aria-required (so AT announces required-ness up front). It is conceptually a 3.3.2 labels/instructions concern that supports 3.3.1 by making required-ness machine-determinable. No authoritative lane verifies that visually-required fields carry aria-required=true (or native required) matching the visual cue: the catalog field-label-probe checks programmatic name + visible label only and does NOT assert aria-required (so I removed it from the lane set to avoid implying authoritative coverage); the 4.1.2 ax-state-diff is a CLOSED state set {expanded,pressed,checked,selected} that does not include aria-required and diffs state on control activation, not required-ness. The form-error-probe READS aria-required (exp-runners.js:435) but only as a constraint trigger, never to verify it matches a visual indicator. axe's aria-required rules exist and run but 3.3.x is outside the v3 surface allow-list {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.*}, so they are dropped. The 3.3.1 rubric and forms skill can only reason about required-field indication as inert/guidance — and the rubric's C2 caveat explicitly forbids inferring failure from a missing aria-required/aria-invalid, so it does not affirmatively assess this either.
techniques.gap: No authoritative or live signal verifies that visually-required fields carry aria-required=true (or native required) value-correct vs the visual cue. The axe capability that would cover it (aria-required-attr) runs but is not surfaced by v3.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic detector: for each field with a visual required cue (asterisk in label, '(required)' text), assert aria-required=true / native required present and value-correct; alternatively surface axe's aria-required-attr findings into v3, or extend the 3.3.2 rubric to flag required fields lacking programmatic required state. Advisory — a shadow/triage signal suffices.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: role=alertdialog modal on input error, requiring an accessible name, focus moved into the dialog, constrained tab order, focus restoration on dismiss, and contents that identify the error. The catalog form-error-probe authoritatively catches the gross-absence BARRIER — an alertdialog that surfaces error text on invalid submit registers as a newly-surfaced, error-associated message (role=alert/status, error-styled markup, or inside the form), so 'no error surface at all' is caught. None of the alertdialog-specific qualities (accessible name present, focus moves to a focusable element, tab order constrained, focus restored) are verified by any authoritative lane for 3.3.1; those mechanics belong to 2.1.2/focus-management. The 'contents identify the error' part is judged only by the inert 3.3.1 rubric. I removed the status-detector lane the analyst did not list here anyway; for the record status-detector would not apply because it skips submit triggers.
techniques.gap: No live verification that the alertdialog has an accessible name, receives/constrains/restores focus, and whose text identifies the error; the error-text-quality part lives only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric.
techniques.recommendation: Run the LLM 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live (it covers 'error identified in text'); for the dialog mechanics lean on the form-error-probe (presence) plus the focus-management instruments, and extend the rubric prompt to note alertdialog name/focus expectations.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: inject error text into a pre-existing role=alert / aria-live container so AT announces it without focus moving. The catalog form-error-probe is the only relevant authoritative lane: it detects total absence of an error surface (BARRIER), and a submit-time live-region injection IS recognized by its isLiveRegion() association test, so the worst case is covered. The analyst's claim that the 4.1.3 status-detector 'is exactly the case it is designed for' and 'could observe' the injection is an OVERCLAIM: status-detector (status-detector.js PASS 1) deliberately EXCLUDES submit/reset/image buttons and default-submit buttons inside a form (isSafe()), and is wired only to 4.1.3 in run-instruments.js — so it never clicks the submit that triggers ARIA19's injection and cannot observe it. I removed the status-detector lane and its recommendation. No authoritative lane verifies the role=alert/aria-live container is present at load and that the injected text identifies the error; that quality lives only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric.
techniques.gap: Presence-at-load of the live container and text-identifies-error are not authoritatively verified; the text-quality judgment is only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric. The 4.1.3 status-detector does NOT apply (it skips submit triggers).
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live to judge the injected error text; add a deterministic check that an empty role=alert/aria-live container exists at page load before submit and is populated with error-associated text on invalid submit. Do NOT rely on status-detector here — it does not fire on form submission.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: set aria-invalid=true on fields that fail validation, tie an error message via aria-describedby, require aria-invalid false/absent when valid and true when invalid, and the associated text gives enough info to understand the error. The catalog form-error-probe catches the gross-absence BARRIER and its association test recognizes aria-invalid=true + aria-describedby-referenced messages as error identification (so absence is covered), but it does NOT affirmatively verify the true/false flip is correct. The 4.1.2 ax-state-diff is correctly disqualified by the analyst's own rationale: its closed state set {expanded,pressed,checked,selected} does not include aria-invalid and it diffs on control activation, not submit-time validity — so I removed it from the lane set (listing an authoritative runner that provably does not touch aria-invalid overstates coverage). The describedby text-quality judgment is only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric. axe's aria-valid-attr-value runs but 3.3.x is dropped by the v3 surface allow-list.
techniques.gap: No live check that aria-invalid flips correctly on validation and that aria-describedby resolves to text that identifies the problem; the text-quality judgment is only in the inert rubric. axe's relevant rule runs but is not surfaced.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic detector for aria-invalid=true + resolvable aria-describedby on post-submit invalid fields (and aria-invalid false/absent when valid), and run the 3.3.1 rubric live to judge the described error text. Optionally add 3.3.x to the axe surface allow-list to consume aria-valid-attr-value findings.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: when a mandatory field is left blank and submitted, a TEXT description identifies which required field(s) were omitted (and previously entered data is re-displayed). The catalog form-error-probe is barrier-only: it confirms an error surface appears on invalid submit (a blank required field is exactly its required-constraint path), authoritatively catching the failure where NO text description is provided. It cannot affirm the description is in TEXT, names the specific omitted field, or that prior data is re-displayed; those quality judgments live in the calibrated-but-inert 3.3.1 rubric. Worst-case absence captured; the substance is PARTIAL.
techniques.gap: No live lane verifies the message is textual and names the specific omitted required field, nor that prior input is preserved; the substantive check is in the inert rubric only.
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live so the text-identifies-which-field quality is judged; the form-error-probe already covers the no-message barrier. Re-display-of-data is largely out of practical single-submit runtime scope — note as advisory.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: when input is not in the allowed set of values, provide a TEXT description of the error (an asterisk or red label is NOT sufficient). The catalog form-error-probe authoritatively catches the barrier where invalid input produces no error surface at all. The heart of the technique — error conveyed IN TEXT (not color-only) describing the allowed-values problem — is precisely what the 3.3.1 rubric judges ('error identified in TEXT with direction, not color-only/silent'), but that rubric is inert by default and the runner deliberately dropped colour as a normative signal (it cannot affirm text vs red-only). PARTIAL.
techniques.gap: The color-only vs text distinction and the allowed-values description quality are only assessable by the inert 3.3.1 rubric; no authoritative lane makes that judgment.
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live (purpose-built for the 'in text, not color-only' requirement of G84); form-error-probe covers the silent-failure barrier.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: when input falls outside the required format/values, provide a TEXT description identifying the field in error and describing the nature of the invalid entry (the how-to-fix part overlaps 3.3.3). For 3.3.1 the catalog form-error-probe authoritatively catches the barrier of no error surface on bad-format submit (pattern/type/email constraints are in its hasConstraint set). Whether the description is in text and identifies the offending field is judged by the inert 3.3.1 rubric (and the fix suggestion by the inert 3.3.3 rubric). No authoritative lane verifies text-content quality.
techniques.gap: Text-identifies-field-and-nature-of-error is only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric (fix suggestion in the inert 3.3.3 rubric); not authoritatively verified.
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live; the form-error-probe already covers the absent-message barrier. Defer the correction-suggestion portion to the 3.3.3 lane.

techniques.rationale: Advisory technique: provide a MECHANISM letting users jump to errors — a text summary at the top that LINKS to each errored field, plus a return link. This is a navigation affordance over the error list, not error identification itself. No lane assesses whether error messages contain in-page anchor links to the corresponding fields and a return link: form-error-probe only checks that some error surface exists (and its summary-link referencesField() test merely confirms association for the barrier decision, it does not affirm the jump-to-error affordance is present/correct); the 3.3.1 rubric judges text-and-direction, not anchor presence; order-check/kbd-graph cover tab/reading order, not error-to-field linking. No axe rule, catalog runner, or rubric covers the jump-to-error mechanism. NOT_CAPTURED is correct.
techniques.gap: Nothing detects whether error messages provide in-page links to the offending fields and a return link to the error summary.
techniques.recommendation: Add a detector (or extend the 3.3.1 rubric prompt) to check that after a multi-error submit the error summary contains anchors (href=#fieldId) resolving to the invalid fields and a return link. Advisory — a shadow/triage signal suffices.

techniques.rationale: Advisory technique: provide explicit SUCCESS feedback on successful submission (e.g. 'You have successfully logged in'). This is the no-error inverse of error identification. The catalog form-error-probe fires only on INVALID submit (barrier-only for the error case) and never exercises the valid-submission/success path; the 4.1.3 status-detector is opt-in, insertion-only, mapped to 4.1.3 not this advisory practice, and additionally skips submit triggers; the 3.3.1 rubric is about error text, not success text. No lane assesses presence/clarity of success feedback. NOT_CAPTURED is correct.
techniques.gap: No lane verifies a successful submission yields explicit success feedback; this requires submitting VALID data (a flow the harness does not exercise) and observing a confirmation message.
techniques.recommendation: Out of typical scope for a single-page barrier scan; if pursued, add a valid-submit flow that checks for an inserted/announced success message. Note status-detector cannot reuse here as-is because it skips submit triggers. Advisory — low priority.

techniques.rationale: Targets required form controls in tagged PDF documents (the /Ff flag in the form field dictionary, Acrobat Pro authoring, document accessibility API). The harness assesses rendered web pages at runtime and does not author or assess PDFs. Conceptually parallels ARIA2 (indicating required fields) but the medium and /Ff/PDF-API verification are entirely outside a web-page-at-runtime harness. OUT_OF_DOMAIN is correct.

Targets format/value validation alerts in tagged PDF forms (Acrobat Pro format masks, PDF JavaScript app.alert). The harness does not author or assess PDFs. Conceptually parallels SCR18/G85 but the PDF medium and Acrobat tooling are outside the runtime web-page scope. OUT_OF_DOMAIN is correct.

Sufficient technique: client-side validation that, on invalid input, surfaces an alert dialog (or page message) describing the error in text. The catalog form-error-probe exercises this path — it makes the field invalid, fires input/change/blur, and clicks submit — so it authoritatively catches the barrier where the DOM-message variant produces no error description. The text-describes-the-error quality is judged by the inert 3.3.1 rubric. Verified caveat: exp-runners.js registers NO page.on('dialog') handler, so a native window.alert() raised by SCR18's onchange/onsubmit handler is auto-dismissed by Puppeteer and leaves no DOM surface — alert()-based SCR18 implementations escape the probe entirely. So absence is captured for the DOM-message variant only, and the text quality is PARTIAL via the inert rubric.
techniques.gap: The error-text-describes-the-error judgment is only in the inert rubric; native window.alert() dialogs are NOT observable by the form-error-probe (no dialog handler), so alert-based SCR18 escapes detection.
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live; add a page.on('dialog') handler to the form-error-probe so native window.alert()/confirm() validation messages are recorded (and their text passed to the rubric) instead of being silently auto-dismissed.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique: client-side validation inserts a TEXT error list (anchor links to fields) into the DOM above the form on submit and moves focus to it. The catalog form-error-probe authoritatively catches the barrier (invalid submit, no error surface inserted) — a newly-inserted error block inside the form / error-styled / with summary anchors referencing the field registers via its before/after diff and association test. The analyst's claim that the 4.1.3 status-detector is 'purpose-built to detect exactly what SCR32 does' and 'would observe the inserted error block' is an OVERCLAIM: status-detector (status-detector.js isSafe()) deliberately EXCLUDES submit buttons and default-submit buttons inside a form, and is wired only to 4.1.3 — SCR32's error list is inserted by the SUBMIT handler, which status-detector never triggers, so it cannot observe it. I removed the status-detector lane and recommendation. The focus-moves-to-errors behavior overlaps focus-management lanes. The text-identifies-each-errored-field quality lives only in the inert 3.3.1 rubric.
techniques.gap: No authoritative verification that the DOM-inserted error list is textual and identifies each invalid field; that quality is in the inert 3.3.1 rubric only. The 4.1.3 status-detector does NOT apply (it skips submit triggers).
techniques.recommendation: Run the 3.3.1 error-identification rubric live to judge the inserted error text; the form-error-probe already covers the no-insertion barrier and recognizes the inserted error block. Do NOT wire status-detector for this — it does not fire on form submission. If a focus-moves-to-errors signal is wanted, use the focus-management instruments after submit.

audit_changes.why: Verdict unchanged, but the analyst's rationale, lanes, and recommendation overclaimed the 4.1.3 status-detector as 'exactly the case it is designed for'. status-detector.js (isSafe()) deliberately excludes submit/default-submit triggers and is wired only to 4.1.3, so it never clicks the submit that injects ARIA19's live-region error and cannot observe it. Removed the status-detector lane and the 'wire status-detector for 3.3.1' recommendation; corrected the gap/recommendation.
