SCR32 inserts its error list from the SUBMIT handler; status-detector skips submit triggers (isSafe()) and is 4.1.3-only, so it cannot observe the insertion. Removed the status-detector lane and the 'wire status-detector as a shadow cross-signal for 3.3.1' recommendation.

Verdict unchanged, but removed the misleading 'deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live)' lane — its own rationale admits the probe does not assert aria-required, so listing an authoritative runner overstates coverage. Replaced with the honest 'axe:aria-required-attr (capable,NOT-surfaced)' lane (3.3.x is outside the v3 surface allow-list) and added that the rubric's C2 caveat forbids inferring failure from missing aria-required, so even the inert rubric does not affirmatively assess it.

Verdict unchanged, but removed the 'deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff (authoritative,live)' lane: ax-state-diff's closed state set is {expanded,pressed,checked,selected} (does NOT include aria-invalid) and it diffs on control activation, not submit-time validity — the analyst's own rationale disqualifies it, so listing an authoritative runner overstates coverage. Added the honest 'axe:aria-valid-attr-value (capable,NOT-surfaced)' lane.

scs.title: Labels or Instructions
scs.summary: 3.3.2's per-field visible-label-presence core (H44) is genuinely AUTHORITATIVE via the catalog field-label-probe; descriptiveness (G131) and the adjacent-button pattern (G167) are PARTIAL (authoritative presence + inert rubric for the quality judgment); and everything group-level or behavioral — F82 and H71 (missing group label), ARIA2 (aria-required vs visual cue), G13 (change-of-context warning) — is NOT_CAPTURED, since the per-field probe is structurally blind to groups, no surfaced axe rule applies (3.3.2 is outside the allow-list), and the only touching rubric is inert and not framed for those cases; PDF10 is out of domain.

techniques.rationale: Advisory: a field shown via presentation to be required should also carry aria-required=true so AT can announce the required state. The authoritative field-label-probe (verified measureFieldLabel, exp-runners.js) only computes accessible NAME + visibleLabelText + nearbyVisibleText; it never reads aria-required and has no notion of a visual required cue. The 4.1.2 ax-state-diff runner tracks name/role/state on ACTIVATION (a closed ARIA set centered on activation diffs), not the static required property of a non-activated input. axe-core does run aria-required-attr/children/parent, but those check ARIA attribute VALIDITY / required owned children — not whether a visually-required field declares aria-required at all — and axe is not surfaced for 3.3.2 (outside the {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.*} allow-list) regardless. The 3.3.2 LLM rubric is framed for label-vs-visible-label agreement, not required-state. No lane assesses presence/correctness of aria-required against the field's visual required cue.
techniques.gap: No lane detects that a field shown visually as required (asterisk, '(required)', red border/star icon) carries a matching aria-required=true. Detecting the VISUAL required cue and comparing it to the programmatic aria-required state is unaddressed.
techniques.recommendation: Add a shadow detector (or extend the field-label rubric) that flags visually-required fields lacking aria-required/required, using the element crop + DOM (asterisk/'required' text near the label vs the aria-required attribute). Advisory, so a non-authoritative cross-signal is sufficient.

lanes: llm-rubric:field-label-v0 (shadow,inert — NOT framed for group identification)
deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — per-field, structurally blind to the group; nearbyVisibleText registers the '(' ')' '-' punctuation so it never fires here)
techniques.rationale: The failure fires when a set of fields visually formatted as one phone number has NO group text label AND no instructions — each field IS trivially 'labeled' by adjacent punctuation. The authoritative field-label-probe is verified per-field: its nearbyVisibleText flag (exp-runners.js l.392-398) registers ANY sibling text node, including the '(' ')' '-' punctuation, so it does NOT even fire a barrier here — it is not merely incomplete, it actively passes the trap case. There is no group/fieldset detector anywhere in scripts/v3/lib, and no surfaced axe rule (3.3.2 is outside the allow-list). The only remaining lane is the 3.3.2 rubric, which is INERT by default AND, per field-label-v0.md, framed for per-field label-vs-visible agreement, NOT for missing group-level identification. With no authoritative, no live, no surfaced-axe, no calibrated-instrument lane and only an inert-and-unframed rubric, the link to F82's defining failure is tangential — NOT_CAPTURED (analyst overclaimed PARTIAL).
techniques.gap: The defining failure — a related field set with no group/aggregate label and no instructions, even though each field has a trivial per-field punctuation label — is detected by NO lane: the per-field probe is structurally blind (and passes the trap), and the rubric is inert and not framed for groups.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic group-label heuristic (detect a logically-grouped field set such as a phone-number triplet and check for a nearby group label / instructions) as a shadow detector, AND extend the 3.3.2 rubric prompt to flag related field groups lacking a group label, feeding it the group geometry; enable the rubric lane (runLlm) for it to fire.

techniques.rationale: Advisory: provide an instruction, ahead of a control in reading order, describing that changing the control's setting will cause a change of context (e.g. an onchange language-select that navigates). No catalog runner models 'changing this control causes a change of context'; the field-label-probe only checks label/instruction PRESENCE for identification, not whether a change-of-context warning exists or precedes the control. No 3.3.2 rubric covers change-of-context warnings, no surfaced axe rule applies, and the order-check/kbd-graph instruments only assess reading/tab-order divergence, not instruction semantics or control behavior.
techniques.gap: No lane detects controls that trigger a change of context on setting change, nor verifies that a preceding instruction warns the user about it.
techniques.recommendation: New (shadow) detector/rubric: identify controls with change-of-context-on-change behavior (e.g. inline onchange navigation/submit) and judge whether a preceding instruction warns the user. Advisory, so cross-signal scoring suffices.

techniques.rationale: Sufficient technique = the label makes the component's PURPOSE clear (Tests: 'check that each label makes the component's purpose clear') — a quality/descriptiveness judgment. The authoritative field-label-probe verifies a label/name is PRESENT and visible (necessary but not sufficient); it cannot judge whether 'field'/'input'/a placeholder-as-label actually conveys purpose. That descriptiveness judgment IS the genuine focus of the 3.3.2 LLM rubric (field-label-v0.md explicitly flags generic-name/placeholder-as-label), which is shadow and INERT by default. So presence is authoritatively captured but the descriptiveness the technique is about is only PARTIAL.
techniques.gap: Whether the present label is genuinely descriptive of purpose is judged only by the inert LLM rubric and the guidance skill; no live/authoritative lane assesses descriptiveness.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the field-label rubric lane (runLlm + injected agent) so the descriptiveness judgment runs as a PROVISIONAL fill on the auto-PARTIAL; keep the catalog probe for presence.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — partial: nearby button text + accessible name)
techniques.rationale: Technique: an adjacent button with a clear name (e.g. 'Search', or an icon button with an accessible name) acts as the field's label; Tests require (1) field+button adjacent in reading order, (2) adjacent in visual rendering, (3) button has an accessible name when no visible text. The field-label-probe partially helps and is genuinely live/authoritative: nearbyVisibleText would register the adjacent button's visible text (averting a barrier) and the probe resolves accessible names — so the labeling-presence aspect is touched. But it does NOT model the field-button pairing nor verify reading-order-vs-visual-order adjacency between them; the order-check/vsr instruments handle generic order divergence, not this pairing. The inert rubric could reason that a button labels the field but is off by default and not framed for the pairing. PARTIAL stands.
techniques.gap: No lane verifies the specific field+adjacent-button labeling relationship as a unit (programmatic-reading-order adjacency AND visual adjacency AND the button's accessible name).
techniques.recommendation: Extend the 3.3.2 rubric (and/or add a detector) to recognize the adjacent-button-as-label pattern and confirm the button's accessible name plus reading/visual adjacency; enable the rubric lane.

techniques.rationale: Technique: associate a label element (for/id or wrapping) with the control AND, specifically for 3.3.2, the label must be VISIBLE. The field-label-probe directly implements this (verified measureFieldLabel): it resolves the accessible name including label[for] (l.378) and wrapping label (l.379), records the visible-label node, computes srOnly() to confirm visibility (visibleLabelText, l.386), and asserts fieldLabelBarrier only when a user-input field has no name AND no visible label AND no nearby visible text (l.404). This is precisely H44's 3.3.2 condition (visible associated label present), authoritatively and live. Adequacy/descriptiveness is a separate concern (G131); the probe also treats an unassociated-but-visible label as inconclusive rather than a barrier, consistent with 3.3.2 not requiring programmatic association — so the visible-label presence the technique hinges on is captured.

lanes: llm-rubric:field-label-v0 (shadow,inert — NOT framed for group description)
deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe (authoritative,live — per-field only, no group concept)
techniques.rationale: Technique: provide a GROUP-level description for logically related controls (radios/checkboxes/address fields) via fieldset + a first-child legend. The authoritative field-label-probe operates per individual field and verifies per-field labels only — there is NO fieldset/legend/group-label concept anywhere in scripts/v3/lib (the lone fieldset reference in exp-runners.js is an unrelated disabled-context check). axe is not surfaced for 3.3.2 (outside the allow-list), and fieldset/legend presence is not in the surface list anyway. The 3.3.2 rubric is inert AND (per field-label-v0.md) framed for per-field label agreement, not group description — the analyst itself notes it 'is not framed for it.' So the credited PARTIAL rests entirely on a tangential, inert, unframed lane with no authoritative/live backing → NOT_CAPTURED (analyst overclaimed PARTIAL).
techniques.gap: No lane verifies that logically-grouped controls needing a collective description are wrapped in a fieldset with a descriptive legend (or an equivalent role=group + aria-label/aria-labelledby). Group-level labeling is unassessed by any authoritative or live lane.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic group-label check (fieldset>legend / role=group+aria-label for related radio/checkbox/address sets) as a shadow detector, AND extend the 3.3.2 rubric prompt to flag related field groups lacking a group description; enable the rubric lane for it to fire.

techniques.rationale: Technique targets tagged PDF documents: providing programmatically-associated labels for PDF form fields via the field dictionary TU (tooltip) entry, verified with Adobe Acrobat Pro or a PDF accessibility-API tool. The v3 harness assesses RENDERED WEB PAGES at runtime and explicitly does not author or assess PDFs. Conceptually parallel to H44/G131 (programmatically-associated field labels), but the medium, attributes (/TU entry, /FT Tx), and tooling (Acrobat) are entirely outside a runtime web-page harness.

audit_changes.why: The only non-guidance lane the analyst credited is the 3.3.2 LLM rubric, which is INERT by default AND, per the rubric file (field-label-v0.md), framed for label-vs-visible-label AGREEMENT and per-field descriptiveness — NOT for missing GROUP identification of a related field set. The authoritative field-label-probe is verified per-field (measureFieldLabel) and its nearbyVisibleText flag registers ANY sibling text node — including the punctuation '(' ')' '-' that F82 hinges on — so it never fires a barrier here and has no group concept at all. There is no group/fieldset detector anywhere in scripts/v3/lib and no surfaced axe rule (3.3.2 is outside the {1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4,3.1.*} allow-list). With no authoritative, no live, no surfaced-axe, no calibrated-instrument lane and only an inert-and-unframed rubric, the link to F82's defining failure is tangential → NOT_CAPTURED.

Identical structural overclaim. H71 is purely group-level (fieldset+legend / role=group description for related radios/checkboxes/address fields). The authoritative field-label-probe is per-field with no group concept (verified: only fieldset mention in exp-runners.js is an unrelated disabled-context check), there is no group-label detector in v3 lib, and 3.3.2 is not in the axe surface allow-list. The 3.3.2 rubric is inert and (per field-label-v0.md) not framed for group description. Analyst itself wrote 'is not framed for it' — so the credited PARTIAL rests entirely on a tangential, inert, unframed lane → NOT_CAPTURED.

scs.title: Error Suggestion
scs.summary: SC 3.3.3 (Error Suggestion) has NO authoritative lane: only the inert, shadow LLM rubric `3.3.3 error-suggestion` can judge whether a correction is suggested; the authoritative catalog `form-error-probe` is an SC 3.3.1 barrier-only runner (cross-signal for 3.3.3, never authoritative for it), so suggestion-content sufficient/advisory techniques are PARTIAL, jump-to-error/success-feedback advisory techniques are NOT_CAPTURED, and the PDF technique is OUT_OF_DOMAIN.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
techniques.rationale: ARIA18's 3.3.3-specific obligation is test #7: the alertdialog contents must SUGGEST how to fix the error (identification is test #6, a 3.3.1 concern). Judging suggestion content is a meaning judgment only the inert, shadow error-suggestion rubric can make; it is non-authoritative and OFF by default (opts.runLlm). The form-error-probe is the SC 3.3.1 authoritative barrier-only runner (catalog.js: sc:'3.3.1', barrier-only, never clears) so for 3.3.3 it is at most a cross-signal confirming an error surface exists, NOT an authoritative 3.3.3 lane. The dialog's structural obligations belong to other SCs. Verified: vision-capture.js maps '3.3.3':'submit' and unions only the FORM-region rect, so a centered/top-layer alertdialog may fall outside the captured clip.
techniques.gap: No authoritative or live signal verifies that the alertdialog contents include a correction suggestion; the error-suggestion rubric that could judge it is inert (opts.runLlm) and non-authoritative. The submit-state capture is form-region-bounded, so a modal alertdialog rendered outside the form rect may not even be in the evidence the rubric sees.
techniques.recommendation: Enable the 3.3.3 error-suggestion rubric (opts.runLlm) for forms with detected error surfaces; in vision-capture.js extend the submit-state clip to also union any visible role=alertdialog / top-layer <dialog> rect (currently form-region-only) so the rubric receives the dialog text; extend the rubric prompt to read alertdialog content.

lanes: llm-rubric:3.3.1 error-identification (shadow,inert; covers the in-text portion)
deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
techniques.rationale: G84's test procedure is narrow (#2: 'check that information is provided IN TEXT about the problem') so it is largely error identification (a 3.3.1 overlap), with the 'list allowed values / suggest most similar' obligation living in the Description. The suggestion-content judgment is the error-suggestion rubric's remit (shadow, inert, non-authoritative); the in-text identification overlaps the error-identification rubric (also inert). The form-error-probe is the SC 3.3.1 authoritative barrier-only runner, not an authoritative 3.3.3 lane; it only confirms some error surface exists. No authoritative/live lane parses whether allowed values are described.
techniques.gap: Whether the error text actually lists/suggests allowed values is judged only by the inert, non-authoritative error-suggestion rubric; no authoritative or live lane verifies it.
techniques.recommendation: Enable opts.runLlm so the 3.3.3 error-suggestion rubric fills the auto-PARTIAL slot as a PROVISIONAL row; confirm its prompt explicitly checks for listing/closest-match of allowed values.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
techniques.rationale: G85 test #2 requires a text description that identifies the field + nature + how to fix (example / describe / show similar values); the 'how to correct' content is exactly the error-suggestion rubric's remit (shadow, inert, non-authoritative). The form-error-probe is the SC 3.3.1 authoritative barrier-only runner so for 3.3.3 only a cross-signal confirming an error surface exists; it cannot tell whether the text explains the correct format. Test #3 (re-display previously entered data) is assessed by NO lane.
techniques.gap: The presence and adequacy of a correction example/description is judged only by the inert error-suggestion rubric; the re-display-of-entered-data check (test #3) has no lane at all.
techniques.recommendation: Enable opts.runLlm for the 3.3.3 error-suggestion rubric; if test #3 (data re-display) is in scope, add a deterministic check that field values persist after an invalid submit round-trip (the submit-state capture in vision-capture.js already round-trips the form and could surface persisted values).

techniques.rationale: G139 is a navigation MECHANISM technique: provide a link from each error message to the field in error (and a link from the error back to the error list). The quality it promotes is jump-to-error linkage, not textual suggestion content. No lane assesses the presence/operability of in-page links from error messages to their corresponding fields: the error-suggestion rubric judges suggestion text not link targets; the order-check/kbd-graph instruments assess tab/reading order not error-link wiring; the form-error-probe (SC 3.3.1) is barrier-only. The skill forms-instructions-errors is guidance-only.
techniques.gap: No detector or rubric checks that error messages contain working links to the offending fields (and back to the error list). This whole mechanism is uncovered.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic check (post-invalid-submit, reusing the vision-capture submit transition) that the inserted error summary contains in-page anchors whose href fragments resolve to the invalid field elements (and a back-link to the error list); optionally an LLM rubric prompt for 'links to errors'.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
techniques.rationale: G177 is the canonical 3.3.3 technique: provide suggested CORRECTION TEXT (correct spelling / similar values from a known pool) placed near the field or linked close to it. The error-suggestion rubric is built for exactly this judgment (is a correction suggested, is it near the field) but is shadow and inert by default (non-authoritative). The form-error-probe is the SC 3.3.1 authoritative barrier-only runner; for 3.3.3 it only confirms an error surface exists, not that a correction is suggested. Proximity/placement (test #4) is partly judgeable by the rubric from layout context but by no deterministic lane.
techniques.gap: The presence of suggested correction text and its placement near the field is judged only by the inert, non-authoritative error-suggestion rubric; no authoritative/live lane verifies it.
techniques.recommendation: Enable opts.runLlm so the 3.3.3 error-suggestion rubric runs and fills the auto-PARTIAL slot; ensure its prompt covers correction-text presence AND proximity-to-field placement.

techniques.rationale: G199 promotes SUCCESS feedback after a successful (error-free) submission, the inverse of error handling. No input error is present, so neither the error-suggestion rubric nor the form-error-probe applies (vision-capture.js drives an INVALID submit only; the catalog probe exercises the invalid path). The status-detector instrument (4.1.3) could in principle observe a newly inserted success message, but it is opt-in/insertion-only, emits SC 4.1.3 findings (confirmed in status-detector.js), and does not judge that the inserted text CONFIRMS success. No rubric exists for success-feedback adequacy.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses whether a successful submission produces an explicit success-confirmation message. The success path is not exercised (the catalog probe and submit-state capture only do the invalid-submit path) and no rubric judges success-feedback content.
techniques.recommendation: Add a success-path probe (valid submit) plus an LLM rubric prompt judging whether an explicit success-confirmation message is surfaced; treat as advisory shadow signal.

techniques.rationale: PDF22 concerns required-format validation and error alerts in tagged PDF forms (e.g., Acrobat field format validation / app.alert JavaScript). This harness assesses rendered web pages at runtime and does not author or assess PDFs. Conceptually it is the PDF analogue of SCR18/G85 (alert describing a format error), but it has no runtime-observable signal in a web-page harness.
techniques.recommendation: None, out of domain (PDF authoring/validation).

lanes: deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
techniques.rationale: SCR18 describes client-side validation that, on invalid input, produces an alert dialog describing the NATURE of the error in text. Whether that text describes the error and points toward a fix is a meaning judgment handled (for 3.3.3) by the inert error-suggestion rubric and (for identification) by the inert error-identification rubric. The form-error-probe is the SC 3.3.1 authoritative barrier-only runner; for 3.3.3 only a cross-signal that some error surface appeared. Capability caveat: SCR18's primary example uses native window.alert(), whose text is NOT DOM-observable; the rubric only sees the captured state-after DOM crop (vision-capture.js), so its capability holds only for the in-DOM error-text variant, not a true native alert. The 'reposition focus to errored field' nicety is assessed by no 3.3.3 lane.
techniques.gap: Adequacy of the alert's descriptive/suggestion content is judged only by inert, non-authoritative rubrics, and only for in-DOM error text; a true native window.alert() produces no DOM evidence for the rubric. The authoritative lane only detects presence/absence of an error surface (and a JS alert may not even register as a DOM error surface).
techniques.recommendation: Enable opts.runLlm so the error-suggestion (and error-identification) rubrics judge the in-DOM alert text; note window.alert() text is not DOM-observable, so either capture native alert content via a dialog handler or scope the rubric/probe to in-DOM error surfaces.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:form-error-probe (authoritative for SC 3.3.1 ONLY; for 3.3.3 a live cross-signal/barrier-gate, never authoritative; barrier-only)
status-detector:4.1.3 (shadow,opt-in,insertion-only; SC 4.1.3, does not judge suggestion content)
techniques.rationale: SCR32 inserts error text into the DOM as a list of anchor links above the fields, moving focus to it, with each anchor jumping to the offending field. The DOM-inserted error text IS runtime-observable (so the rubric has real evidence, unlike native-alert SCR18): the SC 3.3.1 form-error-probe sees that an error surface appeared (cross-signal), and the opt-in/insertion-only status-detector (SC 4.1.3) could observe the insertion, but neither judges whether the text suggests a correction. The inert error-suggestion rubric judges the suggestion content. The distinctive jump-to-error LINK mechanism (anchors resolving to each error field, focus moved to the summary) is assessed by no lane (same gap as G139). So the textual-suggestion portion is PARTIAL via inert rubric while the link-wiring portion is uncovered.
techniques.gap: Suggestion-text adequacy is judged only by the inert rubric; and no lane verifies that the inserted error list contains working in-page links to each offending field or that focus moves to the error summary.
techniques.recommendation: Enable opts.runLlm for the error-suggestion rubric; additionally add a deterministic check (post-invalid-submit, via the vision-capture submit transition) that inserted error-summary anchors' href fragments resolve to invalid fields and that focus moved into the error region.

Lane-label overclaim corrected: form-error-probe was tagged '(authoritative,live)' inside a 3.3.3 verdict, but catalog.js shows it is sc:'3.3.1', barrier-only, never-clearing. The dossier states 3.3.3 has NO authoritative lane, so the probe is authoritative for 3.3.1 only and merely a cross-signal/barrier-gate for 3.3.3. Verdict unchanged. Same lane-label overclaim corrected: form-error-probe relabeled as authoritative-for-3.3.1-only / 3.3.3 cross-signal.

Verdict unchanged. Same lane-label overclaim corrected: form-error-probe relabeled as authoritative-for-3.3.1-only / 3.3.3 cross-signal; status-detector lane clarified as SC 4.1.3 / insertion-only / does-not-judge-suggestion. Recommendation tied to the existing vision-capture submit transition.

scs.title: Name, Role, Value
scs.summary: 4.1.2's authoritative lane is catalog ax-state-diff (AX name/role/state-on-activation, closed ARIA state set, fires only on widget-role/native-control elements) plus field-label-probe (form-input name absence) and the surfaced axe link-name (via 2.4.4); it authoritatively captures the MISSING-ACCESSIBLE-NAME failures (F68/F86/F89), but is blind to (a) ROLE-absence on roleless scripted controls (F59 AND F42 — both excluded by the WIDGET_ROLE applicability gate, only incidentally flagged by vsr if also nameless), (b) NAME ADEQUACY for ARIA14/ARIA16 (no 4.1.2 rubric), and (c) focus-state notification (F79) / stale-text-alternative-on-update (F20), which no lane assesses.

techniques.rationale: ARIA14 Test #1 requires the aria-label value to PROPERLY DESCRIBE the element's purpose. ax-state-diff authoritatively reads the resolved AX name (axNamePresent), so name PRESENCE via aria-label is verified, and vsr-analysis flags an interactive element announced with no name. But the technique's actual test is name ADEQUACY ('properly describes the purpose'), a meaning judgment no authoritative lane makes; vsr-analysis only emits a review-flagged name-text-mismatch (word-overlap heuristic) and the rubric set has NO 4.1.2 name-adequacy rubric (confirmed: the closest are 2.4.4 link-purpose and 2.5.3 label-in-name).
techniques.gap: No lane judges whether the aria-label value adequately describes the control's purpose; only name presence is authoritatively verified.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 4.1.2 LLM rubric for accessible-name adequacy (does the computed accName describe the control's purpose), analogous to the 1.1.1 alt-text and 2.4.4 link-purpose rubrics.

techniques.rationale: ARIA16 Test #1 (aria-labelledby idrefs resolve to real elements) is effectively captured: a broken/dangling idref yields an empty computed accName, which ax-state-diff (axNamePresent) and vsr-analysis (no-accessible-name) detect. But Test #2 (the referenced text ACCURATELY labels the control) is a name-adequacy judgment no authoritative lane makes and no 4.1.2 rubric covers (the rubric set has none for 4.1.2).
techniques.gap: The idref-resolution half is captured via accName computation, but 'referenced text accurately labels the control' (adequacy) is not assessed.
techniques.recommendation: Same 4.1.2 name-adequacy LLM rubric would cover the accuracy half; idref resolution is already authoritatively handled.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff (authoritative,live) — applicability-gated to widget-role/native-control elements via the oracle WIDGET_ROLE family
techniques.rationale: F15 fails custom controls that don't expose role/name/value/state/properties via the AX API, 'or do so incompletely'. ax-state-diff directly probes the AX tree on activation for axRolePresentAndExpected, axNamePresent, axStatePropertyExposed, axStateChanged (closed state inventory) and emits nrvDefectStable BARRIER, capturing the common incomplete-exposure case for controls that DO carry a widget role. But the oracle only emits the name-role-value (4.1.2) obligation when WIDGET_ROLE matches a resolved role, so a fully role-less custom control (the most extreme F15 case) never enters the runner; and 'value'/arbitrary-property completeness is broader than the closed ARIA state set the runner inventories.
techniques.gap: Controls exposing NO widget role bypass the oracle's 4.1.2 applicability gate (no candidate is generated, so ax-state-diff never runs); completeness of value/user-settable properties beyond the closed ARIA state set is not exhaustively checked.
techniques.recommendation: Add an interactivity-without-widget-role detector (event-handler / cursor:pointer heuristic on a generic-role AX node) and relax the oracle WIDGET_ROLE gate so ax-state-diff can be applied to roleless custom controls.

techniques.rationale: F20 fails when non-text content is UPDATED (e.g. chart/image src changes) but its text alternative is NOT updated, leaving stale alt/name semantics. Detecting this requires a temporal comparison of the (new) rendered content's meaning against the unchanged text alternative — a semantic-equivalence-over-time judgment. No lane does this: ax-state-diff diffs AX state on activation but not alt-text-vs-image-content staleness; status-detector is DOM-insertion-only; the un-surfaced axe image-alt rule only checks alt presence; and no 4.1.2/1.1.1 rubric tracks updates over time.
techniques.gap: No lane compares a text alternative against dynamically-updated non-text content to detect staleness.
techniques.recommendation: New capability: capture before/after states across a content update and run an LLM/vision check that the text alternative still matches the current non-text content (extend the 1.1.1 alt-text rubric with a dynamic-update mode).

lanes: shadow:vsr-analysis no-accessible-name sc=4.1.2 (shadow,opt-in) — only fires if the emulated link is ALSO nameless, which is incidental to the role defect
techniques.rationale: DOWNGRADED from PARTIAL. F42's 4.1.2 facet (Check #1) fails a scripted span/img/div emulating a link whose programmatic role is NOT 'link' — i.e. a MISSING/incorrect role on a roleless interactive element. This is identical in kind to F59 (which the analyst correctly marked NOT_CAPTURED): the oracle generates the name-role-value (4.1.2) obligation only when WIDGET_ROLE matches a resolved role, so a roleless emulated link gets no candidate and ax-state-diff NEVER runs on it, and the runner cannot infer the element was INTENDED to be a link. vsr-analysis would flag it only if it is ALSO nameless (no-accessible-name), which is incidental — it never asserts the role defect. The 'axe link-in-text-block' the analyst listed is a 1.4.1 rule, irrelevant to role-missing. No lane asserts 'this interactive element should be role=link but isn't', so the 4.1.2 facet has no asserting lane — the same situation that earned F59 NOT_CAPTURED. (The keyboard half, Check #2, is 2.1.1/2.1.3, a different SC.)
techniques.gap: No lane detects that a scripted interactive element has the wrong/absent role (should be link); intent ('emulates a link') is not inferred and roleless elements never enter the authoritative 4.1.2 runner.
techniques.recommendation: Add a detector flagging elements with click/keypress navigation handlers whose AX role is generic/none (candidate emulated-link/role-missing barrier), feeding a 4.1.2/1.3.1 shadow signal — the same detector that would also cover F59.

lanes: shadow:vsr-analysis no-accessible-name sc=4.1.2 (shadow,opt-in) — only if also nameless
techniques.rationale: F59 fails a div/span turned into a UI control by script without a role (native or ARIA). The defining condition is: element has event handlers (is interactive) AND has no native and no ARIA role. The oracle generates the name-role-value (4.1.2) obligation only when WIDGET_ROLE.test(factRole) is true, and factRole on a roleless div/span resolves to '' (or 'generic' via axRole), so no 4.1.2 candidate is generated and ax-state-diff NEVER fires on exactly the elements F59 targets. The un-surfaced axe rules include no 'scripted-control-without-role' check. vsr-analysis treats a roleless element as a widget only when s.interactive is set, and even then flags only NAME absence, not the absence of ROLE itself. So the core role-missing defect has no asserting lane.
techniques.gap: No lane detects 'element has interaction handlers but no programmatic role'; the 4.1.2 obligation is never generated for roleless elements (oracle WIDGET_ROLE gate), so the authoritative runner is never reached.
techniques.recommendation: Add an event-handler / interactivity probe that flags generic-role (div/span) AX nodes carrying click/key handlers as a missing-role barrier, and relax the oracle WIDGET_ROLE gate / ax-state-diff applicability to admit them.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe fieldLabelBarrier sc=3.3.2 (authoritative,live) — covers ALL input/textarea/select
deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff axNamePresent (authoritative,live) — corroborates only the WIDGET_ROLE subset (checkbox/radio/native controls), NOT plain textbox inputs
axe:label / select-name (capable,NOT-surfaced — both carry only wcag412)
techniques.rationale: F68 fails an input/textarea/select with no programmatically determined name. This is exactly what the authoritative catalog field-label-probe detects for EVERY isUserInputField (input/textarea/select): it requires programmaticNamePresent and emits fieldLabelBarrier when no accessible name is computed from label/for, wrapping label, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or image alt. The probe disposition lives at sc=3.3.2 but detects the identical missing-name physical defect F68 describes. (ax-state-diff corroborates only for native controls / WIDGET_ROLE elements — a plain text input has role=textbox, which the oracle WIDGET_ROLE gate excludes, so ax-state-diff does NOT fire on it; field-label-probe alone authoritatively covers those.)

F79 fails when a component's FOCUS STATE is not programmatically determinable, or there is no AT notification when focus moves between controls. This requires reading the AX focus state and capturing focus-change events emitted to the accessibility API. The catalog focus runner is 2.4.7 focus-visual-retry, which tests a VISIBLE indicator (pixels), not AX focus-state exposure. ax-state-diff diffs name/role/state on ACTIVATION (Enter), not focus-state exposure or focus-move notifications. No lane reads AX focus state or focus-change events, and no rubric covers it.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses programmatic exposure of focus state or AT notification on focus change for custom-scripted components.
techniques.recommendation: New instrument: drive Tab focus across custom widgets and read the AX-tree focused node + listen for accessibility focus-change events via CDP to confirm focus state is exposed and updated on focus move.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe fieldLabelBarrier sc=3.3.2 (authoritative,live) — fires per sub-input
deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff axNamePresent (authoritative,live) — corroborates native sub-controls only
techniques.rationale: F86 fails when one or more sub-fields of a multi-part field (e.g. a 3-part US phone number) lack a programmatically determined name. Each sub-field is a separate INPUT, so each gets its own field-label-probe candidate (every isUserInputField is enumerated); an unnamed sub-input yields a fieldLabelBarrier. The per-subfield missing-name failure is authoritatively detected by field-label-probe; vsr-analysis corroborates on each unnamed sub-control.

lanes: axe:link-name DECIDED+SURFACED (the axe link-name violation carries wcag244, which is in the surface allow-list AXE_SURFACED_SCS={1.3.1,1.3.5,1.4.4,2.4.4}; it surfaces under sc=2.4.4) (shadow,live)

deterministic-catalog:ax-state-diff axNamePresent (authoritative,live) — an <a> matches the native-control gate and link is in WIDGET_ROLE, so nameRoleDefect→nrvDefectStable BARRIER fires on the empty-name link
techniques.rationale: F89 fails an image-only link with no accessible name (img alt='' / role=presentation and no aria-label/labelledby ⇒ empty link accName). Verified: axe link-name carries WCAG tag wcag244, and 2.4.4 is in the surface allow-list, so a link-name violation IS surfaced (under sc=2.4.4) as a DECIDED shadow-live cross-signal for the same empty-name defect. Independently, ax-state-diff picks it up authoritatively: <a> satisfies both the oracle WIDGET_ROLE (link) gate and the runner's native-control gate, so an empty axName yields nameRoleDefect → nrvDefectStable BARRIER. vsr-analysis no-accessible-name corroborates.

lanes: deterministic-catalog:field-label-probe / ax-state-diff axNamePresent (authoritative,live) — name-absence half (mode a)

shadow:LLM rubric label-in-name-v0 sc=2.5.3 (shadow,INERT by default) — judges accName-CONTAINS-visible-label, the proper substring-containment test for mode (b), but bound to 2.5.3 and not surfaced as a 4.1.2 signal
shadow:vsr-analysis name-text-mismatch sc=4.1.2 review:true (shadow,opt-in,uncalibrated word-overlap) — containment half, heuristic only
techniques.rationale: F111 has two failure modes: (a) a control with a visible label has NO accessible name, and (b) the accName does NOT contain the visible label text (the 2.5.3 label-in-name aspect). Mode (a) is authoritatively captured (field-label-probe / ax-state-diff axNamePresent / vsr no-accessible-name). For mode (b) the analyst claimed only an uncalibrated word-overlap review flag exists, but a dedicated 2.5.3 label-in-name LLM rubric (label-in-name-v0.md) DOES perform exactly the visible-label ⊆ accName substring/word containment test F111/2.5.3 require — however that rubric is INERT (LLM lane off by default) and bound to the cross-SC 2.5.3 ○-tier obligation, never surfaced as a 4.1.2 disposition. So mode (b) is only touched by a non-authoritative, default-off lane plus the uncalibrated vsr review flag.
techniques.gap: The label-in-name containment check exists as the 2.5.3 label-in-name rubric but is INERT and bound to 2.5.3, not surfaced/authoritative for 4.1.2; the only live touch on mode (b) is vsr-analysis's uncalibrated word-overlap review flag.
techniques.recommendation: Activate/surface the existing 2.5.3 label-in-name rubric (or add a deterministic visible-label ⊆ accName containment check, or calibrate vsr-analysis name-text-mismatch) into a live 4.1.2/2.5.3 label-in-name signal — the containment judge already exists, it is just inert and unsurfaced.

techniques.rationale: G10 is satisfied when a component built with an AX-API-capable technology exposes name+role, allows user-settable properties to be set, and notifies of changes. For rendered web widgets, ax-state-diff verifies axRolePresentAndExpected, axNamePresent and a change notification (axStateChanged) on activation — directly assessing the name/role-exposed + change-notification facets. PARTIAL because full satisfaction (user-settable properties can be set, full value semantics, works with AT) is broader than the closed name/role/state-on-activation check, the canonical G10 example is a Java applet (outside the web-page-at-runtime medium but the AX principle maps to web), and the runner only fires on oracle-WIDGET_ROLE elements.
techniques.gap: Setting of user-settable properties / full value semantics and 'works with AT' beyond name/role/state-on-activation are not verified; runner only fires for widget-role-bearing elements.
techniques.recommendation: None for the web-relevant name/role/change-notification facet (ax-state-diff covers it); a fuller value/property-setting verification would require extending ax-state-diff's typed outcomes.

techniques.rationale: G108 uses standard MARKUP features (HTML) to expose name/role, set properties, and notify changes (tests: name+role determinable; input components operable from AT). This is the most directly web-relevant of the three general techniques: ax-state-diff authoritatively reads name/role/state-change from the markup-derived AX tree, field-label-probe verifies form-control names, and the 2.1.1 keyboard-activation runner verifies operability. PARTIAL because verifying a SUFFICIENT technique holds for EVERY UI component (full property-setting + value semantics) exceeds the runner's closed check, and applicability is gated on a widget role (roleless components are not swept).
techniques.gap: User-settable property setting / full value semantics not verified; verification is per-widget-role-bearing element, not an exhaustive component sweep.
techniques.recommendation: None — the name/role exposure + change-notification + operability facets are authoritatively covered for HTML markup; property-setting depth is the only residual.

techniques.rationale: G135 uses a technology's AX-API features to expose names/roles, set user-settable properties, and notify of changes; its canonical example is a Java applet using Swing components (a non-web medium). For rendered web/ARIA the principle maps onto ax-state-diff, which authoritatively reads AX name/role and a change notification on activation. PARTIAL because the technique's full scope (value/property setting, applet/Swing framing) is broader than the closed name/role/state-on-activation web check, and the runner only fires on widget-role-bearing elements.
techniques.gap: User-settable property setting and full value semantics not verified; the Java-applet framing is partly outside the web-page-at-runtime medium, though the AX name/role/value/notification principle is exactly ax-state-diff's territory for web.
techniques.recommendation: None — name/role/change-notification exposure for web components is authoritatively covered; deeper property/value verification would extend ax-state-diff.

audit_changes.why: Overclaim. F42's 4.1.2 facet is a MISSING-ROLE defect on a roleless scripted element emulating a link — identical in kind to F59, which the analyst correctly marked NOT_CAPTURED. The oracle only emits the name-role-value (4.1.2) obligation when WIDGET_ROLE matches a resolved role (applicability-oracle.js:107), so a roleless emulated link gets no candidate and ax-state-diff never runs on it; vsr-analysis flags it only if it is ALSO nameless (incidental, not the role defect); and the listed axe:link-in-text-block is a 1.4.1 rule irrelevant to role. No lane asserts the role defect, so the PARTIAL was inconsistent with F59 and overstated coverage.

Verdict unchanged, but lanes/rationale/recommendation corrected: the analyst claimed mode (b) containment was untouched except by an uncalibrated word-overlap flag, but a dedicated 2.5.3 label-in-name LLM rubric (label-in-name-v0.md) does the exact visible-label ⊆ accName containment test — it is just INERT (LLM lane off by default) and bound to 2.5.3, not surfaced for 4.1.2. The recommendation changed from 'add a containment check' to 'activate/surface the existing inert 2.5.3 label-in-name rubric'.

Verdict unchanged (field-label-probe authoritatively covers all input/textarea/select), but corrected a lane overclaim: the analyst listed ax-state-diff axNamePresent as authoritative for F68 generally, yet plain text inputs have role=textbox, which the oracle WIDGET_ROLE gate excludes, so ax-state-diff does NOT fire on them — it only corroborates the checkbox/radio/native-control subset. Lane/rationale clarified.
Verdict unchanged, same ax-state-diff lane-accuracy correction as F68 (ax-state-diff corroborates only native sub-controls; field-label-probe is the authoritative per-subfield lane).

scs.title: Status Messages
scs.summary: 4.1.3 has NO authoritative lane (the registry only carries a never-clearable 4.1.3/INAPPLICABLE entry); the sole runtime signal is the opt-in, shadow, insertion-only status-detector.js, which detects the canonical F103 unannounced-status failure (PARTIAL at best) and inversely recognizes injection into a pre-existing live region (role=status/alert/log/aria-live/alertdialog/output) as a non-barrier; there is NO LLM rubric and NO consumed axe rule for 4.1.3 (axe has no status-message rule and 4.1.3 is outside the surface allow-list), and ariaNotify + the opt-out-toggle + the multimedia-avatar help technique are entirely uncovered — best coverage across the SC is SHADOW_OR_INERT.

techniques.rationale: ARIA18 verifies a modal role=alertdialog used to identify an input error: accessible name (aria-label/labelledby), at least one focusable element, focus MOVED to it on open, tab order constrained, focus restored on dismiss, and contents that identify the error (Tests #2,#3,#5,#6). No lane assesses this 4.1.3-relevant composite. status-detector.js's LIVE allow-list includes role=alertdialog and it explicitly treats focus-MOVED-into-new-content as NOT a barrier (focusMovedToMsg returns null finding, status-detector.js:116-117) — exactly the alertdialog pattern — so it only SUPPRESSES a false positive, never affirms ARIA18 is implemented. The focus trap/restore sub-aspects are nearer the authoritative 2.1.2 keyboard-trap-escape / 2.4.3 order runners, but nothing checks the alertdialog naming + error-identification combination as a 4.1.3 technique. No axe rule (axe has no status-message rule), no LLM rubric (none exists for 4.1.3), dynamic-announcement skill is guidance-only.
techniques.gap: No lane positively verifies an alertdialog correctly identifies an error with an accessible name + focus moved in + error text. The status-detector only suppresses (treats focus-move as non-barrier) rather than confirming the technique.
techniques.recommendation: Add an LLM rubric (or extend dynamic-announcement into a detector) that, for an error-triggered modal, checks role=alertdialog + accessible name + focus moved in + error text present, and cross-reference the 2.1.2/2.4.3 focus runners for the trap/restore aspects. Lower priority since advisory.

techniques.rationale: ARIA19's sufficient test: an EMPTY role=alert / aria-live=assertive container exists in the DOM at page load and error text is later INJECTED into it. status-detector.js inversely covers this — its LIVE allow-list includes role=alert and aria-live=assertive, and inLiveRegion(addedNode) returns null finding (status-detector.js:114), so a click-driven error injected into a pre-existing alert/aria-live region is correctly NOT flagged (it recognizes the success pattern's absence-of-failure). But it is a barrier detector, never a positive verifier: it never asserts 'ARIA19 satisfied' as a clear, it is opt-in shadow, and it snapshots DOM at trigger time (not load) so it cannot confirm the container PRE-EXISTED page load. Crucially the canonical ARIA19 example is SUBMIT-driven with a 500ms setTimeout injection — the detector EXCLUDES submit triggers (status-detector.js:53-54) and settles only 300ms, so for that exact pattern it observes nothing; the inverse recognition only applies to a click-driven variant. The 'region present BEFORE the message' timing and real-AT announcement are not deterministically checked.
techniques.gap: No authoritative lane verifies the sufficient technique is satisfied; status-detector only suppresses a barrier for the click-driven case, misses the technique's own submit-driven 500ms-delayed example, and cannot confirm the live region pre-existed page load.
techniques.recommendation: Promote a deterministic 4.1.3 verifier (or surface status-detector's live-region recognition as a positive PROVISIONAL fill), extend the detector to drive submit and longer settle windows in an isolated/restored page, and wire the VSR /sr-act transcript so injected-error announcement can be confirmed against AT-equivalent voicing.

techniques.rationale: ARIA22's sufficient test: a container has role=status BEFORE the status message occurs, the message lands inside it, and equivalent-visual content (e.g. cart image with alt text) also resides in it (Tests #1,#2,#3). status-detector.js's LIVE allow-list includes role=status, and ARIA22's examples are CLICK-driven (Search button, Add to Cart button), so a message inserted into a role=status container on click is correctly NOT flagged (inLiveRegion → null, status-detector.js:114) — genuine inverse coverage of the success pattern. But it snapshots DOM at trigger time so it cannot confirm role=status pre-existed (Test #1), and it cannot judge Test #3 (visually-equivalent context like alt text inside the container) — a meaning judgment with no rubric. It is shadow/opt-in and only a barrier detector, never a positive clear. No axe rule, no LLM rubric.
techniques.gap: No positive verification that role=status was pre-applied or that visually-equivalent context (alt text etc.) is inside the container; status-detector only avoids false-flagging the success case. The aria-atomic semantics the technique stresses are not assessed.
techniques.recommendation: Add a 4.1.3 LLM rubric (status-message-announced) that judges whether the announced container also carries the equivalent visual context, and/or a deterministic check that role=status/aria-live existed pre-change; consider a PROVISIONAL positive fill from status-detector's live-region recognition.

techniques.rationale: ARIA23's sole sufficient test is purely static markup: the container of sequentially-updating information has role=log (Test #1). status-detector.js includes role=log in its LIVE allow-list, so a log entry appended (e.g. on a click-driven chat 'send') into a role=log region is correctly NOT flagged (inLiveRegion → null, status-detector.js:114) — inverse/partial coverage. But the technique's actual test is a static presence check that NO lane performs as a positive clear — there is no deterministic role-inventory asserting role=log present, and axe has no role=log rule (4.1.3 carries no axe rule and is outside the surface allow-list). The skill routes log/sequential updates under 4.1.3 guidance only. So coverage is shadow non-barrier recognition, not authoritative verification.
techniques.gap: No lane positively verifies role=log presence on a sequentially-updating region (the technique's only test). status-detector merely avoids flagging it; being an opt-in shadow instrument it offers no clear.
techniques.recommendation: Add a deterministic static check / rubric that identifies sequentially-updating regions and verifies role=log (or live-region) markup; surface as PROVISIONAL since 4.1.3 has no authoritative lane.

techniques.rationale: ARIA25 conveys progress-bar status via a SEPARATE pre-rendered aria-live=polite text container whose text is UPDATED via characterData as the bar progresses (the progressbar role itself is explicitly NOT a live region). status-detector.js does observe characterData mutations (status-detector.js:88) and includes aria-live in its LIVE allow-list, so a text update landing in the aria-live region is correctly NOT flagged (inLiveRegion → null) — the same inverse recognition as ARIA19/22/23. But the ARIA25 update is async/timer/upload-driven, started by a click but emitting per-percent updates over seconds, so it generally falls OUTSIDE the 300ms settle window and the detector observes nothing; and even when seen it only non-flags, never positively verifies the progressbar↔aria-live wiring or that aria-valuenow is mirrored into the live text. Shadow/opt-in only; no rubric, no axe.
techniques.gap: Progress updates are typically time/async-driven and span beyond the 300ms settle, so the per-percent characterData updates to the aria-live node usually are not observed; and no lane verifies the progress live-region is correctly wired to the progressbar.
techniques.recommendation: Extend status-detector to drive non-click async progress with a longer/derived settle window (capturing timer-driven characterData updates into the existing aria-live region), and/or add a rubric that verifies a progressbar has an associated live-region status text. Wire VSR transcript for announcement confirmation.

techniques.rationale: ARIA27 conveys progress via the experimental document.ariaNotify() JS method — an imperative announcement API that fires NO DOM mutation and creates NO live region. status-detector.js is purely DOM-mutation based (MutationObserver on childList/characterData, status-detector.js:85-91) and cannot observe an ariaNotify() call; there is no live-region node to inspect. No axe rule, no LLM rubric, and the dynamic-announcement skill's transcript path is unwired. Even the VSR/transcript approach would need an engine modelling the experimental ariaNotify API. Nothing in the harness assesses this.
techniques.gap: No lane can detect an imperative ariaNotify() announcement — it leaves no DOM/live-region footprint that any current instrument inspects.
techniques.recommendation: Instrument ariaNotify by hooking/spying on document.ariaNotify in the collector (record calls + payloads) so an API announcement becomes observable; until then treat as a known blind spot. Low urgency given experimental status.

techniques.rationale: F103 is THE canonical 4.1.3 failure: dynamic content meets the status-message definition (does not take focus; conveys result/wait/progress/error) yet sits in a container with NO role=status/alert/log and NO aria-live, so AT never announces it. status-detector.js directly targets this — it drives a safe AT-perceivable control, confirms NEW text appeared (not pre-existing/relocated), confirms it is NOT in a live region, confirms focus did NOT move, then emits kind:'status-not-announced' (status-detector.js:113-124). A genuine detection of the failure. BUT only PARTIAL: (1) opt-in (runInstruments / V3_INSTRUMENTS=1) and NON-AUTHORITATIVE shadow — it can never set a BARRIER (registry has only 4.1.3/INAPPLICABLE, never-clearable); (2) INSERTION-ONLY — a status revealed by toggling hidden/display/aria-hidden on a pre-rendered node (addedCount=0) is invisible (coverageMode:'insertion-only', audit B3); (3) click-triggered only — it EXCLUDES submit/reset/href/scripted-nav triggers (status-detector.js:52-57) and settles 300ms, so F103's OWN submit-driven search-results example, plus async/timer status, are missed; (4) it cannot truly confirm Test #4 ('not surfaced by AT') — it infers non-announcement structurally, not via real AT.
techniques.gap: Detection is shadow/opt-in (never authoritative), insertion-only (misses hidden/display/aria-hidden toggles of pre-rendered status), and click-only (misses submit/async/timer-driven status — including F103's own submit-driven search-results example, deliberately skipped to avoid navigation). Structural inference, not real-AT confirmation.
techniques.recommendation: Promote 4.1.3 to a PROVISIONAL (or authoritative) disposition fed by status-detector; extend coverage to (a) hidden/display/aria-hidden toggle reveals and (b) submit/async/timer-driven status (drive in an isolated/restored page so submit can be observed), and wire the VSR /sr-act transcript to confirm non-announcement against AT-equivalent voicing.

techniques.rationale: G193 'Providing help by an assistant in the web page' provides a multimedia avatar that helps users (esp. with cognitive disabilities) understand the page; its tests are (1) an assistant exists in the web page and (2) it provides understanding help. The avatar is a rendered-page DOM artifact (an embedded multimedia/video widget), so the technique is IN domain for a rendered-web-page harness — it is NOT a PDF/Flash/SMIL/server-side/pure-authoring technique and the 'must also satisfy Guideline 1.2' note does not move it out of runtime scope. However, no lane assesses 'is there a help-assistant avatar and does it aid page understanding' — it is a content/editorial judgment with no DOM/AX status-change signal, no instrument, no LLM rubric, and no consumed axe rule, and it is at best tangential to the 4.1.3 status-message pattern. So it is uncovered, not out of domain.
techniques.gap: No lane detects the presence of a multimedia help-assistant avatar or judges whether it provides understanding help; this is a content judgment with no detector, rubric, or axe rule.
techniques.recommendation: If pursued, add a low-priority LLM/content rubric that detects an embedded help-assistant/avatar widget and judges whether it aids page understanding; very low priority, as this is a marginal 4.1.3 mapping and an advisory-style help mechanism.

techniques.rationale: SCR14 makes NONESSENTIAL alerts optional: a live (aria-live=assertive, aria-atomic) stock component auto-announces timer-driven updates (every 10s), plus two aria-pressed toggle buttons let the user turn announcements ON/OFF (flipping aria-live between assertive and off). Its tests are (1) no non-emergency alerts displayed by default and (2) a mechanism exists to activate/deactivate the interruptions. status-detector.js would, at most, see the timer-driven stock updates — but those fire on a 10s interval (not click-driven) and fall outside the 300ms settle, and when seen they are inside an aria-live region so treated as non-barrier; clicking the toggle buttons flips aria-live but emits no new status text, so no finding. The detector cannot evaluate the OPT-OUT toggle mechanism (the actual subject of SCR14) nor judge essential-vs-nonessential; the aria-pressed toggle state is a 4.1.2 concern, not assessed here for SCR14's purpose. No rubric, no axe.
techniques.gap: No lane assesses the presence/operability of a user control to toggle nonessential live announcements on/off, nor the timer-driven (non-click) live updates the technique relies on.
techniques.recommendation: Add a rubric/instrument check for a user-facing announcement-toggle affordance bound to a live region's aria-live (and capture timer-driven aria-live updates). Low priority since advisory.

audit_changes.why: OUT_OF_DOMAIN overclaim. G193 is technology=general, applicability 'all technologies', and its subject is a multimedia help-assistant AVATAR embedded in the web page — a rendered-page DOM artifact, NOT a PDF/Flash/Silverlight/SMIL/server-side/pure-authoring technique. The 'must also satisfy Guideline 1.2' note does not move the technique itself out of runtime domain. Per the audit rule (a general/HTML/ARIA/CSS/client-side-script technique about a rendered page is IN domain), it is in domain but genuinely uncovered: no instrument, no rubric, no consumed axe rule assesses help-avatar presence/understanding-help, and it is only tangential to 4.1.3. Correct verdict is NOT_CAPTURED with a gap and a (low-priority) recommendation, not OUT_OF_DOMAIN with an empty gap.
